topThingsToDo.title: Louvre (smart route, not a marathon)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed ticket and enter via Carrousel du Louvre to skip the pyramid lines; pick 10–15 works (e.g., Denon wing highlights) and leave before fatigue hits.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset picnic on Canal Saint-Martin
topThingsToDo.description: Grab wine/cheese from a nearby fromagerie and sit by the locks around République/Jacques Bonsergent; it’s lively but less touristy than the Seine.

topThingsToDo.title: Montmartre beyond Sacré-Cœur
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (before 9:00) and wander Rue de l’Abreuvoir and the quiet backstreets; skip the crowded stairways and take the funicular with a Metro ticket.

topThingsToDo.title: Marais food crawl + hidden courtyards
topThingsToDo.description: Combine falafel on Rue des Rosiers with quick stops at Place des Vosges and Hôtel de Sully’s courtyard; ideal for a half-day without crossing town.

topThingsToDo.title: Night river view without a pricey cruise
topThingsToDo.description: Walk Pont Alexandre III to Pont de la Concorde after dark for Eiffel sparkle views; for a cheap cruise, use Batobus as hop-on/hop-off on the Seine.

scamsToAvoid.title: Friendship bracelet & petition teams
scamsToAvoid.description: Near Sacré-Cœur and Eiffel, don’t stop or accept anything “free”; keep walking and firmly say “Non, merci” with hands to yourself.

scamsToAvoid.title: Ring drop or gold jewelry ‘found’
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone offers a “lost” ring or asks you to hold it, refuse and move on; it’s designed to pressure you into paying.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxis and overcharging rides
scamsToAvoid.description: At airports/stations, only use the official taxi line or a reputable app; confirm the meter is on or use fixed airport taxi fares.

localTips.title: Book museums for the first slot
localTips.description: The first timed entry is consistently calmer at the Louvre/Orsay; you’ll see more in 90 minutes than a packed afternoon.

localTips.title: Eat like Parisians: lunch formulas
localTips.description: Look for “formule midi” on weekdays (main + starter/dessert); quality is high and prices are far better than dinner.

localTips.title: Free water and better coffee
localTips.description: Ask for “une carafe d’eau” (it’s free at restaurants); order “un espresso” and avoid “café crème” unless you want a milky drink.

localTips.title: Avoid the worst Metro crowds
localTips.description: If you can, skip 8:00–9:30 and 17:30–19:00 on major lines (1, 4, 13); walking 20–30 minutes often beats transfers.

foodToTry.title: Jambon-beurre on a proper baguette
foodToTry.description: Buy from a good boulangerie and eat it fresh (within an hour); the bread quality is the whole point.

foodToTry.title: Crêpe complète (ham, egg, cheese)
foodToTry.description: Order it savory (galette) for a real meal; best in small crêperies, not tourist stands near landmarks.

foodToTry.title: Steak-frites with sauce béarnaise/poivre
foodToTry.description: Pick a classic brasserie and ask for cuisson (rare/medium); it’s a reliable “Paris meal” when you don’t want to gamble.

foodToTry.title: Pastries: flan and Paris-Brest
foodToTry.description: Skip the cliché macarons and try flan pâtissier or Paris-Brest from a pâtisserie; they travel well for a park snack.

gettingAround.title: Use Metro/RER with a digital pass
gettingAround.description: Load tickets/passes on a Navigo Easy card or phone when available; keep it away from magnets and validate at every gate.

gettingAround.title: Walk for short hops, Metro for cross-town
gettingAround.description: Many central sights are 15–25 minutes apart on foot; save Metro for longer jumps and to avoid line changes.

gettingAround.title: Airports: choose the right option
gettingAround.description: CDG: RER B is fastest to the center; ORY: Orlyval + RER B is quick, while official taxis have fixed rates—avoid random drivers.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise stroll at Senso-ji (Asakusa)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive around 6–7am to see the temple and Nakamise-dori without crowds; grab a fresh melonpan nearby once shops open.

topThingsToDo.title: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast + knife shopping
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 9am for tamagoyaki and seafood don; compare prices at 2–3 stalls and ask if tax-free is available on higher-ticket knives.

topThingsToDo.title: Meiji Jingu + Harajuku backstreets
topThingsToDo.description: Enter via the south approach for a quieter forest walk, then skip Takeshita-dori and explore Cat Street and side alleys for better shops and cafes.

topThingsToDo.title: Evening views: Shibuya Sky or Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
topThingsToDo.description: Book Shibuya Sky at sunset days in advance; for a free alternative, go to the Gov’t Building observation deck on a clear night.

topThingsToDo.title: Neighborhood bar-hopping in Kichijoji or Ebisu
topThingsToDo.description: Pick one area and try 2–3 tiny standing bars; bring cash and keep groups small to avoid being turned away.

scamsToAvoid.title: Kabukicho touts and “cheap drink” invites
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone trying to lure you into bars or clubs—overcharging and card skimming happen; choose places with posted prices and no street solicitation.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake monks/charity collectors in tourist areas
scamsToAvoid.description: Be wary of aggressive donation requests near major sights; legitimate temples don’t chase tourists for cash on the street.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxi/ride solicitations near stations
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxi ranks and metered rides only; at airports and big hubs, decline anyone offering “special rates” outside the queue.

localTips.title: Use IC cards like a local (Suica/PASMO)
localTips.description: Add a digital IC card to your phone and tap for trains, buses, convenience stores, and many vending machines—faster than tickets.

localTips.title: Master station navigation
localTips.description: Follow exit numbers (not just station names) and save your destination’s closest exit in Maps; big hubs like Shinjuku can add 15–20 minutes if you pop out wrong.

localTips.title: Quiet etiquette that matters
localTips.description: Keep calls off on trains and stand on the left on escalators (right in Osaka); it reduces friction and gets you better service.

localTips.title: Timing beats crowds
localTips.description: Do popular spots before 9am and eat lunch at 11:00; many top ramen/tonkatsu lines peak 12:00–1:30.

foodToTry.title: Ramen (shoyu or tonkotsu)
foodToTry.description: Use ticket-vending-machine shops for speed; go off-peak and look for “kaedama” if you want extra noodles.

foodToTry.title: Sushi at a counter
foodToTry.description: For great value, choose a mid-range sushi-ya near a station and sit at the counter; order omakase to avoid menu confusion.

foodToTry.title: Tempura (tendon or course)
foodToTry.description: Try tendon for a quick meal or a tempura counter for fresh-fried pieces; avoid soggy takeout when possible.

foodToTry.title: Izakaya classics (yakitori + highball)
foodToTry.description: Order a few skewers at a time and pace yourself; many spots charge a small otoshi cover—normal, not a scam.

gettingAround.title: Trains first, taxis late
gettingAround.description: Tokyo Metro/Toei/JR cover almost everything; use taxis mainly after midnight when trains stop and fares jump.

gettingAround.title: Use Google Maps transit filters
gettingAround.description: Toggle “less walking” for huge stations and check last-train times; screenshots help underground where reception drops.

gettingAround.title: Airport transfers without hassle
gettingAround.description: From Narita, use Narita Express or Keisei Skyliner depending on your area; from Haneda, use Keikyu or Monorail—both accept IC cards.

topThingsToDo.title: Colosseum + Forum/Palatine early entry
topThingsToDo.description: Book the first timed slot and add Forum/Palatine to avoid midday crowds; enter the Forum from Via dei Fori Imperiali side for the quickest access.

topThingsToDo.title: Vatican Museums at opening (or late-night)
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve an opening slot (or official late opening) and go straight to the Sistine Chapel first, then backtrack to quieter galleries.

topThingsToDo.title: Trastevere evening walk + viewpoints
topThingsToDo.description: Skip the busiest lanes by starting at Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere, then climb to Gianicolo Terrace for sunset views over the city.

topThingsToDo.title: Hidden ancient Rome: Baths of Caracalla or Appian Way
topThingsToDo.description: Choose Baths of Caracalla for big ruins with space, or rent bikes near Porta San Sebastiano to ride the cobbled Via Appia Antica past aqueducts.

topThingsToDo.title: Borghese Gallery + Villa Borghese break
topThingsToDo.description: Tickets are timed and limited—book ahead; pair it with a walk to Terrazza del Pincio for a classic panorama without paying for a rooftop bar.

scamsToAvoid.title: Friendship bracelet/rose pushers
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t accept anything “free” near major sights; keep walking and keep hands on your items if they try to touch or tie something on.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxi and “fixed price” rides
scamsToAvoid.description: Use white licensed taxis from stands or apps; at airports insist on the official fixed fare and refuse anyone approaching inside terminals.

scamsToAvoid.title: Ticket line “helpers” and fake tours
scamsToAvoid.description: Only buy from official sites or reputable platforms; anyone offering to “skip the line” on the street is usually upselling overpriced or invalid tickets.

localTips.title: Drink from nasoni fountains
localTips.description: Carry a bottle and refill at the small public fountains; plug the spout with a finger to make water arc from the top hole.

localTips.title: Coffee rules that save money
localTips.description: Espresso is cheapest standing at the bar—ask for “un caffè”; table service in tourist zones can double the price.

localTips.title: Avoid the worst crowds with timing
localTips.description: Do Trevi and Pantheon before 8:30am or after 10pm; many streets become jammed from late morning through early evening.

localTips.title: Churches have dress and schedule quirks
localTips.description: Carry a light scarf for shoulders and avoid visiting during midday closures or services; check opening times before crossing town.

foodToTry.title: Carbonara (Roman style)
foodToTry.description: Look for guanciale, pecorino romano, egg, and black pepper—no cream; order it at a sit-down trattoria rather than near major monuments.

foodToTry.title: Cacio e pepe
foodToTry.description: Best when freshly tossed and creamy from pasta water; if it arrives clumpy and dry, it’s a red flag for a tourist kitchen.

foodToTry.title: Supplì
foodToTry.description: Grab these fried rice balls at a forno/pizzeria al taglio; ask for them hot so the mozzarella “filo” stretches when opened.

foodToTry.title: Carciofi (alla giudia or alla romana)
foodToTry.description: In season, try crispy Jewish-style artichokes in the Ghetto or braised Roman-style in Testaccio; order as an antipasto to share.

gettingAround.title: Walk + use Metro strategically
gettingAround.description: Rome is most efficient on foot for the historic center; use Metro A/B mainly to hop between Vatican/Spagna/Termini/Colosseo, then walk from there.

gettingAround.title: Buses and trams: tap-and-go, but validate
gettingAround.description: Contactless taps work on many routes, but paper tickets must be validated; use real-time apps because schedules are unreliable.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and airport transfers
gettingAround.description: Use official taxi stands or apps to avoid overcharging; for Fiumicino/Ciampino confirm the set fare before entering and pay only at the end.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the South Bank at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Westminster, pass the London Eye, stop at Tate Modern (free), then cross Millennium Bridge to St Paul’s for skyline views without paying for a viewpoint.

topThingsToDo.title: See the City from a “free” height
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed slot at Sky Garden (free) or Horizon 22; reserve 1–2 weeks ahead and bring ID for security.

topThingsToDo.title: Explore museums late and strategically
topThingsToDo.description: Go to the British Museum or V&A after 3pm to dodge school groups; for highlights, pick 5 rooms max and use the museum map to avoid zigzagging.

topThingsToDo.title: Do markets with a plan
topThingsToDo.description: Borough is best weekday mornings for food with shorter queues; for vintage and street food, hit Brick Lane on Sunday but arrive before noon.

topThingsToDo.title: Night out in Soho + West End on a budget
topThingsToDo.description: Check TodayTix or TKTS in Leicester Square for same-day theatre deals, then grab a pre-show pint at a nearby pub to avoid inflated interval prices.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed minicabs and fake Uber pickups
scamsToAvoid.description: Only use black cabs, licensed minicabs pre-booked via app/office, or the official Uber app; never accept a ride from someone approaching you at stations.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Gold ring” / charity clipboard pressure
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore drop-and-ask tricks and aggressive donation asks near tourist hubs; keep walking and don’t hand over cash or your contact details.

scamsToAvoid.title: Contactless “tap” distraction theft
scamsToAvoid.description: In busy Tube areas, keep your phone and wallet zipped and don’t hold your card ready in your hand; pickpockets target gates and escalators.

localTips.title: Use contactless/Oyster the smart way
localTips.description: Tap in/out with the same card/device all day to hit daily caps; don’t mix cards or you’ll pay more.

localTips.title: Stand right, walk left on escalators
localTips.description: It’s enforced by social pressure—blocking the left lane in the Tube gets you grief fast, especially at rush hour.

localTips.title: Pub etiquette that saves time
localTips.description: Order and pay at the bar (no table service in most pubs), and don’t queue—wait your turn at the bar edge and catch the bartender’s eye.

localTips.title: Plan around closures and crowds
localTips.description: Many museums are quieter on Friday late openings; avoid Oxford Street on Saturdays—use Regent Street or Marylebone High Street for shopping instead.

foodToTry.title: Fish and chips (proper chippy style)
foodToTry.description: Order cod or haddock with chips and mushy peas; ask for it “wrapped” to keep it crisp on the walk.

foodToTry.title: Sunday roast with all the trimmings
foodToTry.description: Book ahead for popular pubs; look for Yorkshire pudding, roast potatoes, and gravy—aim for a 1–3pm sitting for best availability.

foodToTry.title: Indian or Pakistani curry on Brick Lane or in Tooting
foodToTry.description: Skip the aggressive touts on Brick Lane—choose a place with clear prices; in Tooting, you’ll often get better value and spice.

foodToTry.title: Afternoon tea (but do it efficiently)
foodToTry.description: For a classic experience without hotel markups, try a good bakery or department store tea room; reserve a weekday slot to avoid long waits.

gettingAround.title: Tube + Elizabeth line for cross-city speed
gettingAround.description: Use the Elizabeth line to cut travel time east–west (Paddington–Liverpool Street is minutes); it’s often faster than swapping multiple Tube lines.

gettingAround.title: Buses for sightseeing and cheaper hops
gettingAround.description: Buses are flat fare and great for views; use Citymapper to pick routes like 11 or 24 for landmark-heavy rides.

gettingAround.title: Walk and use river crossings smartly
gettingAround.description: Central London is walkable—cross via Millennium, Waterloo, or Tower Bridge to change neighborhoods fast; save time by avoiding the Tube for 1–2 stop journeys.

topThingsToDo.title: Sagrada Família (book timed entry)
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve online 1–3 days ahead and go early to avoid queues; add the tower ticket for views if the weather is clear.

topThingsToDo.title: Modernisme walk: Passeig de Gràcia
topThingsToDo.description: See Casa Batlló and Casa Milà from outside at sunset, then pop into nearby side streets (Eixample) for quieter tapas.

topThingsToDo.title: Park Güell (smart timing)
topThingsToDo.description: Book the Monumental Zone slot; arrive 30–45 minutes early to explore the free outer paths and viewpoints before entry.

topThingsToDo.title: El Born + Picasso area (small streets, big atmosphere)
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Santa Maria del Mar, then wander Carrer de Montcada; go after 19:30 when day-trippers fade.

topThingsToDo.title: Beach + bunkers viewpoint combo
topThingsToDo.description: Do Barceloneta in the morning, then head to Bunkers del Carmel for sunset; bring water and skip weekends if you want space.

scamsToAvoid.title: Pickpockets on Las Ramblas/metro escalators
scamsToAvoid.description: Keep phone and wallet out of back pockets, zip bags in front of you, and be extra alert at Liceu/Drassanes stations.

scamsToAvoid.title: Friendship bracelets/clipboard petitions
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t stop for “free” gifts or petitions near cathedrals and tourist squares; a distraction often precedes a grab.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxis and overcharging
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official black-and-yellow taxis or apps; confirm the meter is on and avoid unsolicited rides outside clubs.

localTips.title: Eat on Barcelona time
localTips.description: Many kitchens open around 13:00–16:00 and 20:00–23:00; book popular spots and avoid the empty “tourist menu” streets.

localTips.title: Neighborhoods to base yourself
localTips.description: Eixample for transit and walkability, Sant Antoni for food, or Gràcia for local vibe; avoid staying right on Las Ramblas for noise and theft.

localTips.title: Free museum windows (plan ahead)
localTips.description: Some major museums have limited free slots (often evenings or first Sundays); reserve online when required to avoid being turned away.

localTips.title: Beach etiquette and valuables
localTips.description: Don’t leave anything unattended on the sand; bring only what you need and keep items in a small waterproof pouch if swimming.

foodToTry.title: Pa amb tomàquet + anchovies
foodToTry.description: Order tomato-rubbed bread with boquerones or anchovies; it’s a simple staple done best in traditional taverns.

foodToTry.title: Bombes (Barceloneta-style)
foodToTry.description: Try this spicy potato-meat croquette with aioli and brava sauce; ideal as a quick bar snack with a beer.

foodToTry.title: Esqueixada or escalivada
foodToTry.description: Go for these Catalan cold/warm veg dishes when you want something lighter; great pairing with vermut.

foodToTry.title: Crema catalana
foodToTry.description: Ask for it homemade; if it arrives fridge-cold and overly gelatinous, it’s likely industrial.

gettingAround.title: Metro + bus with T-casual
gettingAround.description: A T-casual (10 trips) is usually the best value for short stays; validate once per ride and keep the ticket until you exit.

gettingAround.title: Walk smart between districts
gettingAround.description: Eixample and the center are very walkable, but hills to Park Güell/Bunkers are steep—use metro then a short bus/taxi uphill.

gettingAround.title: Airport transfers
gettingAround.description: Use Aerobús to Plaça Catalunya for simplicity, or metro L9S with a longer transfer; taxis are fixed/regulated but slower in traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Canal cruise at dusk (smaller boat)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a 60–90 min open or small-boat cruise from Jordaan/Prinsengracht for quieter canals and better photos; go near sunset for lit bridge views.

topThingsToDo.title: Rijksmuseum + Museumplein early slot
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve the first time slot and enter via Museumstraat to avoid the longest lines; pair with a quick walk through Vondelpark afterward.

topThingsToDo.title: Anne Frank House (smart timing)
topThingsToDo.description: Tickets sell out weeks ahead—check the official site when new batches drop and choose late-evening entry for fewer crowds outside.

topThingsToDo.title: Jordaan + Nine Streets shopping loop
topThingsToDo.description: Walk Haarlemmerdijk → Westerkerk → De Negen Straatjes for boutiques and vintage; go weekday mornings for calmer streets and better browsing.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip: Zaanse Schans or Haarlem
topThingsToDo.description: For windmills, arrive at Zaanse Schans before 10:00 to beat tour buses; for a local city feel, take a 15–20 min train to Haarlem and stroll the Grote Markt.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxi offers at stations
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore drivers approaching you at Schiphol/Centraal; use the official taxi rank or ride-hail, and confirm the estimated fare before starting.

scamsToAvoid.title: Cash-only ‘broken card machine’ bars
scamsToAvoid.description: If a place suddenly won’t accept cards, leave and pay elsewhere; Amsterdam is largely card-friendly, especially with debit/contactless.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street drug dealers around tourist zones
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid anyone offering cocaine/MDMA near Dam/Red Light District—police stings and adulterated substances are common; coffeeshops don’t sell hard drugs.

localTips.title: Mind the bike lanes
localTips.description: Never stop or walk in the red bike lanes; when crossing, look both ways—bikes are fast, quiet, and have priority.

localTips.title: Reserve restaurants and key museums
localTips.description: Popular dinner spots and museums book out—make reservations 2–7 days ahead, and keep a rainy-day plan ready.

localTips.title: Pick calmer neighborhoods for evenings
localTips.description: For bars without the rowdiness, try De Pijp (around Ferdinand Bolstraat) or Oud-West (De Clercqstraat/Overtoom).

localTips.title: Skip cash, carry a debit/contactless card
localTips.description: Many spots prefer card and some don’t take large notes; a contactless debit card works best for quick payments.

foodToTry.title: Haring (Dutch herring)
foodToTry.description: Try it from a fish stand with pickles and onions; go mid-day for the freshest turnover and ask for it in a broodje if you prefer a sandwich.

foodToTry.title: Stroopwafel (fresh off the press)
foodToTry.description: Buy one made warm at a market stall (Albert Cuypmarkt is a classic) and eat it immediately while the syrup is gooey.

foodToTry.title: Bitterballen with mustard
foodToTry.description: Order with a beer at a brown café; they’re best piping hot—wait a moment before biting to avoid molten filling.

foodToTry.title: Indonesian rijsttafel
foodToTry.description: Book ahead for a multi-dish spread; it’s a uniquely Dutch-Indonesian dining experience and ideal if you want to sample many flavors at once.

gettingAround.title: Use OVpay for trams/metro/buses
gettingAround.description: Tap in/out with contactless card or phone—no need for paper tickets; always tap out to avoid being charged extra.

gettingAround.title: Walk central districts, tram for longer hops
gettingAround.description: The center is compact—walk canals/Jordaan and use trams to jump to Museumplein or De Pijp without navigating bike traffic.

gettingAround.title: Bike only if you’re confident
gettingAround.description: If you rent a bike, practice in a quiet area first and use two locks; otherwise consider e-bikes or public transport to avoid busy intersections.

topThingsToDo.title: Charles Bridge at sunrise (then coffee nearby)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive before 7:00 to beat crowds and tour groups; walk from Malá Strana side for the best light. Grab a quick espresso at a small café on Mostecká afterward.

topThingsToDo.title: Prague Castle via the back route
topThingsToDo.description: Take tram 22 to Pohořelec and walk downhill through Hradčany to avoid the steep climb and busiest entrance. Time it for the hourly Changing of the Guard at noon.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Town Hall Tower + Astronomical Clock (skip the crush)
topThingsToDo.description: Go up the tower 15–30 minutes before the hour for views, then watch the clock show from the side near the tower entrance (not directly in front).

topThingsToDo.title: Vyšehrad for sunset views and quiet
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the ramparts for panoramic river views and far fewer tourists than Letná. Combine with a beer in the nearby Náplavka area if it’s lively.

topThingsToDo.title: Half-day neighborhood escape: Karlín or Holešovice
topThingsToDo.description: Karlín has modern cafés and excellent bakeries; Holešovice offers DOX contemporary art and local breweries. These areas feel more “real Prague” than the center.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street currency exchange “helpers”
scamsToAvoid.description: Never exchange with people offering rates on the street, especially near Old Town Square; use an ATM at a bank or a reputable exchange with clear rate boards.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxis from tourist zones
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid hailing cabs around Old Town and the station; use Bolt/Uber or ask your hotel to book a licensed taxi with a quoted price.

scamsToAvoid.title: ATM and DCC traps
scamsToAvoid.description: At ATMs, choose to be charged in CZK and decline “guaranteed rate” (Dynamic Currency Conversion). Avoid Euronet ATMs, which often have higher fees and bad prompts.

localTips.title: Use PID Lítačka transport tickets correctly
localTips.description: Buy 30/90-minute or 24-hour tickets and validate once when you first enter the system; inspectors do frequent spot checks on trams and metro.

localTips.title: Tram 22 is the scenic shortcut
localTips.description: Ride it for castle views and photogenic stops (Malostranská, Pražský hrad area) without paying for tours; go early to get a seat.

localTips.title: Reserve classic restaurants ahead
localTips.description: Popular Czech spots (and better beer halls) fill fast—book the day before and confirm the final price includes service if a “service charge” is listed.

localTips.title: Carry small cash, but tap is king
localTips.description: Most places take contactless, yet small notes/coins help for public toilets, small bakeries, and tipping (rounding up is common).

foodToTry.title: Svíčková na smetaně
foodToTry.description: Beef in creamy vegetable sauce with dumplings and cranberries; order it at a traditional Czech pub for the classic version.

foodToTry.title: Vepřo knedlo zelo
foodToTry.description: Roast pork with dumplings and sauerkraut; a hearty, good-value lunch option outside the Old Town.

foodToTry.title: Chlebíčky
foodToTry.description: Open-faced Czech sandwiches; perfect for a quick bite from a deli counter (ask for a mixed selection).

foodToTry.title: Pilsner-style lager (čepované pivo)
foodToTry.description: Order draft beer and try different pours (hladinka/šnyt/mlíko) if offered; the foam style changes taste and texture.

gettingAround.title: Metro + trams: fastest combo
gettingAround.description: Use metro for longer jumps and trams for door-to-door routes; Google Maps works well, but PID Lítačka app is great for tickets and disruptions.

gettingAround.title: From the airport: bus + metro is simplest
gettingAround.description: Take bus 59 to Nádraží Veleslavín (metro A) for the quickest public transfer; validate your ticket before boarding.

gettingAround.title: Walking strategy in the center
gettingAround.description: Cross the river early and cluster sights by neighborhood (Old Town, Lesser Town, Castle) to avoid backtracking; comfortable shoes matter on cobblestones.

topThingsToDo.title: Ringstrasse walk + free city views
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the Ring from Staatsoper to Rathaus at dusk, then take the free elevator in Haus des Meeres’ stairwell area or a hotel rooftop bar for skyline photos without paying for big viewpoints.

topThingsToDo.title: Schönbrunn early, then the “secret” back exit
topThingsToDo.description: Go right at opening to beat tour groups in the palace; exit into the gardens and walk up to Gloriette for the best panorama without extra ticketing.

topThingsToDo.title: Belvedere + neighborhood detour
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed slot for Klimt’s “The Kiss,” then walk through the quieter 4th district lanes (Freihausviertel) for boutiques and local cafés.

topThingsToDo.title: Coffeehouse crawl like a local
topThingsToDo.description: Pick two contrasting spots: a grand café (Café Central) and a more local one (Café Jelinek); order one drink and linger—no one rushes you.

topThingsToDo.title: Danube Canal evening hangout
topThingsToDo.description: Head to the Donaukanal between Schwedenplatz and Roßauer Lände for street art, pop-up bars, and relaxed waterside seating—best after 6 pm in warmer months.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street “petition” and donation clipboards
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone asking you to sign something near Stephansplatz/Kärntner Straße—it's often a distraction for aggressive donations or pickpocketing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced concert ticket hawkers
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip promoters selling “Mozart/Vivaldi” tickets on the street; buy directly from venues (Musikverein, Konzerthaus) for real seats and transparent pricing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi add-ons and airport overcharging
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxi ranks or apps and confirm card acceptance; for the airport, avoid unsolicited drivers—use CAT/ÖBB rail or prebooked fixed-fare transfers.

localTips.title: Use a 24/48/72h Wiener Linien ticket strategically
localTips.description: Validate once and ride unlimited on U-Bahn/trams/buses; it’s often cheaper than multiple single tickets if you do museums plus evenings out.

localTips.title: Museum timing hack
localTips.description: Many major museums are quiet in the last 1.5–2 hours before closing; arrive then to avoid tour groups and get better photo moments.

localTips.title: Sunday reality check
localTips.description: Most shops close Sunday; plan groceries on Saturday and use Sundays for parks, museums, and coffeehouses instead.

localTips.title: Water and toilets
localTips.description: Carry a bottle—Vienna tap water is excellent; look for “WC” signs in cafés/department stores, and keep a few coins for paid public toilets.

foodToTry.title: Wiener Schnitzel (veal) or “vom Schwein”
foodToTry.description: For traditional, order veal; if a menu says “Wiener Art,” it’s usually pork—still tasty but not the classic.

foodToTry.title: Tafelspitz
foodToTry.description: Boiled beef with broth, applesauce, and chive sauce; go hungry because portions are large and often served in courses.

foodToTry.title: Käsekrainer at a Würstelstand
foodToTry.description: A cheese-filled sausage best late night; ask for it “mit Senf und Brot” and eat standing like locals.

foodToTry.title: Sachertorte vs. Apfelstrudel
foodToTry.description: Try both, but do it smart: get cake in a café and strudel warm with vanilla sauce—quality varies widely at tourist spots.

gettingAround.title: Public transport is the default
gettingAround.description: U-Bahn + trams are fast and safe; use Google Maps or WienMobil for real-time departures and platform info.

gettingAround.title: Airport into town
gettingAround.description: Use ÖBB Railjet/S-Bahn to Wien Mitte or Hauptbahnhof for value; CAT is faster but pricier and only goes to Wien Mitte.

gettingAround.title: Walking + short tram hops
gettingAround.description: Central Vienna is compact—walk between sights and use trams (especially lines 1/2/D) to save time and avoid unnecessary transfers.

topThingsToDo.title: Reichstag Dome + Government Quarter
topThingsToDo.description: Book the dome slot online in advance and go near sunset for the best views; bring ID for security and arrive 15–20 minutes early.

topThingsToDo.title: Museum Island (pick 1–2, not all)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose based on interest (Neues Museum for Nefertiti, Pergamon panorama/collections as available) and reserve timed tickets to avoid long queues.

topThingsToDo.title: East Side Gallery + Spree riverside walk
topThingsToDo.description: Go early morning to beat crowds, then continue along the Spree toward Oberbaum Bridge for photos and a relaxed stroll.

topThingsToDo.title: Tempelhofer Feld
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike or bring a picnic and use the old runway loops; locals go late afternoon and weekends for casual hangouts.

topThingsToDo.title: Kreuzberg & Neukölln food crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Follow Sonnenallee and around Kottbusser Tor for top Middle Eastern eats; aim for weekday evenings to avoid peak lines.

scamsToAvoid.title: Ticket inspectors on BVG
scamsToAvoid.description: Always validate paper tickets before boarding and ensure you have the correct zones; inspectors are plainclothes and fines are immediate.

scamsToAvoid.title: ATM and card skimming in nightlife areas
scamsToAvoid.description: Use bank ATMs inside branches (Sparkasse/Deutsche Bank) and avoid standalone machines near clubs; cover the keypad and check for tampering.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxi/airport rides
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxis (meter on) or rideshares and confirm the route; from BER, prefer S-Bahn/RE trains unless you have heavy luggage late night.

localTips.title: Sunday shutdown
localTips.description: Most shops close Sundays—stock up Saturday; use Spätis for essentials and plan museums/parks for Sunday.

localTips.title: Cash still matters
localTips.description: Many small bars, kebab shops, and late-night spots are cash-only; carry small bills and coins for quick payments.

localTips.title: Club entry culture
localTips.description: Dress simple, keep your group small, don’t be loud in line, and have a clear answer why you’re there; arriving earlier often improves odds.

localTips.title: Quiet hours and recycling rules
localTips.description: Keep noise down late (especially in courtyards) and use deposit returns (Pfand) at supermarkets—bring bottles/cans to the machines.

foodToTry.title: Döner kebab (Berlin style)
foodToTry.description: Try it fresh-cut with extra salad and spicy sauce; go off-peak for the best meat and shorter queues.

foodToTry.title: Currywurst mit Pommes
foodToTry.description: Order it “mit Darm” (with casing) if available for better snap; great quick meal near transit hubs and late-night spots.

foodToTry.title: Königsberger Klopse
foodToTry.description: Classic Berlin/Prussian comfort food—meatballs in caper sauce; look for it on weekday lunch menus at traditional German restaurants.

foodToTry.title: Berliner Pfannkuchen
foodToTry.description: Berlin’s jam-filled doughnut—ask which filling you’re getting (often raspberry); best picked up from a bakery in the morning.

gettingAround.title: Use BVG like a local
gettingAround.description: U-Bahn/S-Bahn/trams/buses are integrated—use a day ticket if you’ll take 3+ rides; always keep your ticket accessible for checks.

gettingAround.title: Berlin is bike-friendly (with caveats)
gettingAround.description: Use bike lanes and watch for turning cars; ride-sharing bikes are everywhere, but lock properly and avoid leaving them in courtyards.

gettingAround.title: Airport connections (BER)
gettingAround.description: RE and S-Bahn are usually fastest to the center—check if your destination is closer to Ostkreuz, Hauptbahnhof, or Alexanderplatz before choosing.

topThingsToDo.title: Acropolis early entry + Acropolis Museum
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening (or last 1–2 hours before close) to avoid crowds and heat; pair it with the Acropolis Museum and see the Parthenon frieze up close.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset on Lycabettus Hill
topThingsToDo.description: Skip pricey hilltop dining and bring water; take the funicular up and walk down through Kolonaki for a low-stress, best-view route.

topThingsToDo.title: Plaka + Anafiotika backstreets
topThingsToDo.description: Go early morning for quiet lanes and photos; climb to Anafiotika’s tiny whitewashed alleys just below the Acropolis.

topThingsToDo.title: Ancient Agora + Roman Forum combo
topThingsToDo.description: Buy a combo ticket if you’ll see multiple sites; time the Agora’s Stoa of Attalos museum midday when you need shade and A/C.

topThingsToDo.title: Athens Central Market (Varvakios) + Psyrri meze
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the market for snacks and spice shops, then eat nearby in Psyrri/Kerameikos for lively small plates without Plaka markups.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxis and “fixed price” rides
scamsToAvoid.description: Only ride with the meter running in the city; for airport/port, confirm the official flat fare before you get in and avoid drivers who approach you inside arrivals.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced drinks near tourist squares
scamsToAvoid.description: In Monastiraki/Plaka, check menus for per-person minimums and hidden “service” fees; choose spots that list prices clearly on the menu, not just a board.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street bracelets/flowers and distraction pickpockets
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t accept items handed to you “for free”; keep phones and wallets zipped on Metro Line 1/2 and around Monastiraki/Syntagma stations.

localTips.title: Book timed entry smartly
localTips.description: Choose the first or last Acropolis slot and pre-buy online; midday lines are brutal and the sun on the rock is unforgiving.

localTips.title: Best neighborhood bases
localTips.description: Stay in Koukaki (walkable to sites, calmer nights) or near Panepistimio/Syntagma (easy Metro connections); avoid Omonia-side streets late at night if you’re sensitive to grit.

localTips.title: Coffee and water habits
localTips.description: Order “freddo espresso/cappuccino” like locals; carry water—public fountains are limited and kiosks (periptera) are the fastest refill stop.

localTips.title: Day trip timing
localTips.description: For Cape Sounion, go late afternoon and stay through sunset; for Aegina/Hydra, catch the earliest ferry to beat crowds and heat.

foodToTry.title: Souvlaki vs. gyros (and how to order)
foodToTry.description: Ask for “pita souvlaki” (skewer) or “pita gyros” and specify sauces; “ap’ ola” means with everything, including fries inside.

foodToTry.title: Koulouri + bougatsa breakfast
foodToTry.description: Grab sesame bread rings (koulouri) on the go; add bougatsa (custard or cheese pastry) from a bakery for a local-style start.

foodToTry.title: Mezedes with ouzo/tsipouro
foodToTry.description: Order a few shared plates (dolmadakia, saganaki, grilled octopus) and let the kitchen pace them; it’s normal to linger and add as you go.

foodToTry.title: Loukoumades
foodToTry.description: Try honey-soaked dough bites after dinner; choose spots that fry to order so they’re crisp, not soggy.

gettingAround.title: Metro is the workhorse
gettingAround.description: Use Metro for airport, port connections, and cross-town hops; validate tickets and keep them until exit gates.

gettingAround.title: Walk the center, but plan hills
gettingAround.description: Acropolis–Plaka–Monastiraki–Syntagma is best on foot; wear grippy shoes—marble steps and polished stones get slick.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and ride-hailing
gettingAround.description: Use official taxi apps or hotel calls to avoid refusals and detours; have small bills and confirm the route if traffic looks suspicious.

topThingsToDo.title: Ride Tram 28 the smart way
topThingsToDo.description: Board at Martim Moniz before 9:00 or after 19:00 to avoid queues; ride uphill for the best views and fewer crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Belém: Jerónimos + riverfront walk
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for Jerónimos Monastery, then walk the Tagus river path to MAAT and back for a breezy, local-feeling stretch.

topThingsToDo.title: Alfama viewpoints at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Catch sunset from Miradouro de Santa Luzia or Portas do Sol, then wander downhill via back alleys to avoid the tour groups.

topThingsToDo.title: Castelo de São Jorge with a timed entry
topThingsToDo.description: Buy online for a timed slot, enter near opening, and head straight to the ramparts before the midday tour buses arrive.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to Sintra with crowd hacks
topThingsToDo.description: Take the first train from Rossio, start at Pena at opening, then do Quinta da Regaleira later when lines shift away from palaces.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Hash/weed’ street offers
scamsToAvoid.description: In busy areas (Baixa, Bairro Alto), ignore drug offers—it's usually fake and can lead to pressure or pickpocketing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overfriendly restaurant ‘helpers’
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone steers you to a “traditional” spot with no menu prices, walk away; choose places with prices clearly posted outside.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxi or ‘cash only’ surprise
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxis with the meter running or apps (Bolt/Uber); confirm luggage/bridge tolls before you move.

localTips.title: Elevador de Santa Justa alternative
localTips.description: Skip the long lift line and walk up via Largo do Carmo to the same area; you’ll still get great views from nearby miradouros.

localTips.title: Pastéis de Belém without the queue
localTips.description: Use the takeaway line or the side entrance for seated service; weekdays mid-afternoon are much faster than mornings.

localTips.title: Pick a base that saves uphill climbs
localTips.description: Stay near Baixa/Chiado or Avenida for easy transit and flatter walks; treat Alfama/Bairro Alto as places to visit, not commute through.

localTips.title: Fado that feels real
localTips.description: For a more local vibe, go to a small casa de fado in Alfama on a weeknight and book a late seating to avoid tourist-only early shows.

foodToTry.title: Pastel de nata
foodToTry.description: Eat it warm with cinnamon; order “uma nata” at the counter and don’t be shy about a second.

foodToTry.title: Bifana
foodToTry.description: Grab this garlicky pork sandwich at a no-frills snack bar; it’s a quick, cheap lunch between neighborhoods.

foodToTry.title: Bacalhau à Brás
foodToTry.description: Salt-cod with eggs and potatoes—best at classic tascas; ask if it’s made to order for the right texture.

foodToTry.title: Ginjinha
foodToTry.description: Try the sour-cherry liqueur as a quick standing shot in a tiny bar near Rossio; ask “com ou sem fruto” (with or without cherry).

gettingAround.title: Navegante card strategy
gettingAround.description: Get a Navegante/Occasional card and load 24-hour passes for metro/tram/bus on heavy transit days; it pays off quickly.

gettingAround.title: Use funiculars to beat hills
gettingAround.description: Glória and Bica save your legs and time; tap in like any transit ride and avoid expensive tuk-tuks for short climbs.

gettingAround.title: Trains for day trips
gettingAround.description: Cascais trains leave from Cais do Sodré, Sintra from Rossio; go early and sit on the left to catch river/bridge views heading out.

topThingsToDo.title: Prado Museum + Paseo del Arte timing
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed ticket and go at opening or late afternoon; pair it with a quick walk to Retiro via the Paseo del Prado to avoid midday crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Retiro Park: Palacio de Cristal + rowboats
topThingsToDo.description: Enter via Puerta de Alcalá early, hit Palacio de Cristal first, then rent a boat on the lake before 12:00 to skip the longest queues.

topThingsToDo.title: Royal Palace & Almudena viewpoint loop
topThingsToDo.description: Prebook and arrive 15–20 minutes early; after the palace, walk to Mirador de la Cornisa for a great sunset view over Casa de Campo.

topThingsToDo.title: Tapas crawl: La Latina to Lavapiés
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Mercado de la Cebada area for vermut and classic tapas, then walk to Lavapiés for global small plates—pay per drink/plate and keep receipts moving bar-to-bar.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip: Toledo or Segovia by fast train
topThingsToDo.description: Use Renfe AVANT from Madrid-Puerta de Atocha (Toledo) or Chamartín (Segovia-Guiomar) and book ahead; you can do the highlights in 6–8 hours without a tour.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Rose’/bracelet distraction pickpockets
scamsToAvoid.description: Around Sol, Gran Vía, and Plaza Mayor, ignore unsolicited gifts and keep your phone/wallet in a zipped front pocket—don’t stop to argue.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxis from hotspots
scamsToAvoid.description: If the driver won’t use the meter or claims a ‘fixed price’ beyond the official airport fare rules, get out and take an official taxi rank or use an app-based ride.

scamsToAvoid.title: Restaurant bill padding in tourist squares
scamsToAvoid.description: In Plaza Mayor/Sol, confirm prices for bread, olives, and ‘service’ before sitting; ask for the itemized bill and decline extras you didn’t order.

localTips.title: Eat on Madrid hours
localTips.description: Lunch is typically 14:00–16:00 and dinner 21:00–23:00; for earlier meals, target markets and tapas bars rather than sit-down restaurants.

localTips.title: Free/discount museum windows
localTips.description: Major museums often have limited free-entry slots; arrive 30–45 minutes early for the line and keep your plan flexible in case capacity fills.

localTips.title: Sunday vibe: El Rastro + nearby aperitivo
localTips.description: Go to El Rastro by 10:00–11:00, then walk to La Latina for vermut and conservas—avoid carrying valuables in open bags in the crowd.

localTips.title: Skip Gran Vía for evenings out
localTips.description: For better value and atmosphere, drink in Malasaña (bars), Chamberí (wine), or Huertas (classic taverns) where prices are less tourist-inflated.

foodToTry.title: Bocadillo de calamares
foodToTry.description: Get it near Plaza Mayor but choose a busy, no-frills bar; order with a caña and eat standing for the local experience.

foodToTry.title: Cocido madrileño
foodToTry.description: Best as a weekday lunch (it’s heavy); book ahead at traditional taverns and expect a multi-course service.

foodToTry.title: Chocolate con churros
foodToTry.description: Go late-night or early morning to avoid queues; dip, don’t pour, and order “porras” if you want thicker churros.

foodToTry.title: Callos a la madrileña
foodToTry.description: Try it in older tabernas with a glass of Rioja or vermut; it’s richer and spicier than most visitors expect.

gettingAround.title: Metro + Cercanías combo
gettingAround.description: Use the Metro for central neighborhoods and Cercanías trains for fast cross-city hops (e.g., Atocha–Sol–Chamartín); both are reliable and frequent.

gettingAround.title: Airport to center
gettingAround.description: Metro line 8 is cheapest but can require a transfer; Cercanías from T4 is fast, while official taxis have regulated pricing—confirm the fare category before departing.

gettingAround.title: Walking strategy in the center
gettingAround.description: Sol, Gran Vía, Plaza Mayor, and the museums are best on foot; wear comfortable shoes and use parallel streets (Fuencarral/Hortaleza) to avoid the busiest sidewalks.

topThingsToDo.title: Duomo + Cupola (Brunelleschi) early climb
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed slot and go at the first entry for cooler stairs and fewer bottlenecks; bring a small bottle of water (no large bags).

topThingsToDo.title: Uffizi Gallery with a plan
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve ahead and beeline to Botticelli rooms first, then loop back to avoid the mid-morning crush in the central corridors.

topThingsToDo.title: Accademia for Michelangelo’s David (fast in, fast out)
topThingsToDo.description: Pick the first or last timed entry; the museum is small, so focus on David and the unfinished Prisoners to maximize time.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset walk: Oltrarno to Piazzale Michelangelo
topThingsToDo.description: Start in Santo Spirito/Palazzo Pitti area, climb via the ramps to San Miniato al Monte for a quieter viewpoint, then continue to Piazzale.

topThingsToDo.title: Skip the Ponte Vecchio crowd: Arno bridges circuit
topThingsToDo.description: Cross Ponte Santa Trinita for the best Ponte Vecchio photos, then stroll to Ponte alle Grazie for a calmer riverside loop.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bracelet/rose “gift” shakedown
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone puts something in your hand, drop it on the ground and keep walking; don’t engage or negotiate.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial ‘skip-the-line’ ticket sellers
scamsToAvoid.description: Only buy timed museum tickets from official sites or the museum’s ticket office; avoid street hawkers near Duomo/Uffizi.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi overcharging and ‘broken meter’ claims
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official white taxis from stands or call/app; if a driver won’t run the meter, get out before the ride starts.

localTips.title: Time your Duomo square visit
localTips.description: Piazza del Duomo is most pleasant before 9:00 or after 19:00; midday is packed and photos are harder.

localTips.title: Water and restrooms strategy
localTips.description: Refill at free public fountains (nasoni) and plan paid restrooms at major museums/cafés—public toilets are limited in the center.

localTips.title: Aperitivo without tourist traps
localTips.description: Head to Sant’Ambrogio or San Frediano for better-value spritz + snacks; check the drink menu before sitting.

localTips.title: Leather shopping reality check
localTips.description: At San Lorenzo market, many items aren’t local leather; ask for “vera pelle” details, smell/feel the grain, and prefer fixed-price boutiques in Oltrarno.

foodToTry.title: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
foodToTry.description: Order by weight and ask for “al sangue” (rare) as locals do; share a single large cut to avoid over-ordering.

foodToTry.title: Lampredotto panino
foodToTry.description: Try it at a street trippaio stand; ask for salsa verde and a little spicy sauce for the classic combo.

foodToTry.title: Ribollita or pappa al pomodoro
foodToTry.description: Look for these in traditional trattorie at lunch; they’re best when made in advance and reheated (more flavor).

foodToTry.title: Gelato done right
foodToTry.description: Choose shops with muted, natural colors and covered tubs; pistachio should look beige/olive, not neon green.

gettingAround.title: Walk the historic center
gettingAround.description: Most highlights are within a compact area; wear grippy shoes—cobblestones get slick when wet.

gettingAround.title: Use trams for longer hops
gettingAround.description: The T1 tram is the easiest link to/from the airport and nearby districts; validate tickets before boarding to avoid fines.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and ZTL (restricted zones)
gettingAround.description: Don’t drive into the ZTL—cameras issue automatic fines; if you need a ride, take an official taxi from a stand or call one.

topThingsToDo.title: St. Mark’s Basilica early entry + Pala d’Oro
topThingsToDo.description: Go at opening or book a timed ticket to avoid long queues; add the Pala d’Oro and terrace view for the best payoff in under an hour.

topThingsToDo.title: Doge’s Palace + Bridge of Sighs
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve a skip-the-line slot and do the Secret Itineraries tour if available; it’s the only way into the hidden rooms and gives real context.

topThingsToDo.title: Bacaro crawl in Cannaregio
topThingsToDo.description: Hop between small bars for cicchetti and ombra (small wine), starting around Fondamenta della Misericordia for a local-heavy scene.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset walk: Dorsoduro to Zattere
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll from Campo Santa Margherita to Zattere at golden hour; it’s calmer than San Marco and has lagoon-facing views.

topThingsToDo.title: Murano or Burano as a half-day (pick one)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose Murano for glass demos or Burano for colors and lace; go early and return before mid-afternoon crowds swell.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed gondoliers and add-on fees
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official gondola stands with posted rates and confirm the price and duration before boarding, especially for “serenades” or detours.

scamsToAvoid.title: Restaurant “tourist menu” traps near San Marco
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid places with aggressive greeters and photo menus; check for a printed price list and ask about coperto and service charges up front.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bracelet/rose handoff and distraction pickpockets
scamsToAvoid.description: Refuse anything placed in your hand and keep bags zipped on vaporetto lines 1/2 and around Rialto, where crowds make easy cover.

localTips.title: Use side entrances and off-peak timing
localTips.description: Arrive at major sights before 9:30 or after 16:00; for San Marco area, approach via quieter calli from Castello to dodge the main bottlenecks.

localTips.title: Acqua alta planning
localTips.description: Check the tide forecast (Centro Maree) and wear waterproof shoes in fall/winter; platforms appear around San Marco but side streets can stay wet.

localTips.title: Water bottle strategy
localTips.description: Refill at public fountains (look for the “ACQUA POTABILE” sign) and carry a small bottle—shops near major sites often charge premium prices.

localTips.title: Cash for small bars
localTips.description: Many bacari prefer cash for small cicchetti orders; keep small notes/coins to speed up service at the counter.

foodToTry.title: Cicchetti
foodToTry.description: Order a few small bites like baccalà mantecato or sarde in saor; eat standing at the bar for the classic experience.

foodToTry.title: Bigoli in salsa
foodToTry.description: Thick pasta with anchovy-onion sauce; it’s best at simple trattorie away from San Marco where portions are generous and prices fair.

foodToTry.title: Risotto al nero di seppia
foodToTry.description: Squid-ink risotto with intense seafood flavor; look for places that list seasonal lagoon fish rather than generic “seafood mix.”

foodToTry.title: Fritto misto di laguna
foodToTry.description: Mixed fried seafood in a paper cone or plate; choose spots frying to order so it’s crisp, not soggy.

gettingAround.title: Vaporetto passes (ACTV)
gettingAround.description: If you’ll take more than 2 rides in a day, a 24/48/72-hour pass usually pays off; validate every time at the gate to avoid fines.

gettingAround.title: Walk smart: bridges add time
gettingAround.description: Distances look short but bridges slow you down—use landmarks (Rialto, Accademia, Frari) rather than GPS for faster routing.

gettingAround.title: Traghetto crossings
gettingAround.description: Use the stand-up traghetto gondola to cross the Grand Canal where no bridge is nearby; pay a small cash fare and it saves long detours.

topThingsToDo.title: Thermal baths (choose your vibe)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early to Széchenyi for outdoor pools or pick Gellért for architecture; bring flip-flops and a towel to avoid pricey rentals.

topThingsToDo.title: Buda Castle + Castle Hill at sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Ride bus 16 up, then walk down through Fisherman’s Bastion and the Castle District for golden-hour views over Parliament.

topThingsToDo.title: Parliament interior tour
topThingsToDo.description: Book timed tickets online days ahead (they sell out), and arrive 20–30 minutes early for security and check-in.

topThingsToDo.title: Ruin bars in the Jewish Quarter
topThingsToDo.description: Start around Klauzál tér and go before 9 pm for space; for a calmer alternative, try a small wine bar nearby instead of the main party spots.

topThingsToDo.title: Danube cruise (nighttime, shorter is better)
topThingsToDo.description: Pick a 60–75 minute evening cruise for lit-up bridges and Parliament; board 15 minutes early to grab a top-deck seat.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi overcharging
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid street-hailed or “freelancer” taxis; use the Bolt app or call a reputable company and confirm the meter is on.

scamsToAvoid.title: Menu-switch or inflated bar tabs
scamsToAvoid.description: In touristy strips, ask for a printed menu and confirm prices before ordering; decline invitations from strangers to “best bars.”

scamsToAvoid.title: ATM and currency exchange tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip Euronet-style ATMs and “0% commission” exchanges with bad rates; withdraw at bank ATMs and pay in HUF, not EUR.

localTips.title: Use the BudapestGO app
localTips.description: Buy passes/tickets and validate as required; check real-time arrivals to avoid long waits late at night.

localTips.title: Cashless is common, but keep small HUF
localTips.description: Cards work almost everywhere, yet a few bakeries/markets prefer cash; carry coins for public toilets and small buys.

localTips.title: Viewpoints without the crowds
localTips.description: For skyline photos, try Gellért Hill’s quieter paths or the Buda side near Batthyány tér for a straight-on Parliament shot.

localTips.title: Timing for markets and museums
localTips.description: Great Market Hall is best before 10:30 for less crowding; many museums are quieter midweek afternoons.

foodToTry.title: Gulyás (goulash soup)
foodToTry.description: Order it as a soup (not stew) at a traditional Hungarian place; it’s best with fresh bread and strong paprika.

foodToTry.title: Lángos
foodToTry.description: Get it hot and crispy with sour cream and cheese; avoid pre-made ones sitting under heat lamps.

foodToTry.title: Pörkölt or paprikás with nokedli
foodToTry.description: Choose chicken paprikash or a slow-cooked pörkölt; ask for nokedli dumplings instead of rice for the classic combo.

foodToTry.title: Chimney cake (kürtőskalács)
foodToTry.description: Buy from a stall where it’s baked to order over coals; cinnamon-sugar is the baseline, walnut is a solid upgrade.

gettingAround.title: Public transport passes
gettingAround.description: A 24/72-hour pass is usually the best value for multiple rides; keep it handy as inspectors do surprise checks.

gettingAround.title: Metro, tram, and night routes
gettingAround.description: Tram 2 is the scenic Danube line; at night use the 4/6 tram corridor and night buses rather than walking long distances.

gettingAround.title: Airport to city
gettingAround.description: Take bus 100E direct to the center for simplicity, or 200E to Kőbánya-Kispest + metro if you want the cheapest option.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the City Walls (early or late)
topThingsToDo.description: Go right at opening or 1–2 hours before closing to avoid heat and cruise crowds; start at Pile Gate for the best light over Fort Lovrijenac.

topThingsToDo.title: Cable Car to Mount Srđ + Homeland War Museum
topThingsToDo.description: Ride up near sunset for sweeping views, then visit Fort Imperial’s museum; prebook the cable car in peak season to skip long lines.

topThingsToDo.title: Kayak to Betina Cave & along the walls
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a morning tour for calmer seas and clearer water; ask for a route that hugs the walls and includes a swim stop at Betina Cave.

topThingsToDo.title: Lokrum Island half-day escape
topThingsToDo.description: Take the first ferry from the Old Port to beat crowds; bring water shoes for rocky entries and swim at the “Dead Sea” lagoon.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset drinks at Buža bars (cliff-side)
topThingsToDo.description: Enter through the small “Buža” opening in the south wall; arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset to grab a ledge seat.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered/‘special rate’ taxis at Pile Gate & port
scamsToAvoid.description: Use a ride-hailing app or insist the meter is on before moving; if they won’t, walk 2–3 minutes away and try again.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘private boat’ pitches at the Old Port
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm total price, duration, fuel, and maximum passengers in writing before boarding; compare with official Lokrum ferry/posted price lists.

scamsToAvoid.title: ATM dynamic currency conversion (DCC)
scamsToAvoid.description: When offered “charge in your home currency,” always choose EUR to avoid poor exchange rates and extra fees.

localTips.title: Time the Old Town for quiet
localTips.description: Aim for 7:30–9:00 and after 19:30 to experience empty streets; midday is peak when cruise groups flood Stradun.

localTips.title: Avoid the main restaurant drag on Stradun
localTips.description: Walk 1–2 lanes back (Prijeko and side streets) for better value; check menus for ‘cover’ fees and price per 100g on seafood.

localTips.title: Best quick swim spots near town
localTips.description: For easy access, try Šulić Beach by Fort Lovrijenac or the rocks below the south walls; bring water shoes for sea urchins.

localTips.title: Know the shade routes
localTips.description: In summer, stick to the north-side lanes (Prijeko area) for more shade and fewer stairs; carry a refillable bottle and top up at public taps.

foodToTry.title: Black risotto (crni rižot)
foodToTry.description: Order it as a main and expect inky cuttlefish flavor; ask if it’s made fresh that day, not reheated.

foodToTry.title: Dalmatian peka (under the bell)
foodToTry.description: Must be reserved hours ahead; choose octopus or lamb and confirm the portion size (often for 2+ people).

foodToTry.title: Oysters from Ston (kamenice)
foodToTry.description: Best with just lemon; if you can, pair with a day trip to Mali Ston for the freshest and better prices.

foodToTry.title: Rožata (Dubrovnik crème caramel)
foodToTry.description: Look for the local rose-liqueur aroma; great as a lighter dessert after seafood.

gettingAround.title: Use Libertas buses + Dubrovnik Pass math
gettingAround.description: Bus tickets are cheaper at kiosks than onboard; if you’ll do walls plus multiple museums, Dubrovnik Pass often pays off and includes buses.

gettingAround.title: Walk smart: gates and shortcuts
gettingAround.description: Pile is busiest—use Ploče Gate for smoother entry/exit; for fewer stairs, take the Jesuit Stairs only once and loop back via flatter lanes.

gettingAround.title: From airport: shuttle vs. taxi
gettingAround.description: The airport shuttle to Pile/Old Town is the best value; if using a taxi, agree on a fixed fare in advance and confirm drop-off point outside the pedestrian zone.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset from Imerovigli (Skaros Rock)
topThingsToDo.description: Walk to Skaros Rock 60–90 minutes before sunset for caldera views without Oia crowds; bring a headlamp for the walk back.

topThingsToDo.title: Oia early morning photo walk
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive before 8:00 to enjoy empty alleys and blue domes; start near the bus stop and loop down to Ammoudi viewpoint.

topThingsToDo.title: Catamaran cruise (caldera + hot springs)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a small-group catamaran that departs from Vlychada for smoother boarding and fewer crowds; wear dark swimwear for the rusty hot-spring water.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike Fira to Oia (caldera path)
topThingsToDo.description: Start by 7:00–8:00 to avoid heat and tour groups; refill water in Imerovigli and aim to finish before midday.

topThingsToDo.title: Wine tasting in Pyrgos/Megalochori
topThingsToDo.description: Book a late-afternoon tasting at a winery like Santo Wines (views) or Gaia (beach) and try Assyrtiko plus Vinsanto dessert wine.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxi ‘fixed price’ surprises
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm the exact fare before getting in (especially from the airport/port) or prebook a transfer with a written price.

scamsToAvoid.title: ATV/quad rental damage deposits
scamsToAvoid.description: Photograph the vehicle (tires, scratches) and read the insurance exclusions; avoid rentals that won’t provide a clear contract and helmet.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced donkey rides at the Old Port
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip the donkeys; take the cable car or walk the steps if you’re able, and ignore anyone pressuring you at the bottom.

localTips.title: Pick beaches by wind and timing
localTips.description: If it’s windy on the east (Perissa/Perivolos), try the south (Vlychada) or north; arrive before 11:00 for easy parking and sunbeds.

localTips.title: Dine with a caldera view without caldera prices
localTips.description: Go to Pyrgos or Megalochori for sunset dinners with village views; reserve a terrace table a day ahead in high season.

localTips.title: Avoid cruise-ship congestion
localTips.description: Between 10:30–14:30 Fira and Oia get jammed; plan beaches, wineries, or Akrotiri during those hours.

localTips.title: Book key logistics early
localTips.description: Secure rental cars/ATVs and sunset restaurants 2–7 days ahead in summer; last-minute options are pricier and limited.

foodToTry.title: Tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters)
foodToTry.description: Order them as a meze; they’re best in small tavernas using Santorini cherry tomatoes.

foodToTry.title: Fava (yellow split pea purée)
foodToTry.description: Ask for it topped with capers and raw onion; pair with local Assyrtiko for a classic Santorini combo.

foodToTry.title: Chlorotyri (fresh local cheese)
foodToTry.description: Try it as a spread or in salads; it’s tangy and usually made in small batches.

foodToTry.title: Vinsanto
foodToTry.description: Sip it after dinner or with dessert; visit a winery shop to compare styles and buy bottles at better prices than caldera bars.

gettingAround.title: Use the KTEL bus hub in Fira strategically
gettingAround.description: Most routes require changing in Fira; go early evening for easier seats and check the posted timetables at the terminal.

gettingAround.title: Rent a car for villages and wineries
gettingAround.description: A small car is easiest for narrow roads and parking; keep cash/coins for small lots and avoid driving into Oia’s pedestrian core.

gettingAround.title: Transfers for airport/port and late nights
gettingAround.description: Taxis are limited and rideshare is not reliable; prebook a shuttle/driver for ferry arrivals and after 23:00.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Royal Mile (smartly)
topThingsToDo.description: Start early (before 10am) to beat crowds; duck into closes like Mary King’s Close and Advocate’s Close for the best Old Town atmosphere.

topThingsToDo.title: Edinburgh Castle (timed entry + views)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed ticket and enter at opening; for photos, head to the battlements and then walk down to Grassmarket for classic castle angles.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset from Arthur’s Seat or Salisbury Crags
topThingsToDo.description: Arthur’s Seat is windier and longer; Salisbury Crags gives big views with less effort—go 60–90 minutes before sunset and bring a layer.

topThingsToDo.title: Dean Village to Stockbridge stroll
topThingsToDo.description: Walk Water of Leith from Dean Village to Stockbridge for a quieter side of the city; stop at a café on Raeburn Place afterward.

topThingsToDo.title: Explore New Town whisky and bookstores
topThingsToDo.description: Browse independent shops around Dundas Street/Thistle Street, then do a focused whisky flight at a specialist bar rather than a tourist tasting.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial 'cash-only' tour guides on the Royal Mile
scamsToAvoid.description: Stick to booked tours with clear meeting points and pricing; don’t follow anyone offering an unpriced “quick history” that turns into a tip demand.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ghost tours with poor reviews
scamsToAvoid.description: Some operators sell similar routes at wildly different prices; check recent reviews and avoid street hawkers pushing “last seats” deals.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi overcharging from the station or airport area
scamsToAvoid.description: Use the meter in licensed black cabs or pre-book with a reputable app; confirm the approximate fare before getting in, especially late-night.

localTips.title: Dress for four seasons in an hour
localTips.description: Wind cuts through Old Town; carry a packable rain jacket and an extra layer even if it looks clear.

localTips.title: Skip peak Royal Mile hours
localTips.description: The Mile is calmest before 10am and after dinner; use midday for museums or a café break in New Town.

localTips.title: Best quick viewpoint without the climb
localTips.description: Go to Calton Hill for sunrise/sunset views with minimal walking; it’s ideal if Arthur’s Seat is foggy or too windy.

localTips.title: Festival season strategy (August)
localTips.description: Book accommodation and key shows far ahead, but leave gaps for day-of deals; use the tram/bus instead of driving—parking is brutal.

foodToTry.title: Haggis, neeps, and tatties
foodToTry.description: Try it in a proper pub meal rather than a novelty bite; ask for whisky sauce if you want it richer.

foodToTry.title: Cullen skink
foodToTry.description: A smoked haddock chowder that’s perfect in cold weather; look for it as a starter at traditional Scottish restaurants.

foodToTry.title: Scotch pie or a proper sausage roll
foodToTry.description: Grab one from a good bakery for a cheap lunch; it’s best fresh and warm—go earlier in the day.

foodToTry.title: Cranachan (seasonal)
foodToTry.description: A classic dessert with oats, cream, whisky, and berries; if it’s not on the menu, ask what the house Scottish dessert is.

gettingAround.title: Lothian Buses (best value)
gettingAround.description: Tap/contactless is easy and frequent; use Google Maps or the Transport for Edinburgh app for real-time arrivals.

gettingAround.title: Tram (airport to city)
gettingAround.description: Fast and predictable to Princes Street/York Place; buy tickets before boarding and keep them for inspections.

gettingAround.title: Walking + hills strategy
gettingAround.description: Edinburgh is compact but steep—plan routes that zigzag via bridges and closes, and wear grippy shoes for cobbles and wet stone steps.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Town (Altstadt) walk: Lindenhof to Niederdorf
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Lindenhof for the classic river view, then wander Niederdorf’s alleys and pop into hidden courtyards around Predigerplatz.

topThingsToDo.title: Lake Zurich: Bürkliplatz to Zürichhorn
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll the promenade or rent a pedal boat in summer; for a low-effort viewpoint, detour up to Chinagarten and the lakeside parks.

topThingsToDo.title: Uetliberg sunset + Planet Trail
topThingsToDo.description: Take the S10 to Uetliberg and walk to Aussichtsturm for sunset; descend via the easy Planet Trail toward Triemli for a quieter return.

topThingsToDo.title: Kunsthaus + free design stops
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed ticket for popular exhibits, then pair it with nearby free architectural hits like the ETH main building terrace views.

topThingsToDo.title: Thermalbad & Spa Zürich (Hürlimann)
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday evening for fewer crowds; the rooftop pool has the best city panorama when it’s dark.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxis at the airport/near clubs
scamsToAvoid.description: Use the official taxi rank or apps and confirm the approximate fare before getting in; airport-to-center is often faster by train.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street petition/bracelet distraction near Bahnhofstrasse
scamsToAvoid.description: Politely refuse and keep walking—these are often pickpocket setups targeting tourists who stop and engage.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘tourist menu’ drinks in the Old Town
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask for a full menu with prices before ordering; if prices aren’t listed, choose a different spot.

localTips.title: Swim like a local in the river and lake
localTips.description: In summer, use a Badi (e.g., Oberer Letten or Seebad Enge) and stash clothes in a Wickelfisch dry bag for a one-way drift.

localTips.title: Shop smart: Sundays are mostly closed
localTips.description: Plan groceries ahead; on Sunday use the airport shops or Zurich HB’s limited open stores for essentials.

localTips.title: Free views without paying for towers
localTips.description: For skyline photos, head to Lindenhof or Polyterrasse (ETH) instead of paying for church climbs.

localTips.title: Carry a reusable bottle
localTips.description: Zurich has many public fountains with drinkable water; refill instead of buying bottled water.

foodToTry.title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes with Rösti
foodToTry.description: Classic creamy veal (or mushroom) with crispy potato rösti—best at traditional brasseries; book ahead for popular spots.

foodToTry.title: Älplermagronen
foodToTry.description: Swiss comfort food: macaroni, potatoes, cream, and cheese, often served with apple sauce—great on cooler days.

foodToTry.title: Birchermüesli
foodToTry.description: The original Swiss muesli; grab it at bakeries for a quick breakfast that’s cheaper than café brunch.

foodToTry.title: Zuger Kirschtorte
foodToTry.description: A cherry-kirsch layer cake from nearby Zug—buy a slice at a Konditorei and pair it with a coffee.

gettingAround.title: Use trams + S-Bahn with the right pass
gettingAround.description: For most visitors, a 24-hour ZVV pass for zones 110 (city) + 121 (airport) is the simplest; validate rules depend on ticket type.

gettingAround.title: Airport to city: train beats car
gettingAround.description: From ZRH, trains run every few minutes to Zürich HB in ~10–12 minutes; follow signs for “Bahn” and buy tickets before boarding.

gettingAround.title: Ferries and boats as transport, not just sightseeing
gettingAround.description: Short lake boat hops can replace tram rides on nice days; check the ZSG timetable and sit on the right side heading east for views.

topThingsToDo.title: Cycle the harbor loop
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike and do a Nyhavn → Inderhavnsbroen → Christianshavn → Islands Brygge loop; go early for quiet lanes and golden light.

topThingsToDo.title: Eat your way through Reffen (Copenhagen Street Food)
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday afternoon to skip lines; pay by card, then grab a seat by the water for sunset views.

topThingsToDo.title: Tivoli Gardens at night
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive 1–2 hours before closing when crowds thin and the lights hit; book ride passes online if you want more than a couple rides.

topThingsToDo.title: Christiansborg tower + hidden courtyards
topThingsToDo.description: Take the free tower for the best central view, then wander the inner courtyards and nearby canal paths for a calmer vibe than the main square.

topThingsToDo.title: Sauna dip at CopenHot (or harbor baths)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a slot at CopenHot for a classic Nordic sauna + cold plunge; on warm days use Islands Brygge harbor bath—bring a small towel and lock for valuables.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxis at nightlife spots
scamsToAvoid.description: Only use apps (Taxi 4x35, Dantaxi) or marked cabs; confirm card payment and ask for an estimated fare before getting in.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bar ‘tourist menu’ markups in Nyhavn
scamsToAvoid.description: Check prices before sitting and avoid vague “specials”; a quick walk to side streets in Indre By usually halves the bill.

scamsToAvoid.title: Pickpockets in crowded transit and Strøget
scamsToAvoid.description: Keep phones and wallets out of open coat pockets, especially around Nørreport and on busy buses/metro platforms.

localTips.title: Use the Copenhagen Card strategically
localTips.description: It pays off if you’ll do multiple paid attractions in 24–48 hours; otherwise buy individual tickets and focus on free neighborhoods and views.

localTips.title: Do museums late on weekdays
localTips.description: Many places are calmest after 15:00; check late openings for Glyptoteket/SMK-style schedules and avoid rainy-weekend crush.

localTips.title: Respect bike etiquette
localTips.description: Walk on sidewalks, not bike lanes; when cycling, signal turns and don’t stop in the middle of the lane—pull to the right.

localTips.title: Tap water and free public toilets aren’t equal
localTips.description: Refill bottles anywhere (tap water is excellent); for toilets, rely on major stations/malls and carry a small coin just in case.

foodToTry.title: Smørrebrød
foodToTry.description: Go for one fish (herring) and one classic (roast beef) and eat it with a fork and knife; lunch is the best value.

foodToTry.title: Pølsevogn hot dog
foodToTry.description: Order “med det hele” (with everything) at a classic stand; it’s a quick, cheap bite between sights.

foodToTry.title: Boller med ost + Danish pastries
foodToTry.description: Try a simple bun with cheese and a spandauer at a bakery in the morning; arrive before 10:00 for the freshest selection.

foodToTry.title: New Nordic tasting (splurge) or set lunch (smart)
foodToTry.description: If a tasting menu is too much, book a set lunch at a modern Nordic spot—often half the price and just as seasonal.

gettingAround.title: Metro + S-train with Rejsekort or app tickets
gettingAround.description: For short stays, use DOT Tickets app for zones and day passes; if you’ll ride a lot, consider Rejsekort (check in/out every time).

gettingAround.title: Bike rental done right
gettingAround.description: Use Bycyklen (with GPS) or a reputable shop; lock the frame to something solid—bike theft is common even in central areas.

gettingAround.title: From the airport to city center
gettingAround.description: Take the Metro M2 or regional train to Nørreport/Central Station in ~15 minutes; it’s faster and cheaper than a taxi in most cases.

topThingsToDo.title: Gamla Stan early morning loop
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 9:00 to enjoy Stortorget, the alleys, and the Royal Palace courtyards without tour crowds; grab coffee at a small bakery on Västerlånggatan side streets.

topThingsToDo.title: Vasa Museum + Djurgården walk
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed entry for Vasa, then stroll the Djurgården waterfront paths toward Rosendals Trädgård for a fika break and greenhouse café.

topThingsToDo.title: Stockholm archipelago day trip (Vaxholm or Grinda)
topThingsToDo.description: Take a Waxholmsbolaget boat from Strömkajen; pick Vaxholm for a quick half-day or Grinda for beaches and easy trails.

topThingsToDo.title: Södermalm viewpoints and vintage streets
topThingsToDo.description: Walk Monteliusvägen at sunset for the classic skyline, then browse the small shops around Hornstull and Mariatorget for a less touristy vibe.

topThingsToDo.title: Metro art crawl (T-bana)
topThingsToDo.description: Ride the Blue line for standout stations like T-Centralen, Kungsträdgården, and Rådhuset; it’s a cheap “gallery” if you already have a transit pass.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed “fixed price” taxis
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid random cabs outside Centralstation; use Taxi Stockholm, Sverige Taxi, or a ride-hailing app and confirm the price or meter before getting in.

scamsToAvoid.title: Card/contactless surcharge tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Some bars/clubs may add unexpected fees; check the total on the card terminal before tapping and ask for the itemized receipt if it looks off.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tourist-menu upcharging in Gamla Stan
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip restaurants with aggressive hosts and picture-only menus; walk two streets away or eat on Södermalm where prices and quality are usually better.

localTips.title: Fika timing matters
localTips.description: Popular cafés fill up fast; go around 10–11 or after 14:30, and look for “dagens bulle” for a cheaper pastry of the day.

localTips.title: Alcohol is a planning item
localTips.description: Systembolaget has limited hours and is closed/short on Sundays; buy wine/spirits ahead of time if you want them for the evening.
