localTips.title: Free museum windows
localTips.description: Many museums have specific free entry times/days; check each museum’s site the morning you go and book online when time slots are offered.

localTips.title: Swimming spots in the city
localTips.description: In warm months, locals swim at Tanto strandbad or Smedsuddsbadet; bring a small towel and use the public showers nearby.

foodToTry.title: Husmanskost (classic home-style lunch)
foodToTry.description: Order a weekday “dagens lunch” for meatballs, dill potatoes, or stew at a better price; it often includes salad, bread, and coffee.

foodToTry.title: Cinnamon bun (kanelbulle) or cardamom bun
foodToTry.description: Try both—cardamom is often the local favorite; buy one fresh from a bakery rather than a convenience chain.

foodToTry.title: Toast Skagen
foodToTry.description: Shrimp, mayo, dill, and roe on toast; it’s a great starter in brasseries and a reliable Swedish classic.

foodToTry.title: Pickled herring (sill) with crispbread
foodToTry.description: Have it as part of a lunch plate with potatoes and sour cream; it’s mild, varied, and very Swedish.

gettingAround.title: SL transit passes are the best value
gettingAround.description: Use the SL app for tickets/passes that cover metro, buses, trams, and most commuter ferries; validate by activating before boarding.

gettingAround.title: Use the commuter ferries like locals
gettingAround.description: Routes like 80/82 are scenic shortcuts (e.g., city center to Djurgården) and included with SL tickets, unlike many archipelago boats.

gettingAround.title: Walk and bike-smart
gettingAround.description: Central Stockholm is compact; rent a bike for Djurgården/Södermalm, but watch for cobblestones and keep right on shared paths.

topThingsToDo.title: Sauna + fjord dip at Sørenga
topThingsToDo.description: Book a floating sauna (Oslo Badstuforening) and take a quick dip in the fjord; go at sunset for the best skyline views.

topThingsToDo.title: Island-hop the Oslofjord (Hovedøya, Gressholmen)
topThingsToDo.description: Use regular Ruter ferries from Aker Brygge with a standard transit ticket; pack snacks and swim from rocky coves in summer.

topThingsToDo.title: Vigeland Park early or late
topThingsToDo.description: Visit before 10:00 or after dinner to avoid tour groups; walk the full loop from the Monolith to the bridge for the best sculptures.

topThingsToDo.title: Ekebergparken for views and art
topThingsToDo.description: Take tram/bus up and stroll the sculpture park; the lookout points give postcard fjord views without paying for a viewpoint.

topThingsToDo.title: Holmenkollen + forest walk (Nordmarka)
topThingsToDo.description: Ride the T-bane to Holmenkollen, then continue into Nordmarka for easy marked trails; stop at a cabin café (try Sognsvann area for a simple loop).

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxis at night
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip random cars outside clubs; use Oslo Taxi, Norgestaxi, or the app-based ride options and confirm the price estimate before starting.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced tourist menus near Karl Johan/Aker Brygge
scamsToAvoid.description: Check prices and look for locals at the counter; if a place pushes “set menus” without clear pricing, walk two blocks away.

scamsToAvoid.title: Ticket fines on public transport
scamsToAvoid.description: Inspectors are common and fines are steep; buy and activate Ruter tickets in the app before boarding (screenshots don’t count).

localTips.title: Use the Ruter app like a local
localTips.description: It handles tickets, live departures, and ferry access; a single Zone 1 ticket covers most sights including ferries to nearby islands.

localTips.title: Grocery stores for affordable meals
localTips.description: Grab fresh sandwiches, salads, and hot counter food at Meny/Coop Mega; look for “dagens” deals and marked-down evening items.

localTips.title: Sunday planning matters
localTips.description: Many shops close Sunday; rely on kiosks (Narvesen/7-Eleven) and plan museum/park days instead of shopping.

localTips.title: Free water and clean tap refills
localTips.description: Bring a bottle—tap water is excellent; refill at public fountains in parks and along the harbor instead of buying drinks.

foodToTry.title: Waffles with brunost
foodToTry.description: Order a warm vaffel with brown cheese (and jam) at a café or cabin stop; it’s the classic sweet-salty Norwegian combo.

foodToTry.title: Fresh shrimp sandwich (rekesmørbrød)
foodToTry.description: Best enjoyed on the waterfront; look for generous piles of hand-peeled shrimp on buttered bread.

foodToTry.title: Fish soup (fiskesuppe)
foodToTry.description: Try a creamy version with salmon/cod and dill; it’s a reliable, filling option when you want local comfort food.

foodToTry.title: Reindeer or elk (vilt)
foodToTry.description: Choose a viltgryte (game stew) or steak for a true Nordic taste; ask for lingonberry and creamy sauce on the side.

gettingAround.title: Public transport (T-bane, tram, bus, ferry)
gettingAround.description: Zone 1 covers central Oslo and Bygdøy ferries; tap in with the Ruter app ticket and watch for last departures after midnight.

gettingAround.title: Walking and waterfront paths
gettingAround.description: Central Oslo is compact; use the harbor promenade from Opera House to Aker Brygge to connect sights quickly and pleasantly.

gettingAround.title: Bikes and e-scooters
gettingAround.description: City bikes and shared scooters are everywhere; park only in designated zones to avoid fees and check speed limits in pedestrian areas.

topThingsToDo.title: Sauna at Löyly or Allas Sea Pool
topThingsToDo.description: Book ahead on weekends; bring a swimsuit for sea dips and a light jacket for the windy deck. Go on a weekday late afternoon for fewer queues.

topThingsToDo.title: Ferry to Suomenlinna Sea Fortress
topThingsToDo.description: Use the regular HSL public ferry from Market Square (same ticket as trams/metro) and pack snacks for a picnic. Walk to the less-busy western ramparts for views.

topThingsToDo.title: Design District + hidden courtyards
topThingsToDo.description: Start around Punavuori and duck into inner courtyards on Uudenmaankatu/Fredrikinkatu for small studios and galleries. Many shops close early on Sundays, so go Fri–Sat.

topThingsToDo.title: Market Square + Old Market Hall (Kauppatori/Kauppahalli)
topThingsToDo.description: Skip the priciest salmon soup tents and compare portions first; the Old Market Hall is better for quality bites. Go before 11:00 to avoid cruise crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to Nuuksio National Park
topThingsToDo.description: Take bus 245/245A from Espoo Centre and do a short marked loop around Haukkalampi. Bring water and a snack—services are limited once you’re in.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxis at stations/ports
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid drivers approaching you at the terminal; order via app or use official taxi ranks. Confirm the estimated price in-app before you ride.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “tourist menu” salmon soup
scamsToAvoid.description: Some stalls near Kauppatori charge premium prices for small portions. Check posted prices, portion size, and pay only after confirming what’s included.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street petition/bracelet distraction near busy spots
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone crowds you with a clipboard or tries to place something in your hand, keep walking and don’t engage. Hold your bag close in dense crowds.

localTips.title: Use an HSL day ticket wisely
localTips.description: Helsinki sights are mostly Zone AB; buy AB unless you’re going to the airport (ABC). Tap the same card/app on trams, metro, buses, and the Suomenlinna ferry.

localTips.title: Sunday timing matters
localTips.description: Many boutiques and smaller museums have shorter hours or close on Sundays. Plan shopping for Fri–Sat and reserve Sunday for parks, islands, and saunas.

localTips.title: Coffee culture is serious
localTips.description: Order a pulla (cardamom bun) with your coffee at a neighborhood café like in Kallio or Punavuori. Filter coffee is the default; ask for espresso-based drinks if you want them.

localTips.title: Dress for wind, not just temperature
localTips.description: Even in summer the sea breeze can feel cold on the waterfront. Pack a thin windproof layer and comfortable shoes for cobblestones and island paths.

foodToTry.title: Lohikeitto (salmon soup)
foodToTry.description: Try it in the Old Market Hall for better value and quality than some outdoor stalls. Ask for extra rye bread (ruisleipä) on the side.

foodToTry.title: Karjalanpiirakka + egg butter
foodToTry.description: Grab these Karelian pies from bakeries or supermarkets for an easy breakfast. Best warm; eat within a few hours for the right texture.

foodToTry.title: Poronkäristys (sautéed reindeer)
foodToTry.description: Order it with mashed potatoes and lingonberries at a classic Finnish restaurant. It’s richer than it sounds—share if you’re sampling multiple dishes.

foodToTry.title: Korvapuusti (cinnamon bun)
foodToTry.description: Get it fresh from a bakery in the afternoon when trays are coming out. Pair with coffee; locals often buy one to-go for a park bench break.

gettingAround.title: Trams for the center
gettingAround.description: Trams are the quickest way to hop between central neighborhoods; just tap in and keep tickets ready for inspectors. Google Maps works well with HSL routing.

gettingAround.title: Metro and commuter trains for longer hops
gettingAround.description: Use metro for eastern districts and trains for quick trips like Pasila; stations are compact and easy. For the airport you need Zone ABC and the train is usually fastest.

gettingAround.title: Walk + bike/scooter for short distances
gettingAround.description: The core is very walkable, and city bikes are great in summer for the waterfront paths. Watch for bike lanes—locals ride fast and expect you to keep right.

topThingsToDo.title: Grand-Place at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Go just before sunset for the best light, then return after dark when the guildhalls are illuminated; it’s most photogenic and calmer than midday.

topThingsToDo.title: St. Hubert Royal Galleries + chocolate crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Use the covered galleries as a rainy-day route and sample from a few shops (ask for tasting squares) instead of buying one big box.

topThingsToDo.title: Comic Strip Route + Belgian Comic Strip Center
topThingsToDo.description: Hunt the street murals in the city center, then visit the museum (Art Nouveau building) to understand Belgium’s comic culture beyond Tintin.

topThingsToDo.title: Magritte Museum + Mont des Arts viewpoint
topThingsToDo.description: Book timed entry if possible, then walk to the Mont des Arts steps for a classic skyline view; it’s a quick, high-reward combo.

topThingsToDo.title: Atomium + Laeken green loop
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve a time slot for the Atomium and pair it with a stroll in nearby parks around Laeken for a less touristy, spacious half-day.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Friendship” bracelet/petition approaches
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone trying to put something in your hand or asking you to sign a clipboard near Grand-Place/Manneken Pis; they’ll pressure for cash.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxi overcharging
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid hailing random cabs around busy stations; use licensed taxis at marked ranks or an app and confirm the meter/price before moving.

scamsToAvoid.title: Pickpocket clusters in transit hubs
scamsToAvoid.description: Bruxelles-Midi/Central and packed trams are hotspots; keep phone and wallet zipped and don’t place bags on the floor by your feet.

localTips.title: Skip the Manneken Pis crowd
localTips.description: See it early morning, then walk to Jeanneke Pis and Zinneke Pis nearby for the full (quieter) set.

localTips.title: Choose breweries over tourist beer streets
localTips.description: Go to Cantillon (traditional lambic) or Brussels Beer Project rather than overpaying on Rue des Bouchers; ask staff for a small-taster flight.

localTips.title: Markets with real local vibe
localTips.description: Do Place du Jeu de Balle flea market in the morning (best finds before 10:00) and grab cheap eats around the Marolles.

localTips.title: Languages: quick win
localTips.description: Start with “Bonjour/Bonsoir” (French) or “Goeiedag” (Dutch); switching politely to English is normal and gets better service.

foodToTry.title: Moules-frites
foodToTry.description: Order the classic with fries and split if you’re not starving; check for seasonal mussels and avoid the most touristy menu photos.

foodToTry.title: Stoofvlees (carbonnade flamande)
foodToTry.description: Try this beer-braised beef stew with fries in a brasserie; it’s a hearty, very Belgian comfort dish.

foodToTry.title: Waffles: know the two types
foodToTry.description: Get a light Brussels waffle (rectangular) with minimal toppings, and a denser Liège waffle (caramelized) for a grab-and-go snack.

foodToTry.title: Frites from a friterie
foodToTry.description: Go for double-fried fries with andalouse or samurai sauce; eat them immediately—temperature is everything.

gettingAround.title: STIB/MIVB metro, tram, bus
gettingAround.description: Use contactless card/phone to tap in; trams are often fastest for short hops in the center compared to cars.

gettingAround.title: Walk smart between neighborhoods
gettingAround.description: The center is compact, but routes from upper town to lower town are steep; use escalators/lifts around Mont des Arts to save time.

gettingAround.title: Train for quick day trips
gettingAround.description: From Bruxelles-Central you can reach Bruges, Ghent, Antwerp, or Leuven fast; buy tickets at machines and validate your platform on displays.

topThingsToDo.title: Ribeira at golden hour + riverside walk
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Praça da Ribeira, then walk the Douro promenade toward Miragaia for fewer crowds and better photos. Sit on the Gaia side for sunset views back to the old town.

topThingsToDo.title: Cross Dom Luís I and visit Jardim do Morro
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the upper deck for the best skyline view, then picnic at Jardim do Morro (arrive 30–45 min before sunset to snag a spot).

topThingsToDo.title: Port wine cellar tasting in Vila Nova de Gaia
topThingsToDo.description: Book a late-afternoon tour to pair with sunset and reserve ahead in peak season; smaller producers often give better, less scripted tastings. Compare tawny vs ruby and ask for LBV to understand styles fast.

topThingsToDo.title: Clérigos tower + hidden viewpoints
topThingsToDo.description: Go at opening or near closing to avoid queues, then walk to Miradouro da Vitória for a quieter, wide-angle city view. Combine with a coffee break on Rua das Flores.

topThingsToDo.title: Foz do Douro and Atlantic tram/bike ride
topThingsToDo.description: Ride Tram 1 along the river to Foz, then stroll the seafront to Castelo do Queijo for waves and fresh air. Wind can be strong—bring a layer even in summer.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Friendly” street petition/bracelet distractions
scamsToAvoid.description: Around Ribeira and São Bento, ignore clipboard petitions and anyone trying to tie something on your wrist—keep walking and don’t open your wallet.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “Fado/Port tasting” menus near tourist corridors
scamsToAvoid.description: If a host is aggressively inviting you in on Ribeira/Clérigos, check the menu prices and reviews first; many bundle mediocre food with marked-up drinks.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxi upsells from the airport/riverfront
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxis or rideshare and confirm the meter/estimate before moving; refuse “fixed price” offers from random drivers inside arrivals.

localTips.title: Visit Livraria Lello strategically
localTips.description: If you go, book the earliest slot and treat it like a quick photo stop; for a calmer bookshop, try Poetria or small stores around Cedofeita.

localTips.title: São Bento station timing
localTips.description: For azulejo photos without crowds, go before 9:00 or mid-afternoon; it’s an active station, so keep bags close during rush times.

localTips.title: Sunday and Monday closures
localTips.description: Many independent restaurants close Sunday dinner or Monday; line up backups in Cedofeita, Bonfim, or near Mercado do Bolhão.

localTips.title: Porto is hilly—plan by neighborhoods
localTips.description: Group sights by area (Baixa, Ribeira, Cedofeita, Gaia) and save big climbs for morning; comfortable shoes matter more than fashion here.

foodToTry.title: Francesinha
foodToTry.description: Order with a beer and ask for the sauce on the side if you’re sensitive to spice/richness; it’s heavy, so share one at lunch.

foodToTry.title: Bifana or prego sandwich
foodToTry.description: Great fast fuel between viewpoints—grab one at a no-frills café and eat standing at the counter like locals.

foodToTry.title: Bacalhau (cod) dishes
foodToTry.description: Try bacalhau à Brás or assado; ask the server what’s best that day because quality varies by preparation.

foodToTry.title: Pastel de nata and a “cimbalino”
foodToTry.description: Order an espresso (cimbalino) with a warm nata from a local bakery; sprinkle cinnamon and eat it immediately for the best texture.

gettingAround.title: Metro + Andante card
gettingAround.description: Buy an Andante card for Metro/buses and top up as needed; the Metro is the easiest airport connection (line E to Trindade).

gettingAround.title: Walk smart and use funiculars when it counts
gettingAround.description: Walk downhill through Ribeira and take the Funicular dos Guindais back up to Batalha to save your legs; it’s a small spend for a big time-saver.

gettingAround.title: Rideshares/taxis for late nights or steep hops
gettingAround.description: Use Uber/Bolt when it’s raining or you’re crossing hills at night; pickup is smoother a block away from crowded squares like Aliados or Ribeira.

topThingsToDo.title: Soak like a local (city pools + hot pots)
topThingsToDo.description: Go to Sundhöllin, Laugardalslaug, or Vesturbæjarlaug for cheaper, more local vibes than the lagoons; bring a swimsuit and follow the mandatory shower-before rules.

topThingsToDo.title: Hallgrímskirkja + Skólavörðustígur walk
topThingsToDo.description: Ride the church tower elevator for the best city view, then stroll down Skólavörðustígur for small design shops and cafés (best early morning before tour groups).

topThingsToDo.title: Harpa, Old Harbor, and Grandi food crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Time Harpa for sunset light, then walk the harbor to Grandi for breweries and casual seafood; it’s compact and easy even in bad weather.

topThingsToDo.title: Golden Circle day trip (but do it smarter)
topThingsToDo.description: Leave very early or go late-afternoon to miss crowds at Þingvellir/Geysir; add a soak at Secret Lagoon or Laugarvatn Fontana instead of rushing back.

topThingsToDo.title: Northern lights or midnight sun strategy
topThingsToDo.description: For aurora (Sep–Apr), pick a forecast-driven tour with free re-tries and check cloud cover; in summer, do a late-night coastal walk for golden-hour light.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced airport transfers and taxis
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip taxis from KEF unless you’re splitting a group fare; book Flybus/Airport Direct in advance and compare pick-up zones carefully.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tour upsells disguised as “mandatory” add-ons
scamsToAvoid.description: Some operators push premium seats, gear, or extra stops at check-in; confirm what’s included (pickup, entry fees, gear) before paying.

scamsToAvoid.title: Dynamic pricing on car rentals and insurance pressure
scamsToAvoid.description: Inspect for existing damage and photograph everything; understand gravel/sand-and-ash coverage and don’t accept last-minute add-ons without reading terms.

localTips.title: Dress for wind, not cold
localTips.description: Reykjavík’s wind cuts through clothing—use a windproof shell and a warm mid-layer; umbrellas break fast, so use a hood.

localTips.title: Use the pool routine correctly
localTips.description: You must soap-shower without a swimsuit before entering; bring a small towel and flip-flops for comfort in wet changing areas.

localTips.title: Tap water is the best free upgrade
localTips.description: Carry a bottle and refill everywhere; if hot water smells sulfuric, run the cold tap for drinking.

localTips.title: Book popular dinners early (or eat earlier)
localTips.description: Weekends fill up fast; aim for 17:30–18:30 reservations or grab counter seats to avoid long waits.

foodToTry.title: Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa)
foodToTry.description: A filling, budget-friendly meal on cold days; look for it at casual cafés and lunch spots around downtown.

foodToTry.title: Fresh fish of the day (especially Arctic char)
foodToTry.description: Ask what was landed locally and how it’s cooked; char and cod are reliable choices for quality-to-price.

foodToTry.title: Skyr (with berries) and rye bread
foodToTry.description: Grab skyr at any grocery for a cheap snack; try dense rúgbrauð with butter for a classic pairing.

foodToTry.title: Hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur
foodToTry.description: Order “eina með öllu” (one with everything) and add crispy onions; it’s fast, filling, and genuinely local.

gettingAround.title: Walk downtown, bus for anything else
gettingAround.description: Center is compact and walkable; use Strætó buses via the Klappið app for tickets and live times.

gettingAround.title: Know the tour pickup system
gettingAround.description: Many tours use numbered pickup stops to reduce traffic; confirm your stop and arrive 10–15 minutes early.

gettingAround.title: Car rental is for outside the city (and conditions matter)
gettingAround.description: In Reykjavík, parking can be pricey and limited; if driving out, check road.is and vedur.is daily and avoid F-roads without a proper 4x4.

topThingsToDo.title: Wawel Castle & Dragon
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for the State Rooms, then walk down to the Smok Wawelski dragon statue for the fire-breathing (usually every few minutes). Book the Cathedral Tower climb for the best river-and-old-town view.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Town walk: Main Square to Planty
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Rynek Główny, pop into St. Mary’s Basilica, then loop the leafy Planty park ring for a calm, traffic-free stroll. For photos, catch sunrise at the square before the carriages and groups arrive.

topThingsToDo.title: Kazimierz + Schindler’s Factory
topThingsToDo.description: Spend late afternoon in Kazimierz’s courtyards and synagogues, then pair it with the excellent Schindler’s Factory museum in Podgórze. Reserve timed entry online—walk-ins often sell out.

topThingsToDo.title: Wieliczka Salt Mine (half-day)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the early slot to avoid crowds and bring a light layer (it’s cool underground year-round). Use the official tours and leave buffer time—routes and exits can take longer than expected.

topThingsToDo.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau day trip (do it right)
topThingsToDo.description: Book official museum entry and choose an early morning departure for a quieter visit. Pack snacks/water and bring ID; security lines and transport time add up.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxis and inflated fares
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid random cars offering rides near the station/Old Town; use Bolt/Uber or licensed taxis with visible tariff and a working meter. Confirm the price in PLN before you get in if booking by phone.

scamsToAvoid.title: Currency exchange tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip street exchangers and “0% commission” kantor with bad rates—check the rate board and compare to Google mid-market. Use reputable kantors or ATMs inside banks.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘private’ Auschwitz/Wieliczka sellers
scamsToAvoid.description: Some kiosks bundle tours at steep markups and vague inclusions; buy directly from the museums or well-reviewed operators with clear pickup, entry, and guide language. Double-check that museum tickets are included, not just transport.

localTips.title: Sunday trading is limited
localTips.description: Many shops close on most Sundays (Poland’s trading restrictions), so stock up on basics Saturday. Żabka convenience stores are often open even when others aren’t.

localTips.title: Time St. Mary’s trumpet signal
localTips.description: Listen for the hejnał from St. Mary’s tower on the hour; it’s loudest near the Basilica’s north side. Arrive a few minutes early to avoid squeezing through crowds.

localTips.title: Cash helps in small spots
localTips.description: Cards are widely accepted, but older milk bars, small bakeries, and market stalls may prefer cash. Keep small bills/coins for toilets and quick snacks.

localTips.title: Avoid the worst crowds with smart timing
localTips.description: Do Wawel and Old Town before 10:00, and leave Kazimierz for late afternoon/evening when it feels more local. Weekdays are noticeably calmer than weekends year-round.

foodToTry.title: Obwarzanek krakowski
foodToTry.description: Grab this braided ring bread from a street cart (best warm, with salt or seeds). Look for the official carts near Planty and the Main Square.

foodToTry.title: Pierogi (and not just ruskie)
foodToTry.description: Order a mix: ruskie, meat, cabbage-and-mushroom, or seasonal fruit. Ask for pan-fried (podsmażane) if you like a crispy edge.

foodToTry.title: Zapiekanka in Kazimierz
foodToTry.description: Try the classic open-faced baguette at Plac Nowy—go in the evening for the full atmosphere. Split one if you’re sampling multiple toppings; they’re filling.

foodToTry.title: Żurek or barszcz + kielbasa
foodToTry.description: Warm up with sour rye soup (żurek) or beet soup (barszcz) and a simple sausage. Milk bars (bar mleczny) are the cheapest, most authentic place to try them.

gettingAround.title: Trams are fastest for most trips
gettingAround.description: Buy tickets from machines at stops or in trams (not all vehicles have them), then validate if required. Use Jakdojade to plan routes and pick the correct time-based ticket.

gettingAround.title: From the airport to the center
gettingAround.description: Take the train from Kraków Airport to Kraków Główny (fast and predictable) and walk or tram onward. If using a ride-hailing app, confirm the pickup point—airport signage can be confusing.

gettingAround.title: Walking beats traffic in the core
gettingAround.description: Old Town and Kazimierz are compact and best on foot; many streets are restricted to cars. Wear grippy shoes—cobblestones get slick in rain and winter.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Town & Royal Castle (early or late)
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 10:00 or after 19:00 to avoid tour groups; climb the St. Anne’s Church tower nearby for one of the best skyline views.

topThingsToDo.title: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed ticket online and plan 2–3 hours; the multimedia core exhibition is the highlight even if you’re not a museum person.

topThingsToDo.title: Łazienki Park (Chopin & palaces)
topThingsToDo.description: Visit on a sunny day and walk from the Palace on the Isle toward the peacocks; in season, the free Chopin concerts by the monument draw locals (arrive early for seating).

topThingsToDo.title: Praga neighborhood (street art + vodka history)
topThingsToDo.description: Explore around Ząbkowska and 11 Listopada for murals and old courtyards; pair it with the Polish Vodka Museum at Koneser for a well-run tasting.

topThingsToDo.title: Warsaw Uprising Museum
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday morning for a calmer visit; pick up the English audio guide to follow a coherent route through a huge collection.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxis from the airport/central station
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip drivers who approach you; use official taxi stands/apps (Bolt/Uber/Free Now) and confirm the plate matches the app.

scamsToAvoid.title: ATM “dynamic currency conversion” traps
scamsToAvoid.description: At ATMs or card terminals, always choose PLN and decline conversion; the offered rate is usually much worse.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced strip-club invitations
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid aggressive promoters around Nowy Świat/Old Town offering “free entry”; bills can be inflated and disputes are common.

localTips.title: Sunday shopping is limited
localTips.description: Most big stores close on many Sundays; plan groceries for Saturday or use Żabka convenience stores when needed.

localTips.title: Look for “bar mleczny” for cheap Polish lunches
localTips.description: Milk bars serve classic dishes at great prices; go around 13:00 for the freshest trays and shortest queues.

localTips.title: Viewpoints locals actually use
localTips.description: For a quick panorama, take the elevator to the Palace of Culture & Science terrace or head to the Vistula boulevards at sunset.

localTips.title: Free walking tours—tip fairly, but verify language/route
localTips.description: Check the meeting point and group size online; tours vary a lot, and good guides book out in high season.

foodToTry.title: Pierogi (dumplings)
foodToTry.description: Try ruskie (potato/cheese) or meat; ask for pan-fried after boiling for a crisp edge.

foodToTry.title: Żurek in bread
foodToTry.description: Sour rye soup often served in a bread bowl; great comfort food on cold days.

foodToTry.title: Zapiekanka
foodToTry.description: Polish open-face baguette with mushrooms/cheese; best as late-night street food after a walk in the center.

foodToTry.title: Pączki
foodToTry.description: Polish doughnuts with rose or custard filling; go early to top bakeries so they’re still warm and not overhandled.

gettingAround.title: Public transport tickets (ZTM)
gettingAround.description: Buy 20/75/90-minute tickets or 24-hour passes via biletomat machines or apps (Jakdojade); validate only paper tickets in the yellow machines.

gettingAround.title: Metro + trams for fastest cross-city trips
gettingAround.description: Use Metro lines M1/M2 to avoid traffic, then connect by tram; Google Maps works, but Jakdojade is usually more accurate for platforms and disruptions.

gettingAround.title: Airport transfers
gettingAround.description: From Chopin Airport, take SKM rail or bus 175 to the center; it’s cheaper and often as fast as a car during rush hour.

topThingsToDo.title: Grand Palace + Wat Phra Kaew (early)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening to beat heat and crowds; bring long pants/covered shoulders or rent/buy on-site. Skip unsolicited “closed today” advice and walk to the official entrance.

topThingsToDo.title: Wat Pho + riverside walk
topThingsToDo.description: Pair Wat Pho with a stroll along the Chao Phraya River afterward for great light and fewer tour groups. If you want a massage, choose the official school inside for fixed prices.

topThingsToDo.title: Chao Phraya River local ferry hop
topThingsToDo.description: Use the orange-flag boat to bounce between piers (cheap, fast, scenic) instead of sitting in traffic. Tap in/out with cash at the pier and avoid private “tour boats” upsells.

topThingsToDo.title: Chinatown (Yaowarat) night food crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Go after 6pm and follow the busiest stalls; order small plates and share to sample more. Walk side streets (Song Wat, Charoen Krung) for calmer bars and old shophouses.

topThingsToDo.title: Chatuchak Weekend Market (strategic loop)
topThingsToDo.description: Start around 10am, pin your entrance/section in your phone, and do one full loop before buying to avoid overpaying. For vintage and crafts with less heat, try the indoor sections near JJ Mall.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Temple is closed today” detour
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone offering an alternate tour or a “special ceremony”; it’s usually a shopping run to gem/suit shops. Check opening hours online and go straight to the gate.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tuk-tuk “cheap city tour” with surprise stops
scamsToAvoid.description: If they mention “lucky Buddha,” “government outlet,” or multiple stops, decline. Use tuk-tuks only for short rides with a price agreed upfront, no stops.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter refusal and padded tolls
scamsToAvoid.description: If the driver won’t use the meter, get out immediately and hail another. If using expressways, confirm who pays tolls and pay the toll booth directly when possible.

localTips.title: Time your sightseeing
localTips.description: Do temples and markets before 11am, then malls/museums mid-day, and return outdoors after 4pm. Bangkok heat and traffic peak hard in the afternoon.

localTips.title: Dress and entry rules for temples
localTips.description: Carry a light scarf and wear long shorts/pants; many sites enforce covered knees/shoulders strictly. Slip-on shoes save time because you’ll remove them often.

localTips.title: Cash and payments
localTips.description: Street food and river boats are mostly cash; keep small bills (20/50/100). ATMs can charge fees, so withdraw larger amounts less often.

localTips.title: Use official pricing cues
localTips.description: Prefer places with posted menus/prices and pay at the counter when possible. If a vendor won’t quote a price clearly, walk away—there’s always another stall.

foodToTry.title: Pad krapow (holy basil stir-fry)
foodToTry.description: Order “krapow moo/ped + kai dao” (pork/duck with fried egg) and ask for your spice level. Best from busy lunch stalls near offices.

foodToTry.title: Boat noodles (kuay tiew reua)
foodToTry.description: Start with 2–3 small bowls to find your favorite broth (beef or pork) and add chili/vinegar to taste. Great around Victory Monument.

foodToTry.title: Som tam + grilled chicken
foodToTry.description: Pair papaya salad with gai yang and sticky rice; ask “mai sai pla ra” if you don’t want fermented fish. Many top Isan spots are in malls’ food courts too.

foodToTry.title: Mango sticky rice (khao niao mamuang)
foodToTry.description: Go for ripe nam dok mai mango and warm coconut sauce; late afternoon is best when batches are freshest. Avoid versions sitting pre-plated under lights.

gettingAround.title: BTS/MRT (fastest for most trips)
gettingAround.description: Use BTS/MRT to bypass traffic; connect to malls and major neighborhoods efficiently. Buy a stored-value card if doing multiple rides to skip ticket lines.

gettingAround.title: Grab/Bolt and metered taxis
gettingAround.description: Apps reduce haggling and help with language/address issues; compare prices between apps. For street taxis, insist on meter and have your destination in Thai on your phone.

gettingAround.title: River boats for old town
gettingAround.description: Use Chao Phraya Express boats to reach temples and historic areas quickly. Check the flag color and final pier to avoid boarding tourist-only boats.

topThingsToDo.title: Hawker centre crawl (Maxwell, Old Airport Road, Tiong Bahru)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (before noon) to avoid queues; bring cash/PayNow and return trays—some stalls close once sold out.

topThingsToDo.title: Gardens by the Bay at night + Supertree Grove
topThingsToDo.description: Time your visit for the Garden Rhapsody light show and walk to Marina Bay for skyline photos without paying for an observation deck.

topThingsToDo.title: Chinatown–Telok Ayer heritage walk
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, cut through Ann Siang Hill, then explore Telok Ayer’s temples—best done late afternoon before dinner crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Southern Ridges hike (Henderson Waves to Mount Faber)
topThingsToDo.description: Go near sunset for cooler weather and city views; carry water as amenities are sparse between trail segments.

topThingsToDo.title: Pulau Ubin by bumboat + Chek Jawa wetlands
topThingsToDo.description: Take the bumboat from Changi Point Ferry Terminal; rent a bike on the island and check tide times for the best Chek Jawa boardwalk experience.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered/overpriced taxis at airports or tourist spots
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxi stands or book via Grab/Gojek; insist on the meter and decline “fixed price” offers.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overcharging in nightlife areas (boat quay/clarke quay)
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm menu prices, taxes, and service charges before ordering; avoid places that won’t show a printed menu.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake charity or survey solicitations
scamsToAvoid.description: Politely decline anyone pushing donations or “free gifts” in busy areas; legitimate charities won’t pressure you on the street.

localTips.title: Master peak vs off-peak timing
localTips.description: Avoid MRT rush hours (8–9:30am, 6–7:30pm) and popular attractions on weekends; weekday late afternoons are calmest.

localTips.title: Use “chope” culture respectfully
localTips.description: Seats at hawkers are often reserved with tissue packets or cards—don’t take those seats; queue first, then grab a table.

localTips.title: Dress for indoor cold and sudden rain
localTips.description: Carry a light layer for air-conditioned malls and a compact umbrella—storms can appear fast even on sunny days.

localTips.title: Tap water is safe and free
localTips.description: Refill a bottle at hotels and many public facilities to save money and reduce plastic waste.

foodToTry.title: Hainanese chicken rice
foodToTry.description: Order with extra chilli and ginger; try roasted vs steamed and ask for soup on the side.

foodToTry.title: Laksa (Katong-style)
foodToTry.description: Look for rich coconut broth and cockles; some stalls cut noodles short—bring a spoon and enjoy it like locals.

foodToTry.title: Char kway teow
foodToTry.description: Ask for “less sweet” if you prefer; go to busy stalls so the wok hei is strong and the noodles aren’t soggy.

foodToTry.title: Kaya toast set
foodToTry.description: Order with soft-boiled eggs and kopi/teh; learn the coffee lingo (e.g., kopi-c, kosong) to get it exactly how you like.

gettingAround.title: MRT + bus with contactless payment
gettingAround.description: Tap in/out with a contactless card or mobile wallet—no need to buy a separate card unless you want fare discounts for heavy use.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing for late nights or rain
gettingAround.description: Grab and Gojek are reliable; prices surge in storms, so consider walking into a mall entrance and waiting 10–15 minutes.

gettingAround.title: Walking via sheltered connectors
gettingAround.description: Use underground links (e.g., City Hall–Raffles Place) and covered walkways to stay dry and cool; it often beats short taxi rides in traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise hike on Mount Batur (Kintamani)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a licensed guide and start around 2–3am; bring a light jacket for the summit wind. Go on a weekday to avoid big tour crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Ubud rice terraces + subak walk (Tegalalang or Jatiluwih)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose Jatiluwih for wider, quieter trails; arrive before 9am for cooler temps. Expect small cash donations at path checkpoints.

topThingsToDo.title: Temple hopping in East Bali (Lempuyang + Tirta Gangga)
topThingsToDo.description: Start at dawn to beat traffic and photo queues at Lempuyang. Pair with Tirta Gangga mid-morning and carry a sarong (or rent on site).

topThingsToDo.title: Waterfalls with minimal crowds (Tukad Cepung or Tibumana)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for best light and fewer influencers; wear grippy sandals for slippery steps. Keep valuables in a dry bag for river crossings.

topThingsToDo.title: Nusa Penida day trip (Kelingking + Crystal Bay)
topThingsToDo.description: Hire a private driver on the island and prioritize 2–3 stops max due to rough roads. Take the earliest fast boat and confirm return time the day before.

scamsToAvoid.title: Currency exchange shorting
scamsToAvoid.description: Use bank/authorized money changers with visible rates and count cash slowly at the counter. Avoid “no commission” street booths with too-good rates.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi/driver price switching
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree on the total price (including parking, tolls, waiting) before you get in and have it written in chat. If the meter is “broken,” walk away.

scamsToAvoid.title: Temple/attraction “mandatory guide” upsells
scamsToAvoid.description: Some entrances have unofficial touts pushing expensive guides or VIP lines—confirm the official ticket desk price first. Pay only at the counter and keep the receipt.

localTips.title: Time your days around traffic
localTips.description: North–south routes (Canggu–Seminyak–Kuta–Uluwatu) jam hard 3–7pm; do long drives before 10am. Use Google Maps but add buffer on rainy days.

localTips.title: Respect ceremonies and offerings
localTips.description: Don’t step on canang sari (small offerings) on sidewalks; walk around them. If a road is closed for a procession, reroute without arguing.

localTips.title: Temple dress code made easy
localTips.description: Carry a lightweight sarong and sash to avoid rental hassles and fit issues. Cover shoulders and knees; remove shoes where locals do.

localTips.title: ATMs and cards: reduce risk
localTips.description: Use ATMs attached to banks in daylight and cover the keypad; decline dynamic currency conversion. Keep a backup card and small cash for parking/donations.

foodToTry.title: Babi guling (spit-roast pork)
foodToTry.description: Best before noon when it’s freshest; ask for a mix of crispy skin and satay. Skip if you don’t eat pork (it’s common in Bali).

foodToTry.title: Bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck)
foodToTry.description: Order ahead at popular warungs because it can sell out. Great with sambal—ask for “sedang” if you want medium spice.

foodToTry.title: Nasi campur Bali
foodToTry.description: A practical way to sample multiple dishes; point at what you want in the display case. Check for “pedas” (spicy) components before they plate it.

foodToTry.title: Lawar + sate lilit
foodToTry.description: Try at busy local spots for turnover and freshness; lawar can include raw elements, so choose cooked versions if you have a sensitive stomach. Sate lilit is usually mild and travel-friendly.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing (Grab/Gojek) with pickup strategy
gettingAround.description: Pickups can be blocked in some areas (beach clubs/markets); walk 2–5 minutes to a main road for smoother matching. Use in-app payment to avoid cash disputes.

gettingAround.title: Private driver for day trips
gettingAround.description: Best value for long loops (Ubud, East Bali, North Bali); negotiate a full-day rate and confirm fuel/parking included. Share your itinerary the night before to avoid detours.

gettingAround.title: Scooter rental (only if experienced)
gettingAround.description: Wear a helmet, avoid night riding, and photograph the bike before leaving. Carry an international driving permit and don’t leave your passport as deposit—use cash instead.

topThingsToDo.title: Victoria Peak via Peak Tram (go early/late)
topThingsToDo.description: Ride up near opening or after 8pm to dodge queues; walk the Lugard Road loop for better skyline angles than the main terrace.

topThingsToDo.title: Star Ferry + Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront at night
topThingsToDo.description: Take the cheap ferry between Central and TST near sunset, then stroll the Avenue of Stars for harbor views and photos.

topThingsToDo.title: Temple Street Night Market + dai pai dong-style eats
topThingsToDo.description: Go after 7pm for peak atmosphere; bargain lightly for goods and grab claypot rice or wok-fried noodles nearby.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike Dragon’s Back to Shek O
topThingsToDo.description: Start at To Tei Wan bus stop, finish at Big Wave Bay for a swim; bring water because shops are limited on the trail.

topThingsToDo.title: Lantau day: Ngong Ping 360 + Tai O stilt village
topThingsToDo.description: Take the cable car early, then bus/taxi to Tai O for boat tours and salted egg yolk treats; weekdays are much quieter.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tailor shops with bait-and-switch fabrics
scamsToAvoid.description: If ordering suits in TST/Central, confirm fabric code, lining, buttons, and final price in writing before paying a deposit.

scamsToAvoid.title: Electronics stores pushing “tourist warranties”
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid shops offering unreal prices then adding fees for batteries/chargers; buy from reputable chains and check return policy.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxis from tourist zones
scamsToAvoid.description: Insist on the meter and use the correct color taxi for the area; avoid drivers offering fixed prices outside hotels/ferry piers.

localTips.title: Use Octopus for almost everything
localTips.description: Tap for MTR, buses, trams, some taxis, and convenience stores; add value at MTR machines or 7-Eleven.

localTips.title: Carry cash for small eateries
localTips.description: Many cha chaan tengs and old-school dessert shops are cash-only or have card minimums; keep small notes and coins.

localTips.title: Know the MTR exits
localTips.description: Stations have many exits; use the exact letter/number from maps to save 10–15 minutes of walking.

localTips.title: Plan around humidity and rain
localTips.description: Summer downpours are sudden—pack a light umbrella and choose indoor backups like PMQ, Tai Kwun, or malls connected to MTR.

foodToTry.title: Dim sum (yum cha)
foodToTry.description: Go before 11am for fresher batches and shorter waits; order har gow, siu mai, and cheung fun.

foodToTry.title: Roast meats (siu mei)
foodToTry.description: Try char siu and crispy roast pork over rice; look for places with meat hanging and a fast-moving line.

foodToTry.title: Cha chaan teng classics
foodToTry.description: Order milk tea, pineapple bun with butter, and baked pork chop rice; expect quick service and shared tables.

foodToTry.title: Egg waffles and street snacks
foodToTry.description: Grab gai daan jai, curry fish balls, and stinky tofu from busy stalls; eat near the stand to avoid mess on transit.

gettingAround.title: MTR for speed, walk for neighborhoods
gettingAround.description: Use the MTR to hop districts, then explore on foot (Central–Sheung Wan–Sai Ying Pun and Mong Kok–Yau Ma Tei are great).

gettingAround.title: Trams on Hong Kong Island (ding ding)
gettingAround.description: Board from the back, pay when you exit; sit upstairs front for views from Kennedy Town to Causeway Bay.

gettingAround.title: Buses and minibuses for hard-to-reach spots
gettingAround.description: Use Citybus/NWFB for routes like Stanley and Shek O; minibuses are faster but require exact drop-off and can be cash-only.

topThingsToDo.title: Gyeongbokgung + secret photo spots
topThingsToDo.description: Go right at opening for empty courtyards; after the main hall, walk to Hyangwonjeong pavilion for quieter photos. Time it with the changing of the guard (check same-day schedule at the gate).

topThingsToDo.title: Ikseon-dong to Jongno night stroll
topThingsToDo.description: Start in Ikseon-dong alleys for cafes, then walk to Cheonggyecheon stream after dark for a calmer city vibe. Avoid peak weekend lines by going before 5pm.

topThingsToDo.title: Namsan Seoul Tower via the local hike
topThingsToDo.description: Skip the cable car queue and take the shaded Namsan Dulle-gil trail up; it’s an easy, scenic climb. Go near sunset, then walk down to Myeongdong for street snacks.

topThingsToDo.title: Hongdae after-hours live music
topThingsToDo.description: Catch indie shows around Hongdae/Seogyo (look for small club posters near Exit 9); doors are often earlier than you’d expect. Weeknights are cheaper and less crowded.

topThingsToDo.title: DMZ day trip (the efficient way)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a morning tour that includes Dora Observatory and 3rd Tunnel; tours sell out on weekends. Bring your passport and avoid tight schedules—returns can vary with checkpoints.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Tea ceremony’ or ‘culture’ invitation
scamsToAvoid.description: If strangers in tourist areas invite you to a “traditional experience,” decline—these can lead to overpriced bills. Walk away and don’t follow to a second location.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxi overcharging
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid drivers who approach you offering a ride at airports or nightlife zones; use Kakao T or the official taxi stand. If a meter isn’t used, get out before the ride starts.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced bar/club tab traps
scamsToAvoid.description: In some nightlife streets, promoters may lure tourists with “free entry” then inflate drink/seat fees. Only enter places with clear menus/prices and pay as you go.

localTips.title: Use Naver Map, not Google Maps
localTips.description: For transit and walking routes, Naver Map is far more accurate and shows the best subway exits. Save places in English, then copy the Korean name when needed.

localTips.title: Master subway exits and last trains
localTips.description: Some stations have 10+ exits; the right exit can save 15 minutes of walking. Last trains are earlier than many expect—check the timetable before heading out late.

localTips.title: Cash-light, but carry a little
localTips.description: Cards work almost everywhere, but small markets and some street food stalls may prefer cash. Keep a small amount of won for topping up transit or late-night snacks.

localTips.title: Etiquette that actually matters
localTips.description: Keep your voice down on public transit and don’t eat on the subway. When handing over a card or receiving something, using two hands is appreciated.

foodToTry.title: Samgyeopsal (pork belly BBQ)
foodToTry.description: Go to a busy BBQ spot in Mapo or Hongdae and order 볶음밥 (fried rice) to finish using the grill drippings. Ask for more banchan refills—they’re usually free.

foodToTry.title: Gukbap (soup + rice comfort food)
foodToTry.description: Perfect for a quick, cheap meal; try 돼지국밥 (pork) or 순대국 (blood sausage) and season it yourself with salt and saeujeot. Late-night shops are common near stations.

foodToTry.title: Gwangjang Market bites
foodToTry.description: Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and mayak gimbap; pay per dish and avoid lines by walking one row deeper into the market. Go mid-morning for easier seating.

foodToTry.title: Naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles)
foodToTry.description: Best after BBQ; choose 물냉면 (broth) or 비빔냉면 (spicy) and add vinegar/mustard gradually. Many places cut noodles with scissors—normal and helpful.

gettingAround.title: T-money card (your best tool)
gettingAround.description: Buy and top up at any convenience store or subway station; it works on subways, buses, and some taxis. Tap in/out and keep it handy—transfers are discounted automatically.

gettingAround.title: Buses for faster cross-town trips
gettingAround.description: Use Naver Map to pick the right bus; they’re often quicker than multiple subway transfers. Board at the front, tap, and tap again when getting off.

gettingAround.title: Taxis via Kakao T
gettingAround.description: Kakao T reduces language friction and shows estimated fares; regular (일반) is usually enough. In peak rain or late-night surges, switch to nearby pickup points to match faster.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Bund at golden hour + night
topThingsToDo.description: Start near Waibaidu Bridge and walk south for skyline views; come back after dark for the light show vibe without paying for a rooftop.

topThingsToDo.title: Explore the Former French Concession by foot
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll tree-lined blocks around Wukang Rd and Anfu Rd, then duck into side lanes for cafés and small boutiques away from tour groups.

topThingsToDo.title: Yu Garden + Old City, early
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening to avoid crowds, then snack-hop on nearby lanes for xiaolongbao; skip the busiest main bazaar strip if you want calmer photos.

topThingsToDo.title: Lujiazui viewpoints without the highest ticket
topThingsToDo.description: For a great panorama, try Shanghai Tower’s observation deck if you want the top view, or save money with a Bund-side bar/restaurant that has window seating.

topThingsToDo.title: Half-day art + industry in M50
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Moganshan Road (M50) galleries in the afternoon when spaces are open; pair it with a riverside walk nearby for a less-touristy slice of the city.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tea ceremony / art student invitation scam
scamsToAvoid.description: If strangers near People’s Square/Nanjing Rd invite you for tea or an “exhibition,” decline—bills can be wildly inflated and pressured.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake taxi or unmetered ride at airports/stations
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore solicitors inside arrivals and outside hubs; use the official taxi queue and insist on the meter (or use a reputable ride-hailing app).

scamsToAvoid.title: Bar/club bill switch in nightlife areas
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid being led into empty venues by street promoters; pick places with posted prices and pay at the counter with an itemized bill.

localTips.title: Use mobile payments, but have a backup
localTips.description: Many small shops are QR-first; set up Alipay/WeChat Pay before arrival, and keep some cash for edge cases.

localTips.title: Avoid peak lines with smart timing
localTips.description: Hit Yu Garden and Nanjing Rd early, and museums on weekdays; weekends can mean long security checks and queues.

localTips.title: Carry a Chinese address screenshot
localTips.description: Save your hotel name and address in Chinese for taxis and deliveries; it’s faster than trying to pronounce it.

localTips.title: Bring a transit card mindset
localTips.description: The metro is fastest for most trips; stations are huge, so plan a few extra minutes for transfers and the right exit.

foodToTry.title: Xiaolongbao (soup dumplings)
foodToTry.description: Eat carefully (bite, sip, then eat) and go early to avoid lines; compare a classic shop vs. a neighborhood dumpling stall.

foodToTry.title: Shengjianbao (pan-fried soup buns)
foodToTry.description: Best hot off the pan—ask for a fresh batch if possible and watch for splattering broth.

foodToTry.title: Hongshaorou (red-braised pork)
foodToTry.description: Try it in a Shanghainese restaurant for the sweeter local style; it pairs well with plain rice and light greens.

foodToTry.title: Congyoubing (scallion pancake)
foodToTry.description: Grab one from a street-side griddle for a cheap snack; ask for it extra crispy if you like crunch.

gettingAround.title: Metro (best default)
gettingAround.description: It’s clean, frequent, and bilingual; avoid rush hours (8–9:30am, 5–7pm) when platforms and transfers get packed.

gettingAround.title: Taxi
gettingAround.description: Use official taxis, ensure the meter is on, and keep your destination in Chinese; receipts help if you leave something behind.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing + shared bikes
gettingAround.description: Apps are great for door-to-door trips when it’s raining or late; shared bikes work well in the French Concession where streets are calm and scenic.

topThingsToDo.title: Forbidden City (Palace Museum) early-entry loop
topThingsToDo.description: Book the official ticket in advance and enter at opening; go straight to the central halls, then peel off to quieter west/east side palaces to avoid tour-group congestion.

topThingsToDo.title: Great Wall day trip: Mutianyu for views, Jinshanling for hiking
topThingsToDo.description: Choose Mutianyu for a smooth half-day with cable car; pick Jinshanling for a longer ridge walk with fewer crowds—leave by 7–8am to beat traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Temple of Heaven morning scene + park walk
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive before 9am to see locals doing tai chi, choir singing, and shuttlecock; combine with a slow loop through the cypress groves for the best atmosphere.

topThingsToDo.title: Hutongs by bike: Shichahai to Nanluoguxiang (with detours)
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike and wander side lanes behind Shichahai, skipping the busiest stretch of Nanluoguxiang; stop at small courtyards and neighborhood snack shops instead of souvenir streets.

topThingsToDo.title: 798 Art District late afternoon + dinner nearby
topThingsToDo.description: Go after 4pm for softer light and fewer families; pair gallery-hopping with a nearby restaurant in Jiuxianqiao for better value than the touristy cafes inside.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tea house/“art student” invitation scam
scamsToAvoid.description: If friendly strangers invite you for tea, calligraphy, or an English chat near Wangfujing/Qianmen, decline—bills can be massively inflated.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake taxi or “meter broken” overcharge
scamsToAvoid.description: Use the official taxi line and insist on the meter; avoid drivers who approach you inside arrivals or offer fixed prices without a receipt.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial Great Wall tours and “closed section” claims
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore salespeople saying your chosen wall section is closed; book through reputable platforms or go self-guided to the official ticket gates.

localTips.title: Payments: set up Alipay/WeChat Pay before you land
localTips.description: Most small vendors don’t take foreign cards or cash; link your card in Alipay/WeChat and keep a backup card plus some RMB for emergencies.

localTips.title: Timed-entry attractions need advance booking
localTips.description: Popular sites (especially the Palace Museum) often sell out—reserve as soon as your dates are fixed and bring your passport for entry checks.

localTips.title: Air quality and weather planning
localTips.description: Check AQI daily; on bad-air days do indoor museums (Capital Museum, National Museum) and save outdoor wall/hutong time for clearer mornings.

localTips.title: Avoid peak-hour crush on Line 1/2/10
localTips.description: If you can, travel outside 7:30–9:30am and 5–7pm; stations like Guomao and Xizhimen get extremely packed and slow.

foodToTry.title: Peking duck (北京烤鸭)
foodToTry.description: Go with 3–4 people to try more dishes; ask for two styles (pancake wraps and stir-fried duck) and reserve ahead at top spots.

foodToTry.title: Old Beijing hotpot (涮羊肉)
foodToTry.description: Order thin-sliced lamb and dip in sesame sauce with cilantro; go early for shorter waits at classic copper-pot places.

foodToTry.title: Jianbing (煎饼) breakfast
foodToTry.description: Best grabbed from a street stall near subway exits in the morning; ask for extra “bao cui” (crispy cracker) for texture.

foodToTry.title: Zhajiangmian (炸酱面) with side dishes
foodToTry.description: Mix the sauce well and add cucumber, bean sprouts, and garlic; a great quick meal between sightseeing blocks.

gettingAround.title: Subway is fastest for most routes
gettingAround.description: Use the metro to bypass traffic; download a map offline and keep your passport handy for occasional security checks at stations.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing beats street hails in rain or late nights
gettingAround.description: Use DiDi inside Alipay/WeChat for clear pickup points and pricing; double-check the license plate before getting in.

gettingAround.title: Bikes for hutongs and lakeside areas
gettingAround.description: Use shared bikes (scan via Alipay/WeChat) around Shichahai, Beihai, and side lanes; avoid main arterials where traffic is stressful.

topThingsToDo.title: Fushimi Inari at dawn or after dark
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 7:00 or after 19:00 to avoid tour crowds; walk past Yotsutsuji to quieter torii tunnels and bring a small flashlight for late visits.

topThingsToDo.title: Arashiyama bamboo + Okochi Sanso detour
topThingsToDo.description: Enter the grove around 7:00, then escape the crush by paying for Okochi Sanso Villa (garden + tea) just uphill from the path.

topThingsToDo.title: Philosopher’s Path in the rain + Nanzen-ji
topThingsToDo.description: Light rain thins the crowds and makes the canal walk photogenic; add Nanzen-ji’s aqueduct and a quick stroll to a sub-temple for calm.

topThingsToDo.title: Kiyomizu-dera via backstreets (Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive right at opening and approach from the uphill side to beat buses; exit through the lanes early before shops turn into shoulder-to-shoulder traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Nishiki Market for snacks, not lunch
topThingsToDo.description: Sample a few bites (pickles, yuba, grilled seafood) then eat a proper meal on nearby side streets to avoid overpriced, crowded stalls.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “geisha photo” solicitations in Gion
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone pushes a paid photo or “private show” on the street, decline and walk on; real geiko/maiko aren’t selling encounters curbside.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxi overcharges
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxis with illuminated roof lights and a working meter; avoid drivers who quote a flat price for common routes.

scamsToAvoid.title: Temple/tea house “special access” upsells
scamsToAvoid.description: Be wary of anyone offering secret entry or guided access at the gate; buy tickets only at the official counter and check posted prices.

localTips.title: Start early, end late
localTips.description: Kyoto’s headline spots are calmest before 8:00 and after 18:00; plan midday for indoor sights (museums, tea, shopping streets).

localTips.title: Respect photo rules in Gion
localTips.description: Many alleys ban photography; follow signs, keep phones down around maiko, and stay off private lanes to avoid fines and confrontation.

localTips.title: Use coin lockers and travel light
localTips.description: Stations like Kyoto, Sanjo, and Arashiyama have lockers that sell out; stash bags early to make temple steps and crowded buses manageable.

localTips.title: Cash and quiet manners still matter
localTips.description: Small eateries and temple shops often prefer cash; keep conversations low on buses/trains and avoid eating while walking in busy streets.

foodToTry.title: Yudofu (tofu hot pot)
foodToTry.description: Best near Nanzen-ji on cool days; go for simple sets that highlight tofu texture and yuzu/ponzu rather than heavy sauces.

foodToTry.title: Obanzai (Kyoto home-style small plates)
foodToTry.description: Look for counter spots with rotating seasonal dishes; order 3–5 small plates to sample local vegetables and lighter seasoning.

foodToTry.title: Kaiseki (seasonal multi-course)
foodToTry.description: Book lunch for better value and shorter seating times; confirm dietary restrictions in advance because substitutions can be limited.

foodToTry.title: Matcha sweets + tea in Uji
foodToTry.description: Take a short train trip to Uji for serious matcha; try thick koicha with wagashi or a matcha parfait from a reputable tea shop.

gettingAround.title: Buses are useful but slow—time them
gettingAround.description: During 10:00–16:00, buses around Higashiyama/Gion crawl; use subway + short walks or taxis for cross-town moves.

gettingAround.title: IC card + one-day passes (choose carefully)
gettingAround.description: Use ICOCA/Suica for tap-and-go; only buy a bus/subway day pass if you’ll do multiple rides—otherwise pay per trip.

gettingAround.title: Cycling is the local cheat code
gettingAround.description: Rent a bike for flat areas (Kamo River, downtown, Philosopher’s Path); avoid riding in crowded tourist lanes and use bike parking lots to prevent towing.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Dubai: Al Fahidi + Creek abra
topThingsToDo.description: Go early to Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, then take a 1 AED abra from Bur Dubai to Deira for the best quick “local” experience.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset at The View at The Palm (or Palm Boardwalk)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a sunset slot for skyline photos; for a free option, walk the Palm Jumeirah Boardwalk and grab a drink at a beachfront café.

topThingsToDo.title: Desert safari done right
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a small-group or private operator and ask for “less dune bashing, more sunset + dunes” if you get motion sick; confirm pickup time and camp quality in writing.

topThingsToDo.title: Dubai Marina to JBR walk + evening dhow cruise
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll Marina promenade to JBR at golden hour, then do a Marina dhow cruise only if it departs after 8pm (cooler + better views).

topThingsToDo.title: Dubai Mall fountain + Burj Khalifa views (without queues)
topThingsToDo.description: Watch the fountain from the Souk Al Bahar bridge; if going up Burj Khalifa, book “At The Top” on a weekday and avoid 5–8pm peak.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake ‘closed’ attractions and forced detours
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone says a site is closed and offers an alternative shop/tour, ignore and check Google/official timings yourself.

scamsToAvoid.title: Gold/Spice Souk ‘helpful’ guides
scamsToAvoid.description: Politely refuse anyone steering you to a specific stall; agree on price per gram for gold and confirm stone quality/certification before paying.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxis or “cash only” demands
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official RTA taxis or apps (Careem/Uber) and ensure the meter is on; don’t accept inflated flat rates from unofficial cars.

localTips.title: Ride the Metro strategically
localTips.description: Use Metro for traffic-heavy corridors (Marina/Downtown/Deira) and avoid rush hour (roughly 5–7:30pm) when trains get packed.

localTips.title: Dress codes are venue-specific
localTips.description: Malls are relaxed, but bring a light layer for mosques/old areas and upscale restaurants (covered shoulders/knees avoids hassle).

localTips.title: Beat the heat with timing
localTips.description: Do outdoor sights before 10am or after 5pm; midday is best for museums, malls, or a long lunch.

localTips.title: Free views that locals use
localTips.description: For Burj views without tickets, go to Burj Park, the Souk Al Bahar bridge, or Kite Beach for a skyline + sea combo.

foodToTry.title: Emirati breakfast (balaleet + chebab)
foodToTry.description: Try sweet-salty balaleet and saffron pancakes (chebab) at an Emirati café in Al Fahidi or Jumeirah.

foodToTry.title: Shawarma from a busy corner spot
foodToTry.description: Order “extra garlic + pickles” and eat it fresh; high turnover places usually mean better meat and bread.

foodToTry.title: Mandi or madfoon (Yemeni-style rice + meat)
foodToTry.description: Go with a group and order one platter to share; ask for the smoky “haneeth” option if available.

foodToTry.title: Karak chai and luqaimat
foodToTry.description: Grab karak from a small cafeteria and pair it with hot luqaimat drizzled with date syrup for an easy local snack.

gettingAround.title: NOL card (Metro/tram/bus/abra in some areas)
gettingAround.description: Buy a Silver NOL at any Metro station and top up; it’s faster than single tickets and works across most public transport.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and ride-hailing
gettingAround.description: RTA taxis are reliable and often cheaper than surge-priced apps; use Careem/Uber when you need pickup precision or larger cars.

gettingAround.title: Short hops by tram + walking in Marina/JBR
gettingAround.description: In Marina/JBR, use the tram and walk the promenades; driving here is slow and parking can cost more than the ride.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise in Sultanahmet (Hagia Sophia + Blue Mosque exterior)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive around sunrise for near-empty squares and great photos; then walk to the Hippodrome before crowds and tour groups arrive.

topThingsToDo.title: Bosphorus ferry like a local (Şehir Hatları)
topThingsToDo.description: Skip pricey cruises and take the public ferry from Eminönü/Karaköy; grab a window seat on the right side going north for best shoreline views.

topThingsToDo.title: Balat & Fener backstreets
topThingsToDo.description: Go early weekday for quiet streets and cafes; wear grippy shoes for steep cobbles and keep your route flexible to avoid crowded photo spots.

topThingsToDo.title: Kadıköy market + Moda waterfront
topThingsToDo.description: Take the ferry to Kadıköy for food stalls, meyhanes, and a local vibe; finish with a walk to Moda for sunset and tea.

topThingsToDo.title: Grand Bazaar strategy + hidden hans
topThingsToDo.description: Use it for browsing and head to nearby hans (historic courtyards) for calmer shopping; ask for the final price and pay in lira if possible.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Friendly bar invite” in Beyoğlu
scamsToAvoid.description: If a stranger insists you join a bar/club, decline—this often ends with an inflated bill and pressure to pay.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter games
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may avoid the meter, take long routes, or claim “night tariff”; use app-based rides or ensure the meter starts at 0 and stays on.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “authentic” carpet/hamam detours
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid anyone steering you to a specific shop or “family” hamam; choose places yourself and confirm full prices (including extras) before entering.

localTips.title: Use an Istanbulkart for everything
localTips.description: Buy and top up at metro/ferry stations; it works on metro, tram, bus, ferries, and funiculars and saves time versus single-use tickets.

localTips.title: Time Topkapı, cisterns, and museums smartly
localTips.description: Go right at opening on weekdays; book official online tickets where available to avoid long midday lines.

localTips.title: Prayer times and mosque etiquette
localTips.description: Plan mosque visits outside prayer times and carry socks or easy-off shoes; women should bring a scarf to avoid relying on loaners.

localTips.title: Cash and cards: what actually works
localTips.description: Many small eateries prefer cash; use ATMs attached to banks (inside/next to branches) and decline dynamic currency conversion on card machines.

foodToTry.title: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) at Eminönü
foodToTry.description: Go to the grills near the square for a quick, cheap lunch; add pickles and squeeze lemon for the classic taste.

foodToTry.title: Simit + Turkish tea
foodToTry.description: Best grabbed warm from street vendors in the morning; pair with tea at a ferry-side kiosk for a local routine.

foodToTry.title: Islak burger in Taksim
foodToTry.description: Try it late evening from the small buffets around Taksim; it’s a garlicky, steamed snack locals love after a night out.

foodToTry.title: Meyhane dinner in Kadıköy or Asmalımescit
foodToTry.description: Order a few meze, then a shared fish or kebab; ask for the day’s meze prices to avoid surprises.

gettingAround.title: Tram/metro for the European side core
gettingAround.description: The T1 tram is fastest for Sultanahmet–Eminönü–Karaköy; avoid weekday rush hours if you have luggage.

gettingAround.title: Ferries beat traffic
gettingAround.description: Use ferries between Eminönü/Karaköy and Kadıköy/Üsküdar to save time and enjoy views; check return times late night.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and ride-hailing: do it safely
gettingAround.description: Prefer apps or taxis from official stands; always confirm the destination on the map and keep small notes for payment.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Phuket Town evening wander
topThingsToDo.description: Go around Thalang/Romanee Roads at golden hour for Sino-Portuguese shophouses, murals, and cafés; visit Sun–Thu for quieter streets, or Sunday night for Lard Yai market (arrive before 6pm).

topThingsToDo.title: Island-hop without the crowds (early or south)
topThingsToDo.description: For Phi Phi/James Bond tours, choose the earliest departure and a smaller boat; for a calmer day, base on Rawai and do Coral Island (Koh Hey) or Racha Yai with snorkel stops.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise at Promthep + Yanui swim
topThingsToDo.description: Beat the tour vans by arriving before 6:15am at Promthep Cape, then drop to nearby Yanui Beach for a morning swim or kayak when the water is glassy.

topThingsToDo.title: Karon Viewpoint to Nui Beach via backroads
topThingsToDo.description: Drive the coastal viewpoints (Kata/Karon) then continue south; stop at Nui Beach for a quieter cove—confirm access fee and parking upfront.

topThingsToDo.title: Big Buddha area viewpoints (when open) + Wat Chalong
topThingsToDo.description: Pair Wat Chalong with the hilltop viewpoints for a half-day; go early to avoid heat and traffic, and dress modestly (covered shoulders/knees) for temples.

scamsToAvoid.title: Jet ski “damage” shakedown
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip jet skis on busy beaches; if you must, film a full 360° condition video, note existing scratches, and only rent from places with clear pricing and ID-free deposits.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxis and “meter broken”
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree the price before getting in or use app-based rides; for airport runs, use the official taxi queue or prebook and keep the receipt.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tour upsells and surprise fees
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask in writing what’s included (national park fees, pier transfers, fins, lunch) and confirm boat type; avoid agents pushing “VIP” upgrades at the pier.

localTips.title: Pick your beach by vibe, not fame
localTips.description: Kamala and Nai Harn are more relaxed; Kata has surf in monsoon season; Patong is for nightlife—don’t expect quiet there.

localTips.title: Time your beach for tides and wind
localTips.description: For clear water, go mornings and check wind forecasts; in monsoon (rough seas), swim only where lifeguards and flags indicate safe conditions.

localTips.title: Cash still wins at markets
localTips.description: Many night markets and local food stalls are cash-only; carry small bills (20/50/100 THB) to avoid awkward change issues.

localTips.title: Avoid the worst traffic choke points
localTips.description: The Patong hill and Chalong Circle bottleneck at 4–7pm; plan inter-beach moves before mid-afternoon or after dinner.

foodToTry.title: Kanom jeen (southern curry noodles)
foodToTry.description: Try it for breakfast at local shops with multiple curries; ask for “nam ya” (fish curry) and add fresh herbs and pickles from the side tray.

foodToTry.title: Mee Hokkien Phuket
foodToTry.description: Thick yellow noodles stir-fried with seafood and egg; order “sai kai” (add egg) for the classic old-town style.

foodToTry.title: O-aew (Phuket shaved-ice dessert)
foodToTry.description: A light jelly-and-ice dessert perfect after walking Old Town; look for small carts in the afternoon heat.

foodToTry.title: Roti + Thai tea (late-night staple)
foodToTry.description: Grab crispy banana or egg roti from street carts after dinner; request “หวานน้อย” (wan noi) if you want it less sweet.

gettingAround.title: Use ride-hailing where available
gettingAround.description: Compare prices on Grab/Bolt/Indrive depending on area; confirm pickup pins carefully in Patong and at malls to avoid delays.

gettingAround.title: Rent a scooter only if confident
gettingAround.description: Wear a helmet, carry your license/IDP, and avoid night rides in rain; take a timestamped video of the bike and don’t leave your passport as deposit.

gettingAround.title: Local buses for budget hops
gettingAround.description: Use the blue songthaew between Phuket Town and main beaches (slow but cheap), or the Smart Bus along the west coast for airport-to-beach trips.

topThingsToDo.title: Old City temples loop (early morning)
topThingsToDo.description: Start around 7–8am to beat crowds: Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang, then Wat Chiang Man; carry a light cover-up for shoulders/knees.

topThingsToDo.title: Doi Suthep + Hmong village combo
topThingsToDo.description: Go late afternoon for cooler weather and sunset views; continue to Doi Pui Hmong Village for coffee and easy short walks.

topThingsToDo.title: Sticky Waterfall (Bua Tong)
topThingsToDo.description: Bring water shoes and a dry bag; arrive before 10am for fewer tour groups and climb the grippy limestone tiers.

topThingsToDo.title: Night market strategy (where locals actually eat)
topThingsToDo.description: Skip the most crowded stalls—head to Chang Phuak North Gate night market for khao kha moo and street snacks, then walk to low-key bars on Ratchadamnoen side streets.

topThingsToDo.title: Ethical elephant experience (no riding/bathing)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a sanctuary that focuses on observation/feeding and limits contact; book directly and ask for their no-riding, no-chains policy in writing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced songthaew ‘private tour’ upsell
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may quote a cheap ride then push a full-day itinerary with commission stops; confirm destination and total price before getting in.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake/low-standard ‘elephant sanctuary’ packages
scamsToAvoid.description: Some tours rebrand riding or forced bathing as “rescue”; avoid any place offering tricks, riding, or group bathing photos.

scamsToAvoid.title: Temple donation pressure + paid ‘guides’
scamsToAvoid.description: At popular temples, someone may offer unsolicited guiding then demand payment; politely decline and use posted signs/official guides only.

localTips.title: Visit on weekdays and time it right
localTips.description: Temples and markets are calmer Mon–Thu; for Doi Suthep go after 4pm for light and fewer tour buses.

localTips.title: Coffee scene: avoid tourist clusters
localTips.description: For better beans and prices, try cafes just outside Nimman’s main lanes or in Santitham; order “less sweet” if you don’t want dessert-level drinks.

localTips.title: Burning season reality check (Feb–Apr)
localTips.description: Air can get rough—pack an N95, check AQI daily, and plan indoor days or day trips to higher/cleaner areas if needed.

localTips.title: Dress and etiquette that actually matters
localTips.description: In temples: covered shoulders/knees and shoes off; don’t point feet at Buddha images and keep voices low in prayer halls.

foodToTry.title: Khao Soi
foodToTry.description: Northern curry noodle with crispy noodles on top; ask for “mai wan” (not sweet) and add pickled mustard greens + lime.

foodToTry.title: Sai Oua (Northern sausage)
foodToTry.description: Herby, spicy sausage—best grilled at markets; pair with sticky rice and fresh veg to cut the heat.

foodToTry.title: Nam Prik Noom + sticky rice
foodToTry.description: Smoky green chili dip served with pork crackling and veggies; great quick lunch at local eateries.

foodToTry.title: Khao Kha Moo (stewed pork leg)
foodToTry.description: Go early at Chang Phuak gate stalls before it sells out; request extra pickled greens and chili-vinegar.

gettingAround.title: Songthaews (red trucks) smart use
gettingAround.description: Best for short hops—tell the driver your destination and agree on price first; if they say “meter,” they mean a higher private rate.

gettingAround.title: Grab/Bolt for fixed fares
gettingAround.description: Use ride-hailing when it’s raining or late; compare both apps for price and wait time, especially around Nimman and the Old City.

gettingAround.title: Scooter rental (only if you’re confident)
gettingAround.description: Inspect and film the bike before leaving, wear a helmet, and avoid riding at night or in rain; keep your license/IDP and insurance sorted.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Quarter street loop (early morning)
topThingsToDo.description: Walk Hoan Kiem Lake at sunrise, then weave through Hang Dao–Hang Gai–Ta Hien before 8am to see daily life and avoid traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Coffee crawl: egg coffee + salt coffee
