topThingsToDo.description: Try cà phê trứng at a classic spot near the Old Quarter, then compare with cà phê muối in a modern cafe around Ba Dinh or Tay Ho.

topThingsToDo.title: Street-food night in the Old Quarter
topThingsToDo.description: Go to Hang Buom/Hang Giay lanes for bun cha, pho, and snacks; sit where locals pack the stools and pay at the end.

topThingsToDo.title: Train Street (responsible visit)
topThingsToDo.description: If you go, book a cafe that has permission and follow staff directions; don’t stand on the tracks or block residents’ doors.

topThingsToDo.title: West Lake (Tay Ho) sunset + Tran Quoc Pagoda
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bicycle or grab a short ride to loop the lake, stop at Tran Quoc near golden hour, and finish with lakeside snacks on Thanh Nien.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter tricks and “broken meter”
scamsToAvoid.description: Use Grab (car/bike) or reputable taxis only; if a driver won’t use the meter, get out before the trip starts.

scamsToAvoid.title: Motorbike taxi price swap
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree the total price before you hop on and confirm it’s for the whole ride (not per km); take a screenshot of the quote if using apps.

scamsToAvoid.title: Money handling and fake notes
scamsToAvoid.description: Count change slowly and avoid exchanging on the street; use bank ATMs and check the zeros on 100k/200k/500k notes.

localTips.title: Crossing streets like a local
localTips.description: Step in steadily, keep a predictable pace, and don’t dart; traffic flows around you when you’re consistent.

localTips.title: Best time for key sights
localTips.description: Do Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum area and the Temple of Literature right at opening to beat school groups and heat.

localTips.title: Cash and small bills matter
localTips.description: Carry 10k–50k notes for street food and parking; many stalls can’t break 500k.

localTips.title: Dress and etiquette in pagodas
localTips.description: Cover shoulders and knees, remove hats, and keep voices low; donate in the box rather than handing cash to individuals.

foodToTry.title: Bun cha
foodToTry.description: Go at lunch (it’s a midday dish); look for smoky grilled pork aroma and order extra nem cua be (crab spring rolls) if available.

foodToTry.title: Pho bo (Hanoi style)
foodToTry.description: Eat it early morning when broth is freshest; ask for “tai” (rare) or “chin” (well-done) and add quay (fried dough) for dipping.

foodToTry.title: Cha ca (turmeric fish)
foodToTry.description: Ideal for dinner with friends; mix fish with dill, spring onion, peanuts, and lots of herbs, then wrap with rice noodles.

foodToTry.title: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls)
foodToTry.description: Order with extra fried shallots and a side of chả quế (cinnamon pork sausage); dip lightly in nuoc cham to avoid overpowering the filling.

gettingAround.title: Grab and ride-hailing
gettingAround.description: GrabBike is fastest for short hops; wear the provided helmet and confirm the license plate matches the app before riding.

gettingAround.title: Walking smart in the Old Quarter
gettingAround.description: Use small lanes parallel to main roads to cut noise and traffic; keep valuables in front pockets because sidewalks get crowded.

gettingAround.title: Airport to city (Noi Bai)
gettingAround.description: Pre-book a fixed-price car or use the official airport taxi counters; if taking public bus, confirm the final stop and keep small cash ready.

topThingsToDo.title: Saigon street-food crawl (District 1–4)
topThingsToDo.description: Go around 5–9pm: try Nguyễn Huệ side alleys, then cross to Vĩnh Khánh (D4) for seafood; bring small bills and order one dish per stall to sample more.

topThingsToDo.title: War Remnants Museum + Reunification Palace combo
topThingsToDo.description: Visit the museum at opening to avoid crowds, then walk 10 minutes to the Palace; buy tickets on-site and keep 2–3 hours total.

topThingsToDo.title: Chợ Lớn (Chinatown) temples and markets
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Bình Tây Market early morning, then loop to Thiên Hậu Temple and nearby herb streets; it’s best on weekdays when shops are open.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset on the Saigon River (waterbus or ferry view)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the Saigon Waterbus near 4:30–6pm for cheap skyline views; sit on the right side outbound for the best photo angles.

topThingsToDo.title: Coffee culture: cà phê sữa đá + hidden cafés
topThingsToDo.description: Order at the counter, pay first, and ask for “ít đá” (less ice); check old-apartment café buildings around Nguyễn Huệ for quiet views.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter tricks and fake brands
scamsToAvoid.description: Use Grab (car/bike) or only reputable taxis (Mai Linh, Vinasun); if the meter runs unusually fast, end the ride immediately and pay a fair amount.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced shoe-shine and ‘helpful’ street fixes
scamsToAvoid.description: Politely refuse and keep walking; they may start work without consent and demand a high fee.

scamsToAvoid.title: Currency confusion and inflated change
scamsToAvoid.description: Count zeros carefully (VND has many), confirm the note before handing it over, and avoid exchanging on the street—use banks or licensed gold shops.

localTips.title: Crossing streets like a local
localTips.description: Walk steadily at a constant pace and don’t dart; drivers flow around you—make eye contact and commit.

localTips.title: Beat the heat and rain
localTips.description: Plan indoor sights 12–3pm, and carry a compact poncho in rainy season (sudden showers are common even on sunny days).

localTips.title: Cash strategy
localTips.description: ATMs often limit withdrawals, so take two smaller withdrawals instead of one large; keep 20k/50k notes for street food and parking fees.

localTips.title: Where to stay by vibe
localTips.description: District 1 (walkable sights/nightlife), District 3 (quieter, leafy, cafés), Thảo Điền (expat area, brunch, more space but more rides).

foodToTry.title: Bánh mì
foodToTry.description: Order with “đầy đủ” (everything) or specify “không ớt” (no chili); best as a quick breakfast or late-night snack.

foodToTry.title: Cơm tấm (broken rice)
foodToTry.description: Try sườn nướng (grilled pork chop) with egg and pickles; go at lunchtime when the pork comes fresh off the grill.

foodToTry.title: Hủ tiếu (especially Nam Vang style)
foodToTry.description: Choose “khô” (dry with sauce) or “nước” (soup); add chili and lime gradually—spice levels vary by stall.

foodToTry.title: Ốc (snails/seafood) on Vĩnh Khánh
foodToTry.description: Point-and-order seafood by the tray, ask the price before cooking, and share a few sauces across dishes to keep it affordable.

gettingAround.title: Grab motorbike (GrabBike)
gettingAround.description: Fastest in traffic and usually cheapest; wear the provided helmet, keep your phone zipped away, and use in-app chat for pickup pin accuracy.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and airport transfers
gettingAround.description: From SGN, use official taxi lines or book Grab from the app pickup area; ignore touts offering “fixed price” rides inside the terminal.

gettingAround.title: Walk + short hops
gettingAround.description: Downtown District 1/3 is very walkable early morning or after 5pm; use 1–2 km GrabBike hops to avoid long, sweaty walks.

topThingsToDo.title: Petronas Towers (KLCC) at sunset + park night show
topThingsToDo.description: Book Skybridge tickets online early (slots sell out) and time it for golden hour; after, watch the free fountain light show at KLCC Park.

topThingsToDo.title: Batu Caves early morning
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 9am to beat heat/crowds and bring water; keep shiny items/food tucked away because macaques grab them.

topThingsToDo.title: Jalan Alor + hidden hawker alternatives
topThingsToDo.description: Use Jalan Alor for variety but compare prices; for better-value local crowds, head to ICC Pudu food court or Lot 10 Hutong (air-conditioned).

topThingsToDo.title: Merdeka Square + River of Life night stroll
topThingsToDo.description: Walk from Dataran Merdeka to Masjid Jamek and the River of Life after dark when it’s cooler and photogenic; dress modestly near mosques.

topThingsToDo.title: KL Forest Eco Park canopy walk
topThingsToDo.description: Enter from KL Tower side for the quickest access and go right at opening for quieter trails; combine with KL Tower observation for city views.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxis and 'meter broken' rides
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip street-hail taxis; use Grab and confirm pickup point in-app to avoid inflated fares and detours.

scamsToAvoid.title: Currency exchange short-changing
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid tiny booths with too-good rates; count cash at the counter and keep the receipt, especially around Bukit Bintang.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced tours/transport at Batu Caves
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore aggressive sellers pushing “mandatory” guides or shuttle fees; the caves are free (except optional attractions) and reachable by KTM.

localTips.title: Carry a small umbrella, not a poncho
localTips.description: Tropical downpours are short and intense; an umbrella also helps with sun while walking between malls and stations.

localTips.title: Use malls as pedestrian shortcuts
localTips.description: KL is humid and sidewalks can be patchy—cut through Pavilion/Suria KLCC and use covered walkways like the Bukit Bintang–KLCC link.

localTips.title: Plan around Friday prayers and mosque etiquette
localTips.description: Some areas get busy around midday Friday; at mosques, cover shoulders/knees and borrow robes at the entrance if needed.

localTips.title: Skip peak traffic with smart timing
localTips.description: Roads jam 7:30–9:30am and 5:30–8pm; do indoor sights or take rail during these windows.

foodToTry.title: Nasi lemak
foodToTry.description: Try it for breakfast with sambal, anchovies, egg and fried chicken; village-style spots often sell out by late morning.

foodToTry.title: Char kway teow
foodToTry.description: Order with extra cockles if you like it richer; best from busy wok stalls where the queue signals fresh, high-heat frying.

foodToTry.title: Bak kut teh (near Klang or PJ, also in KL)
foodToTry.description: Go for the herbal soup with you tiao (fried dough) and rice; ask for “dry” version if you want a caramelized, garlicky style.

foodToTry.title: Teh tarik + roti canai
foodToTry.description: Pair pulled milk tea with flaky roti and dhal; order “kurang manis” if you want it less sweet.

gettingAround.title: Use rail for core routes
gettingAround.description: LRT/MRT/Monorail are fast for KLCC–Bukit Bintang–Pasar Seni; tap with a Touch ’n Go card for smoother transfers.

gettingAround.title: Grab for door-to-door
gettingAround.description: Cheapest and most reliable for short hops; set pickup at a known entrance (mall lobby/hotel porte-cochère) to avoid confusion.

gettingAround.title: Airport transfers: KLIA Ekspres vs Grab
gettingAround.description: KLIA Ekspres is fastest to KL Sentral; Grab can be cheaper for groups but allow extra time during peak traffic and rain.

topThingsToDo.title: Eat through a night market (Raohe or Ningxia)
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday 6–9pm to avoid peak crowds; bring cash and start with pepper buns (Raohe) or oyster omelet and taro balls (Ningxia).

topThingsToDo.title: Hike Elephant Mountain for Taipei 101 views
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset for golden-hour photos; use the Xiangshan MRT exit signs and expect lots of stairs and humidity.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to Jiufen + Shifen (lanterns)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the train to Ruifang, then bus/taxi to Jiufen; in Shifen, write wishes on lanterns but launch only in designated tracks for safety.

topThingsToDo.title: Beitou hot springs + Thermal Valley
topThingsToDo.description: Visit on weekday mornings for quieter public baths; bring a towel and flip-flops and check the bathing rules (some facilities are gender-separated).

topThingsToDo.title: Taipei 101 Observatory + nearby hidden eats
topThingsToDo.description: Book a timed ticket online and go early evening for city lights; afterward walk to Tonghua/Linjiang Night Market for food without the Ximending crush.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxis from airports or outside stations
scamsToAvoid.description: Use official taxi stands and insist on the meter; from Taoyuan Airport, the Airport MRT is usually faster and cheaper than traffic-dependent taxis.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake “tea ceremony/tea tasting” upsell
scamsToAvoid.description: Some touristy areas push high-priced tea sets or “rare” leaves; ask for prices per gram before tasting and buy from reputable shops with marked pricing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Night market game stalls with unclear rules
scamsToAvoid.description: If the game rules or prize conditions keep changing, walk away; play only where costs and win conditions are clearly posted.

localTips.title: Get an EasyCard on day 1
localTips.description: Use it for MRT/buses, some trains, YouBike, and convenience stores; top up at MRT stations and keep a small balance for quick transfers.

localTips.title: Time your museum/temple visits to dodge crowds
localTips.description: Longshan Temple is calm early morning; National Palace Museum is easiest right after opening or late afternoon on weekdays.

localTips.title: Convenience stores are your secret weapon
localTips.description: 7-Eleven/FamilyMart do bill pay, parcel pickup, ATM cash, and solid snacks; try fresh tea eggs, onigiri, and seasonal iced teas.

localTips.title: Trash cans are scarce—carry a small bag
localTips.description: You’ll often need to hold onto cups and skewers until you find a bin; dump liquids before tossing to avoid mess in your bag.

foodToTry.title: Xiao long bao (soup dumplings)
foodToTry.description: Go beyond Din Tai Fung by trying neighborhood dumpling shops; order ginger and black vinegar and eat carefully to avoid hot broth burns.

foodToTry.title: Beef noodle soup
foodToTry.description: Ask for half tendon/half beef for the best texture; many shops offer a free self-serve pickled mustard green—add gradually.

foodToTry.title: Lu rou fan (braised pork rice)
foodToTry.description: Order with a soft-boiled tea egg and pickles; small bowls are common, so pair with a soup or side to make it a full meal.

foodToTry.title: Bubble tea and “fresh milk” tea
foodToTry.description: Choose shops that cook pearls to order (ask for warm pearls); fresh-milk versions are less sweet and taste better even with reduced sugar.

gettingAround.title: MRT is fastest; mind the last train
gettingAround.description: Stations are clean and English-friendly; last trains are around midnight, so plan night markets and bars with a backup taxi option.

gettingAround.title: Use buses for cross-town hops the MRT doesn’t cover
gettingAround.description: Google Maps is reliable for routes; tap EasyCard on and off, and board from the rear if locals are doing so on that line.

gettingAround.title: YouBike for short rides, especially along riverside paths
gettingAround.description: Register with a local number or use kiosk options where available; avoid rush-hour scooter traffic and stick to dedicated bike paths when possible.

topThingsToDo.title: Dotonbori at night + backstreets
topThingsToDo.description: Do the canal walk after dark, then duck into Hozenji Yokocho’s stone alleys for quieter bars and skewers away from the crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Kuromon Ichiba breakfast crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 10:30 for shorter lines; buy small bites (uni, grilled scallop, wagyu) and pay as you go—many stalls are cash-only.

topThingsToDo.title: Osaka Castle Park + museum timing
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive right at opening for the main tower, then spend more time in the surrounding park moats and gates—the exterior grounds are the real highlight.

topThingsToDo.title: Shinsekai + Tsutenkaku retro strip
topThingsToDo.description: Visit late afternoon, then eat kushikatsu on Janjan Yokocho; remember the local rule: no double-dipping sauce.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to Minoh Park (local nature fix)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the Hankyu to Minoh, walk the easy river trail to the falls, and try momiji tempura from stands near the entrance.

scamsToAvoid.title: Cabaret/host bar touts in Namba/Shinsaibashi
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid anyone offering “first drink free” or “cheap set”—these often lead to inflated bills; stick to places with clear menus at the door.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘tourist menu’ seafood near Dotonbori
scamsToAvoid.description: If prices aren’t clearly labeled per piece/100g, walk away; check Japanese price tags (円) and confirm total before ordering.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial ticket resellers and ‘skip-the-line’ guides
scamsToAvoid.description: Buy attraction and transit tickets from official sites, convenience stores (Lawson/7-Eleven), or station machines; avoid street sales.

localTips.title: Use depachika for great meals on a schedule
localTips.description: Department store basements (Hanshin/Umeda, Takashimaya/Namba) discount bento and sushi after ~7–8 pm—perfect for a hotel dinner.

localTips.title: Plan around last trains
localTips.description: Many lines stop around midnight; check your final connection before staying out in Namba to avoid expensive late-night taxis.

localTips.title: Aim for standing bars in Ura-Namba
localTips.description: For better value than Dotonbori, look for tachinomi (standing) spots around Nippombashi—fast service, small plates, local vibe.

localTips.title: Avoid peak transfers at Umeda/Osaka Station
localTips.description: The station complex is huge; if you’re switching lines, add 10–15 minutes and follow line names (Midosuji/Yotsubashi) not just exits.

foodToTry.title: Takoyaki
foodToTry.description: Order it extra hot and eat carefully; for crisp outside, choose shops that cook in batches and let them rest briefly before serving.

foodToTry.title: Okonomiyaki (Osaka style)
foodToTry.description: Sit at the griddle counter if available; it’s usually cooked for you—ask for extra negi (green onion) for a lighter finish.

foodToTry.title: Kushikatsu
foodToTry.description: Try mixed skewers in Shinsekai; follow the house rule: no double-dipping sauce—use the cabbage to scoop instead.

foodToTry.title: Kitsune udon
foodToTry.description: A local comfort classic; order at a station-side noodle shop for a quick, inexpensive meal between neighborhoods.

gettingAround.title: Tap-in with ICOCA (or any major IC card)
gettingAround.description: Use it on subways, private railways, and most buses; it’s also handy for vending machines and convenience stores.

gettingAround.title: Use the Osaka Metro for core areas
gettingAround.description: Midosuji Line is the spine (Umeda–Shinsaibashi–Namba–Tennoji); consider a 1-day Metro pass only if you’ll ride 4+ times.

gettingAround.title: Choose the right rail company for day trips
gettingAround.description: Hankyu is great for Kyoto/Arashiyama access, Hanshin/Kintetsu for Nara, and JR for airport/USJ—save time by matching the network to your destination.

topThingsToDo.title: Snorkel a house reef at sunrise
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for calmer water and better visibility; ask your island’s dive shop which side of the reef is current-safe that day.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to a local island (not a resort)
topThingsToDo.description: Visit islands like Maafushi, Dhigurah, Thulusdhoo, or Ukulhas for cafes, beaches, and local life—carry a light cover-up for village areas.

topThingsToDo.title: Manta ray or whale shark excursion (seasonal)
topThingsToDo.description: For mantas, aim for Hanifaru Bay (Baa Atoll) in the southwest monsoon; for whale sharks, try South Ari—confirm sightings policy and time in water before paying.

topThingsToDo.title: Night fishing + beach BBQ
topThingsToDo.description: Book with a small local operator and confirm what’s included (gear, grill, sides); bring reef shoes for rocky shorelines when landing the catch.

topThingsToDo.title: Sandbank picnic or lagoon paddle
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a half-day with tides that leave the sandbank exposed; request a dry bag and ask the captain about stingray-safe shallow zones.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bait-and-switch excursion pricing
scamsToAvoid.description: Operators may quote per-boat then charge per-person (or add “tax/fuel” later); get a written total including taxes, transfers, and gear.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed “private” speedboat transfers
scamsToAvoid.description: Cheap offers can mean unsafe boats or sudden cancellations; book through your guesthouse/resort or a reputable operator with clear departure times.

scamsToAvoid.title: Free room upgrade tied to mandatory add-ons
scamsToAvoid.description: Some deals push compulsory meal plans, excursions, or resort fees on arrival; ask for an itemized confirmation before you land.

localTips.title: Know the bikini-beach rule
localTips.description: On local islands, swimwear is typically only allowed on designated bikini beaches; keep a sarong/shirt handy when walking through town.

localTips.title: Plan around Friday and prayer times
localTips.description: Some shops and services slow down on Fridays; schedule transfers, dives, and government-office needs on other days when possible.

localTips.title: Bring reef-safe essentials that are pricey locally
localTips.description: Reef-safe sunscreen, snorkel masks that fit, and motion-sickness tablets can be limited or expensive on islands—pack them in advance.

localTips.title: Cash helps on local islands
localTips.description: Many small cafes and ferries prefer cash (MVR or USD); ATMs can run out, so withdraw in Malé or at the airport if needed.

foodToTry.title: Mas huni + roshi (breakfast)
foodToTry.description: Tuna, coconut, onion, and chili eaten with flatbread—order it with black tea for the classic morning combo.

foodToTry.title: Garudhiya
foodToTry.description: Clear tuna broth served with rice, lime, chili, and onions; add rihaakuru (fish paste) for a deeper, salty kick.

foodToTry.title: Fihunu mas (grilled fish)
foodToTry.description: Try reef fish or tuna marinated in Maldivian spices; ask for “medium chili” unless you’re used to heat.

foodToTry.title: Hedhikaa (snacks)
foodToTry.description: Grab assortments like bajiya and gulha at local cafes in the afternoon; go early because popular items sell out.

gettingAround.title: Public ferries (cheapest, slowest)
gettingAround.description: Great for budget travel between local islands, but schedules can change with weather; confirm the latest timetable with your guesthouse.

gettingAround.title: Speedboats (fast, mid-range)
gettingAround.description: Best for most atolls near Malé and many local islands; reserve seats ahead and ask about baggage limits and sea conditions.

gettingAround.title: Domestic flights + boat (for far atolls)
gettingAround.description: Use for places like Baa, Noonu, Laamu, or Addu; align flight times with resort/guesthouse boat transfers to avoid long waits.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise at Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive around 6:00–7:00 am to beat crowds and haze; walk up from the west steps for the classic valley view and fewer touts.

topThingsToDo.title: Boudhanath Stupa + monastery rooftops
topThingsToDo.description: Go at dusk when butter lamps are lit; take one clockwise kora, then grab a rooftop tea on the north side for a quieter view.

topThingsToDo.title: Pashupatinath evening aarti
topThingsToDo.description: Watch the ceremony from the east bank across the Bagmati for the best vantage; keep a respectful distance and skip anyone selling “special access.”

topThingsToDo.title: Kathmandu Durbar Square + hidden courtyards
topThingsToDo.description: Ask locals for Kumari Ghar timings and wander into nearby bahals (courtyards) like Itum Bahal for a calmer Newari vibe after the main square.

topThingsToDo.title: Patan day trip for craft streets
topThingsToDo.description: Head to Patan Durbar Square early, then walk to Oku Bahal and the metalwork alleys around Mahabouddha for artisans without Thamel pricing.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Government tourism office” or “closed road” helpers
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone insists your hotel/route is closed and redirects you to a “friend’s” agency, leave and go directly to your booked place or a known office.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi without a clear fare
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may quote inflated “tourist rates” or claim the meter is broken; agree on a price before getting in or use a ride-hailing app.

scamsToAvoid.title: Temple ‘donation’ pressure
scamsToAvoid.description: Random “priests” may tie a thread/tilak then demand high payment; refuse services you didn’t ask for and give only what you choose.

localTips.title: Time your sightseeing for clear skies
localTips.description: Best visibility is usually early morning; plan viewpoints first and save indoor museums/shops for midday haze.

localTips.title: Carry small notes and coins
localTips.description: Entry tickets, tips, and snacks often require exact change; ATMs can run out or add fees, so top up when you find a working one.

localTips.title: Use a scarf or mask on busy roads
localTips.description: Dust and exhaust are intense on Ring Road and Thamel lanes; a simple covering makes walking far more comfortable.

localTips.title: Respect clockwise movement at stupas
localTips.description: Walk clockwise around Boudha/Swayambhu and don’t step on prayer flags or mani stones; it helps you blend in and avoid awkward moments.

foodToTry.title: Momos (steam or jhol)
foodToTry.description: Try jhol momo (in spicy broth) at busy local spots; ask for “medium” spice unless you’re sure about Kathmandu heat.

foodToTry.title: Newari khaja set
foodToTry.description: Order a small sampler plate with bara, choila, and aloo; it’s the quickest way to taste Newari flavors beyond dal bhat.

foodToTry.title: Thakali dal bhat
foodToTry.description: Go for Thakali-style for cleaner, balanced curries; many places offer refills, so arrive hungry and pace yourself.

foodToTry.title: Sel roti with milk tea
foodToTry.description: Best in the morning from neighborhood bakeries; pair with chiya for a simple local breakfast.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing over street taxis
gettingAround.description: Use apps like Pathao or inDrive for more predictable pricing; confirm pickup points on main roads because alley access is limited.

gettingAround.title: Microbuses/local buses for short hops
gettingAround.description: Cheap and frequent on main corridors, but crowded; ask “Patan/Boudha/Kalanki?” before boarding and keep valuables in front pockets.

gettingAround.title: Walk between close neighborhoods (with a map)
gettingAround.description: Thamel–Ason–Indra Chowk routes are faster on foot than traffic; download offline maps since lanes are maze-like and signage is scarce.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset walk at Galle Face Green + street snacks
topThingsToDo.description: Go 5:00–7:00pm for the sea breeze and busiest food stalls; try isso wade (prawn fritters) and manioc chips, and keep small notes for quick payments.

topThingsToDo.title: Pettah Market backstreets (guided self-walk)
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Main Street, then duck into Sea Street (gold), 1st/2nd Cross (textiles) and the spice lanes; go early morning for less heat and fewer touts.

topThingsToDo.title: Colombo Fort heritage loop
topThingsToDo.description: Walk from the Old Dutch Hospital complex to Cargills Building and the Fort Clock Tower; weekdays show the area’s working-city vibe, weekends are quieter.

topThingsToDo.title: Gangaramaya Temple + Seema Malaka
topThingsToDo.description: Visit late afternoon to avoid crowds; cover shoulders/knees and remove shoes, then cross to Seema Malaka on Beira Lake for photos and calm.

topThingsToDo.title: Colombo National Museum + Cinnamon Gardens stroll
topThingsToDo.description: Pair the museum with a walk around Viharamahadevi Park and leafy side streets; it’s a cooler, low-hassle break from the traffic-heavy core.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tuk-tuk meter “broken” / inflated fare
scamsToAvoid.description: Use PickMe/Uber for set pricing or agree the total before getting in; if they won’t, take the next tuk.

scamsToAvoid.title: Temple/attraction ‘closed’ redirect
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore strangers claiming a site is closed and offering a “special” alternative; confirm on Google/at the gate and keep walking.

scamsToAvoid.title: Gem/spice shop commission detours
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may push “government-approved” gem or spice shops; say no firmly and don’t enter if you’re not buying—prices are rarely fair.

localTips.title: Cash and change matter
localTips.description: Many snack stalls and small shops prefer cash; carry small LKR notes for tuk rides, markets, and tipping.

localTips.title: Dress and timing for temples
localTips.description: Bring a light scarf to cover up and socks for hot ground; mornings are cooler and quieter for worship sites.

localTips.title: Plan around traffic
localTips.description: Cross-town trips can crawl in rush hours (8–10am, 4:30–7pm); bundle nearby sights and use trains for longer jumps when possible.

localTips.title: Buying tea and souvenirs smartly
localTips.description: For tea, choose sealed packs from reputable supermarkets or official shops and compare prices; in markets, ask the price first and bargain politely.

foodToTry.title: Rice & curry (lunch plates)
foodToTry.description: Go at lunchtime for the freshest trays; ask for “less spicy” if needed and try at least one mallung (greens) and a sour curry.

foodToTry.title: Kottu roti
foodToTry.description: Best eaten hot off the griddle; order chicken/cheese/veg and ask for “not too spicy” if you’re heat-sensitive.

foodToTry.title: Hoppers (appa) + egg hopper
foodToTry.description: Ideal for breakfast or dinner; pair with pol sambol and a mild dhal curry for balance.

foodToTry.title: Isso wade and other Galle Face bites
foodToTry.description: Choose stalls with high turnover and hot oil; eat while walking and keep napkins—hands get oily fast.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing (PickMe/Uber)
gettingAround.description: Best value and least hassle for tuk-tuks and cars; double-check pickup pin and keep small cash for tips or when cards fail.

gettingAround.title: Tuk-tuks on the street
gettingAround.description: Good for short hops—set the fare before you start and avoid letting drivers “suggest” extra stops.

gettingAround.title: Local trains for longer moves
gettingAround.description: Useful to reach coastal areas or suburbs cheaply; buy tickets at the station, keep an eye on belongings, and expect crowded peak times.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Siq early to beat crowds
topThingsToDo.description: Enter at opening time and walk the Siq in the cool morning light for the quietest approach to the Treasury and best photos.

topThingsToDo.title: Climb to the Monastery (Ad-Deir)
topThingsToDo.description: Go mid-morning or late afternoon; bring water and take short breaks at the tea stalls near the top for shade and views.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike to the High Place of Sacrifice
topThingsToDo.description: Start before 9am for shade and clearer views; descend via Wadi Farasa to see the Garden Temple and Soldier’s Tomb on the way back.

topThingsToDo.title: Explore the Royal Tombs at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Head to the Urn, Silk, Corinthian, and Palace Tombs late afternoon when the rock colors pop and the crowds thin.

topThingsToDo.title: Visit Little Petra (Siq al-Barid)
topThingsToDo.description: Go the day before or after Petra for a quieter canyon and painted interiors; combine with a sunset viewpoint on the back ridge.

scamsToAvoid.title: "Free" guiding then demanding money
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone offers to “show a shortcut” or “best photo spot,” agree on a fixed price upfront or politely decline and keep walking.

scamsToAvoid.title: Animal rides with unclear pricing
scamsToAvoid.description: Donkey/horse/camel handlers may quote one-way then charge extra for return or tips; confirm total cost, distance, and where it ends before mounting.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced tea/souvenirs at viewpoints
scamsToAvoid.description: Some stalls charge tourist rates when you sit; ask the price before ordering and carry small bills to avoid “no change” upsells.

localTips.title: Use the back door to the Monastery (if time allows)
localTips.description: Arrange a 4x4 to Little Petra and hike in to reach Ad-Deir with fewer steps and crowds; start early to avoid midday heat.

localTips.title: Plan your days around light and heat
localTips.description: Do Siq + Treasury first, then shaded trails midday; save open areas like the Royal Tombs for late afternoon.

localTips.title: Bring the right cash and gear
localTips.description: Carry small JD notes for water/snacks and tips, plus a sun hat and grippy shoes—slick sandstone steps are common.

localTips.title: Stay in Wadi Musa and walk to the gate
localTips.description: Hotels near the visitor center let you enter at opening time without taxis and return quickly for a midday rest.

foodToTry.title: Mansaf
foodToTry.description: Jordan’s signature lamb-and-rice dish with jameed yogurt sauce; try it in Wadi Musa for a hearty post-hike meal.

foodToTry.title: Zarb (Bedouin pit-cooked meal)
foodToTry.description: Slow-cooked meat and vegetables, often served as a set dinner; book ahead at a reputable camp or restaurant.

foodToTry.title: Falafel and hummus breakfast
foodToTry.description: Grab a quick, cheap plate in town before entering Petra; ask for fresh-baked khubz bread.

foodToTry.title: Kanafeh or baklava with mint tea
foodToTry.description: Finish the day with a sweet and strong tea; many local cafes in Wadi Musa serve it late.

gettingAround.title: On foot inside Petra
gettingAround.description: Most routes are walking-only; download an offline map and start early so you can take breaks without rushing.

gettingAround.title: Official site transport options
gettingAround.description: Horses at the entrance and donkeys/camels deeper in are available but not required; only use if you’ve agreed on a full fare and route.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and hotel shuttles in Wadi Musa
gettingAround.description: Taxis are plentiful but meters aren’t always used—confirm the price before getting in; some hotels offer free drops to the gate.

topThingsToDo.title: Old City early walk (Jaffa Gate → Cardo → Western Wall)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive around opening time to avoid crowds and heat; enter via Jaffa Gate, follow the Cardo, and reach the Western Wall before tour groups stack up.

topThingsToDo.title: Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif visit (when open to non-Muslims)
topThingsToDo.description: Go first slot of the day with passport; dress modestly and expect security lines—check same-day opening windows as they change frequently.

topThingsToDo.title: Holy Sepulchre at quiet hours
topThingsToDo.description: For a calmer experience, go late afternoon near closing or during weekday mornings; enter from Christian Quarter and circle counterclockwise to avoid bottlenecks.

topThingsToDo.title: Mahane Yehuda Market like a local
topThingsToDo.description: Shop mornings for produce/spices, then return at night for bars; use the side alleys (e.g., Etz Hayim) for better prices and less tourist push.

topThingsToDo.title: Mount of Olives sunrise + Garden of Gethsemane
topThingsToDo.description: Take a taxi early to the viewpoint for the classic skyline, then walk downhill through the Jewish cemetery path to Gethsemane before day-trippers arrive.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘This way is closed’ detours in the Old City
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore unsolicited guides claiming gates/streets are closed and trying to lead you to a shop; follow official signs or use offline maps.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi ‘no meter’ or inflated fixed prices
scamsToAvoid.description: Insist on the meter (“moneh”) or agree on a price before entering; avoid taxis waiting right at major tourist exits when possible.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘authentic’ goods in tourist souks
scamsToAvoid.description: If a shopkeeper says a price is “special today,” it’s usually not—compare across 2–3 stalls and be ready to walk away.

localTips.title: Plan around Shabbat and holidays
localTips.description: From Friday afternoon to Saturday night, many businesses close and public transport slows or stops; stock snacks/water and pre-book rides if needed.

localTips.title: Dress code varies by neighborhood
localTips.description: In ultra-Orthodox areas (e.g., Mea She’arim), wear covered shoulders/knees and avoid taking photos to prevent confrontations.

localTips.title: Old City navigation hack
localTips.description: Pin your entry gate (Jaffa/Damascus/Zion) and your exit before you wander; GPS drifts in alleys, so rely on landmarks and quarter signs.

localTips.title: Security checks are normal
localTips.description: Carry an ID/passport copy and keep bags simple; museums and the light rail often have quick bag checks that move faster with fewer items.

foodToTry.title: Jerusalem mixed grill (me’orav yerushalmi)
foodToTry.description: Best fresh off the plancha in the Machane Yehuda area; ask for it in a pita with tahini, pickles, and amba.

foodToTry.title: Knafeh in the Muslim Quarter
foodToTry.description: Go mid-morning for a hot tray; ask for a small portion—it’s rich and very sweet.

foodToTry.title: Sabich
foodToTry.description: Order with extra amba and chopped salad; it’s a filling vegetarian option that’s quick and cheap.

foodToTry.title: Malabi or tahini halva
foodToTry.description: Grab malabi from a market stall after lunch, or buy halva by weight—ask to taste before choosing flavors.

gettingAround.title: Light Rail (Rakevet Kala)
gettingAround.description: Fastest way between the Central Bus Station area and the Old City edge (get off at City Hall/Jaffa Center); validate tickets and expect spot checks.

gettingAround.title: Buses + Rav-Kav card
gettingAround.description: Buy/charge a Rav-Kav at stations or kiosks for buses and the light rail; many lines stop earlier on Fridays, so check last departures.

gettingAround.title: Walking + short taxis for hills
gettingAround.description: The center and Old City are walkable but steep; use taxis for uphill hops (e.g., Old City to Mount of Olives) and confirm meter before moving.

topThingsToDo.title: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque (early morning)
topThingsToDo.description: Go right after opening for cooler temps and fewer tour groups; bring a scarf and long sleeves/trousers (abayas available to borrow/rent near the entrance).

topThingsToDo.title: Mutrah Corniche + Souq at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the waterfront before sunset, then enter the souq for frankincense and silver; start bargaining at ~40–50% of the first price and pay in OMR cash.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Muscat: Al Alam Palace + forts viewpoint
topThingsToDo.description: Skip midday heat and go late afternoon; the best photos are from the road between Al Mirani and Al Jalali forts and the small lookout points nearby.

topThingsToDo.title: Wadi Shab or Wadi Tiwi day trip (self-drive)
topThingsToDo.description: Leave Muscat by 7:00–7:30 to beat crowds; bring water shoes and a dry bag, and avoid swimming after heavy rain warnings.

topThingsToDo.title: Snorkel the Daymaniyat Islands (half-day boat)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose early departures for calmer seas and better visibility; confirm your operator includes permits and provides reef-safe guidance to avoid fines and coral damage.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxi pricing at tourist hotspots
scamsToAvoid.description: Many taxis quote inflated flat rates at the airport, Mutrah, and malls; agree the total price before getting in or use an app-based ride (e.g., Otaxi/Careem where available).

scamsToAvoid.title: Souq “antiques” and fake silver
scamsToAvoid.description: Items marketed as old Omani khanjars/coins are often replicas; buy from reputable silver shops and look for clear purity marks if you’re paying a premium.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tour add-ons and surprise fees
scamsToAvoid.description: Some operators upsell “permits,” snorkel gear, or extra stops after pickup; ask for a written inclusions list (transport, entry fees, permits, gear) before paying.

localTips.title: Dress codes are stricter than you expect
localTips.description: In mosques and government areas, cover shoulders and knees (women cover hair in mosques); keep a light scarf in your day bag.

localTips.title: Friday timing changes the city
localTips.description: Friday mornings are quiet and many places open later; plan beaches/wadis early and do malls/souq after mid-afternoon.

localTips.title: Best beach swims are early or after 4 pm
localTips.description: Heat and glare are intense midday; Qurum Beach and Al Bustan are most pleasant at sunrise/sunset and you’ll see locals picnicking then.

localTips.title: Cash helps in souqs and small eateries
localTips.description: Cards are common in hotels and malls, but small shops may prefer cash; ATMs are everywhere, and small OMR notes make bargaining easier.

foodToTry.title: Shuwa
foodToTry.description: Slow-cooked, banana-leaf wrapped meat often served on weekends and holidays; ask Omani restaurants for the day it’s available and reserve early.

foodToTry.title: Majboos (machboos)
foodToTry.description: Spiced rice with chicken or fish; try it with Omani dates and kahwa (cardamom coffee) as locals do.

foodToTry.title: Mishkak
foodToTry.description: Charcoal-grilled meat skewers sold at street stalls; go in the evening near Mutrah/Ruwi and ask for extra lime and chili.

foodToTry.title: Halwa Omani + kahwa
foodToTry.description: Sticky saffron-rose dessert served warm; buy small portions from reputable sweet shops and pair with bitter coffee to balance sweetness.

gettingAround.title: Use ride-hailing for predictable fares
gettingAround.description: Apps (Otaxi/Careem where available) reduce haggling and show pricing upfront; keep a local SIM or hotel Wi‑Fi for pickups.

gettingAround.title: Renting a car is easiest for beaches and wadis
gettingAround.description: Muscat is spread out and sidewalks are limited; choose a car with good AC, keep fuel above half for longer drives, and watch speed cameras.

gettingAround.title: Public buses work on main corridors but are slow
gettingAround.description: Mwasalat buses connect key areas (airport, Ruwi, Mutrah) but schedules can be sparse; use them for daytime point-to-point trips, not tight itineraries.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset walk on the Brooklyn Bridge + DUMBO
topThingsToDo.description: Enter from Brooklyn (York St/Jay St) to avoid crowds, then catch the Manhattan skyline from Washington St & Water St and Brooklyn Bridge Park’s Pier 1.

topThingsToDo.title: Central Park loop with key stops
topThingsToDo.description: Start at 72nd St, hit Bethesda Terrace, The Mall, and Bow Bridge; go early for fewer bikes and better photos, then exit near 59th St for Fifth Ave.

topThingsToDo.title: The High Line to Hudson Yards (or reverse)
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday morning; enter at Gansevoort St and finish at 34th St, grabbing a quick bite at Chelsea Market right off the trail.

topThingsToDo.title: Ferry to Statue of Liberty views (cheap hack)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the Staten Island Ferry (free) for close-up harbor views; sit on the right side outbound and left side returning for best skyline angles.

topThingsToDo.title: Museum + neighborhood pairing
topThingsToDo.description: Pick one major museum (Met or MoMA) and pair it with nearby wandering—Upper East Side after the Met, or Midtown/HELL’S Kitchen after MoMA—to avoid museum fatigue.

scamsToAvoid.title: CD/bracelet/photo hustles in Times Sq and parks
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t take anything handed to you; a quick “no thanks” and keep walking prevents pressure for cash.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed “gypsy” cabs and fake ride offers
scamsToAvoid.description: Only use yellow/green taxis, official taxi stands, or rideshare apps; ignore anyone offering a ride inside airports or busy areas.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced pedicabs and surprise fees
scamsToAvoid.description: If you ride, get the total price in writing (not per minute/block) before sitting down; otherwise skip—they’re rarely worth it.

localTips.title: Use the right subway entrance and exit
localTips.description: Stations can be huge and directional; match the uptown/downtown sign and use the correct exit to save 10+ minutes and avoid backtracking.

localTips.title: Rush hour strategy
localTips.description: Avoid moving between 4–6:30 pm if you can; if you must, stand to the side on platforms and let riders off before boarding.

localTips.title: Bathrooms and water without hassle
localTips.description: Use hotel lobbies, major museums, or large chain coffee shops; refill water in parks (seasonal fountains) or at museum fountains after security.

localTips.title: Skip the worst crowds without losing the view
localTips.description: For skyline photos, choose Top of the Rock at night or One World Observatory near sunset on weekdays; book timed tickets to avoid long lines.

foodToTry.title: NY slice (thin, foldable pizza)
foodToTry.description: Order a plain slice first to judge the spot; eat it standing at the counter—most classic slice shops have limited seating.

foodToTry.title: Bagel with lox and schmear
foodToTry.description: Go early for fresh batches; ask for it “scooped” only if you really want less bread—locals often prefer full bagels.

foodToTry.title: Halal cart chicken over rice
foodToTry.description: Look for a cart with a steady line and quick turnover; ask for white sauce on the side if you don’t want it drenched.

foodToTry.title: Jewish deli pastrami on rye
foodToTry.description: Split a sandwich—portions are huge; go off-peak to avoid long waits and higher stress ordering.

gettingAround.title: Subway with tap-to-pay
gettingAround.description: Use OMNY by tapping a contactless card/phone at the turnstile; it’s fastest and avoids MetroCard lines.

gettingAround.title: NYC Ferry for views and less stress
gettingAround.description: Great for East River neighborhoods (DUMBO, Williamsburg, LIC); buy tickets in the NYC Ferry app and arrive 10 minutes early for popular routes.

gettingAround.title: Walking smart in Manhattan
gettingAround.description: Use avenues for north-south and streets for east-west; crosstown buses are slow, so walk 10–15 blocks when feasible to beat traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Griffith Observatory + Sunset Hike
topThingsToDo.description: Go 60–90 minutes before sunset for golden-hour views; hike up via the West Observatory Trail for an easy, scenic climb and skip parking stress.

topThingsToDo.title: The Getty Center (Art + Views)
topThingsToDo.description: Entry is free—reserve a timed ticket online; arrive right at opening for quiet galleries and clear city views before haze builds.

topThingsToDo.title: Santa Monica to Venice by Bike
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike near the Santa Monica Pier and ride the beach path; go before 10am for smoother lanes and fewer crowds at Venice Boardwalk.

topThingsToDo.title: DTLA: Grand Central Market + The Broad
topThingsToDo.description: Pair a quick food crawl at Grand Central Market with The Broad (reserve ahead); use Angels Flight or walk to avoid DTLA parking hassles.

topThingsToDo.title: Malibu: Point Dume + Seafood Stop
topThingsToDo.description: Hit Point Dume early for ocean views and tidepool vibes, then grab casual seafood at Malibu Farm Pier Cafe or nearby fish tacos—weekends book fast.

scamsToAvoid.title: Hollywood Blvd “Free” CD/Photo Hustles
scamsToAvoid.description: Street promoters may pressure you for cash after handing you something or posing; don’t accept items, and keep walking without engaging.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial Parking Attendants
scamsToAvoid.description: In busy areas, random people may direct you to “paid” curb spots; only pay at posted meters/official lots and check signs carefully.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced Tour Tickets on the Sidewalk
scamsToAvoid.description: Vendors push last-minute “celebrity” tours with vague routes; book directly with established operators and confirm pickup location and refund terms.

localTips.title: Pick Neighborhoods, Not a Citywide Checklist
localTips.description: LA is sprawling—plan 1–2 adjacent areas per day (e.g., Santa Monica/Venice or DTLA/Chinatown) to avoid spending hours in traffic.

localTips.title: Time Your Drives
localTips.description: Aim for drives between 10am–2pm or after 7:30pm; crossing the city during rush hour can double your ETA.

localTips.title: Beach Mornings Beat Beach Afternoons
localTips.description: For clearer skies and easier parking, go early; afternoons can bring marine layer “June Gloom” and heavy congestion.

localTips.title: Parking Signs Are a Puzzle
localTips.description: Read every line on the pole (street cleaning, permits, tow-away hours); when unsure, use a paid lot to avoid expensive tickets.

foodToTry.title: Street Tacos (Al Pastor + Asada)
foodToTry.description: Look for busy evening taco stands (often near major intersections); order al pastor from the spit with pineapple and ask for salsa on the side.

foodToTry.title: Korean BBQ in Koreatown
foodToTry.description: Go late-night for shorter waits; choose a spot with charcoal grills if you can, and add soju cocktails or cold buckwheat noodles.

foodToTry.title: Japanese Ramen or Tsukemen (Sawtelle or Little Tokyo)
foodToTry.description: Weeknights are best; for richer flavor, try tsukemen (dipping noodles) and be ready to line up at popular shops.

foodToTry.title: California-Style Burrito or Breakfast Burrito
foodToTry.description: Grab a breakfast burrito from a local Mexican spot or diner; ask for the salsa that locals use (often a separate, spicier option).

gettingAround.title: Rent a Car—But Park Strategically
gettingAround.description: A car saves time for beach-to-hills itineraries; use paid lots near hotspots and budget for $10–$40/day parking depending on area.

gettingAround.title: Metro for Specific Corridors
gettingAround.description: Use the B/D Lines for DTLA/Hollywood and the E Line for Santa Monica/DTLA; it’s often faster than driving for those routes.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare for Night Out + One-Way Trips
gettingAround.description: Great for bar nights and airport-to-hotel legs; check pickup pins carefully in crowded zones like Hollywood and around large venues.

topThingsToDo.title: River Architecture Cruise (even in cool weather)
topThingsToDo.description: Book an architecture cruise on the Chicago River for the best skyline/architecture context; sit on the outside edge for photos and bring a layer—the wind cuts hard.

topThingsToDo.title: Millennium Park + Art Institute combo
topThingsToDo.description: See Cloud Gate early (before 9am) for fewer crowds, then walk 10 minutes to the Art Institute; don’t miss the Modern Wing and the Thorne Miniature Rooms.

topThingsToDo.title: Lakefront Trail by bike
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a Divvy and ride the Lakefront Trail from Navy Pier to North Avenue Beach (or farther to Belmont); stick to the right and watch for fast cyclists.

topThingsToDo.title: Neighborhood food crawl (West Loop or Pilsen)
topThingsToDo.description: Skip downtown-only dining: do Fulton Market/West Loop for hotspots and cocktails, or Pilsen for murals and Mexican spots; go on a weekday to avoid long waits.

topThingsToDo.title: 360 Chicago or Willis Tower at off-peak
topThingsToDo.description: Go near opening or 1–2 hours before close for shorter lines; 360 has great north views, while Willis gives the classic downtown grid and Skydeck.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street performers pressuring for big tips
scamsToAvoid.description: Around tourist hubs, some acts aggressively solicit cash after photos; decide your tip upfront and keep walking if you’re not stopping.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake ticket/QR sellers near attractions
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid anyone selling “skip-the-line” tickets outside museums/boats; buy directly from official sites or the venue box office.

scamsToAvoid.title: Card skimmers at off-brand ATMs
scamsToAvoid.description: Use bank ATMs (inside branches) instead of sidewalk kiosks, especially near nightlife areas; tap-to-pay reduces risk.

localTips.title: Weather whiplash is real
localTips.description: Carry a light waterproof shell year-round and add layers; lake wind makes it feel 10–15°F colder on the water and bridges.

localTips.title: Museum deal strategy
localTips.description: CityPASS can pay off if you’re doing multiple big sights, but compare to individual tickets; some museums have free Illinois days (not for most visitors).

localTips.title: Do the Riverwalk, but pick the right stretch
localTips.description: For the best vibe, start near the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Plaza and head west toward Wolf Point; it’s less crowded than the Wabash-to-Michigan section.

localTips.title: Nightlife logistics
localTips.description: If you’re out late in River North/West Loop, pre-plan your ride home (CTA timing drops); rideshare pickup is easier one block off the main drag.

foodToTry.title: Italian beef (hot or dipped)
foodToTry.description: Order it “hot, dipped” if you like spice and mess; ask for sweet peppers if you want flavor without heat.

foodToTry.title: Tavern-style thin-crust pizza
foodToTry.description: Locals often choose square-cut thin crust over deep dish; it’s crisp, shareable, and easier for a quick meal.

foodToTry.title: Chicago-style hot dog
foodToTry.description: Get it “dragged through the garden” (no ketchup); it’s a quick, cheap classic near parks and ballgames.

foodToTry.title: Jibarito or Puerto Rican staples
foodToTry.description: Try a jibarito (fried plantains instead of bread) in Humboldt Park/West Town; pair with arroz con gandules or pernil.

gettingAround.title: CTA trains and buses with Ventra
gettingAround.description: Use a Ventra card or contactless tap; the Blue Line is the most reliable airport link (O’Hare) and runs 24/7.

gettingAround.title: Walking + river bridges
gettingAround.description: Downtown is very walkable, but bridges get windy and can bottleneck at rush times; give yourself extra time crossing the river near Michigan Ave.

gettingAround.title: Divvy bikes for the lakefront and short hops
gettingAround.description: Divvy is fastest for flat, short trips and the Lakefront Trail; check the app for dock availability before committing to a one-way ride.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise walk + Art Deco in South Beach
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (7–9am) to Ocean Drive/Collins for cooler temps and fewer crowds; book an Art Deco walking tour from the Welcome Center for the best context.

topThingsToDo.title: Wynwood Walls + nearby galleries (weekday late afternoon)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive around 4–6pm for softer light and smaller lines; wander NW 2nd Ave side streets for free murals beyond the ticketed walls.

topThingsToDo.title: Little Havana evening: Calle Ocho, dominoes, live music
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Máximo Gómez Park (domino park), grab a cafecito window stop, then follow live music spots along SW 8th St after 6pm.

topThingsToDo.title: Biscayne Bay boat day (better value from Bayfront/Marina)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose smaller-group skyline/sandbar trips and confirm what’s included (fees, tips, drinks); weekday departures are calmer and often cheaper.

topThingsToDo.title: Key Biscayne: beach + lighthouse at Bill Baggs Cape Florida
topThingsToDo.description: Rent bikes or bring a picnic; climb the lighthouse for the best views and go on weekdays to avoid bridge traffic and full parking lots.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced South Beach parking/tow traps
scamsToAvoid.description: Only use metered city spots or reputable garages; avoid lots with unclear rates and take photos of signs since towing is fast and expensive.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street promoters selling “VIP” club/boat deals
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t pay cash to random promoters; book directly with the venue/operator and confirm taxes, service charges, and exact pickup location in writing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Inflated taxi fares from airports/cruise port
scamsToAvoid.description: Use rideshare with upfront pricing or licensed taxis with the meter/flat-rate rules; confirm the total before getting in, especially at the port.

localTips.title: Time your beach for comfort
localTips.description: Midday sun is brutal most of the year—go early or after 4pm, and bring shade because umbrellas/rentals add up quickly.

localTips.title: Expect sudden rain and dress for humidity
localTips.description: Carry a compact poncho and wear quick-dry shoes; indoor AC is cold, so a light layer helps in museums/restaurants.

localTips.title: Plan around traffic chokepoints
localTips.description: Avoid driving to Miami Beach 4–7pm and weekend afternoons; if you must, use the MacArthur Causeway and budget extra time for parking.

localTips.title: Waterfront views without the premium
localTips.description: For free skyline sunset spots, try South Pointe Park, Maurice A. Ferré Park, or the Brickell Key loop—bring your own drinks/snacks.

foodToTry.title: Cuban cafecito + pastelito
foodToTry.description: Order at a ventanita (walk-up window); try a guava-and-cheese pastelito with a sweet espresso shot.

foodToTry.title: Croquetas (ham or chicken)
foodToTry.description: Best as a quick snack—ask for them hot and crispy, and pair with a cortadito.

foodToTry.title: Stone crab (seasonal) or fresh seafood
foodToTry.description: Stone crab is typically in season roughly Oct–May; otherwise go for local fish like mahi or snapper and confirm it’s not “market price” surprise.

foodToTry.title: Key lime pie
foodToTry.description: Look for tart, not overly sweet, and try it after a beach day; many spots sell slices to-go for a quick dessert.

gettingAround.title: Use Metrorail + Metromover for Downtown/Brickell
gettingAround.description: Metromover is free and easiest for Brickell/Downtown loops; pair with Metrorail from the airport to avoid pricey traffic.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare smartly (and avoid surge)
gettingAround.description: Walk 1–2 blocks off busy corridors like Ocean Drive to reduce pickups and pricing; check both apps and lock in the quoted fare.

gettingAround.title: Beach logistics: walk, bike, or trolley
gettingAround.description: Miami Beach is compact—use bikes and the free trolley routes; driving is rarely worth it once you’re on the island.

topThingsToDo.title: Golden Gate Bridge: walk one way, return differently
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Crissy Field/East Vista Point, walk to the first tower, then return via the Presidio’s Batteries to Bluffs trail for big views without the wind tunnel.

topThingsToDo.title: Alcatraz night tour
topThingsToDo.description: Book 2–4 weeks ahead; the night tour has fewer kids and better audio-tour atmosphere. Take the earliest ferry you can for calmer water and more time on the island.

topThingsToDo.title: Ferry Building + Embarcadero stroll
topThingsToDo.description: Go on weekday mornings for shorter lines; grab coffee and walk north to Pier 14 for skyline photos without the crowds at Pier 39.

topThingsToDo.title: North Beach + Coit Tower via Filbert Steps
topThingsToDo.description: Climb the Filbert Steps through the gardens to Coit Tower; go late afternoon for softer light and then drop into North Beach for an easy dinner.

topThingsToDo.title: Lands End to Sutro Baths at sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Lands End Lookout, walk the coastal trail to Sutro Baths, and bring a wind layer; it’s one of the best free viewpoints in the city.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street “gold” jewelry swap
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone offers a ring/chain as “thanks” or tries to sell it cheap, walk away; it’s typically fake and designed to pressure you.

scamsToAvoid.title: Counterfeit event tickets near venues
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid buying paper tickets from sidewalk sellers around Chase Center/Oracle Park; use official resale apps with verified transfer.

scamsToAvoid.title: Car break-in bait in tourist lots
scamsToAvoid.description: Smash-and-grab crews target visible luggage at overlooks (Twin Peaks, Palace of Fine Arts); don’t leave anything in the car, even in the trunk after you park.

localTips.title: Dress for microclimates
localTips.description: It can be 15–20°F colder and windier by the ocean than downtown; carry a light puffer or windbreaker year-round.

localTips.title: Skip Pier 39 for better waterfront
localTips.description: For fewer crowds and better views, walk Crissy Field, Marina Green, or Pier 14 instead; you’ll still get postcard scenery.

localTips.title: Plan hills and transit like a local
localTips.description: Use buses/ride share to climb steep neighborhoods (Nob Hill, Twin Peaks) and walk downhill; it saves time and your legs.

localTips.title: Reservations and timing matter
localTips.description: Popular restaurants book out; aim for early weeknights or late lunches, and check last seating times—many kitchens close earlier than visitors expect.

foodToTry.title: Mission burrito
foodToTry.description: Order it “super” if you want it fully loaded; many locals prefer it without rice for a less soggy wrap.

foodToTry.title: Dungeness crab (seasonal)
foodToTry.description: Best in-season (often winter); go for simple cracked crab with sourdough—skip overpriced tourist combos.

foodToTry.title: Sourdough bread
foodToTry.description: Buy a fresh loaf and eat it the same day; it’s at its peak crunchy-chewy in the first few hours.

foodToTry.title: Chinese dim sum in Richmond or Sunset
foodToTry.description: Head west for better value and fewer lines than Chinatown; go before 11am for the freshest trays.

gettingAround.title: Use Clipper for almost everything
gettingAround.description: A Clipper card/app works on Muni, BART, and ferries; add it to your phone to tap-and-go without ticket machines.

gettingAround.title: Muni is best for neighborhoods; BART is best for airport/East Bay
gettingAround.description: Use Muni buses/Metro for getting around the city and BART mainly for SFO, Oakland, and Berkeley; they serve different corridors.

gettingAround.title: If driving, plan for parking and break-ins
gettingAround.description: Street parking rules are strict and tickets are common; choose monitored garages and never leave items visible in the car.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Strip strategically (Bellagio to Venetian at night)
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Bellagio fountains after dark, cut through connected casinos (Bellagio–Cosmo–Aria) to avoid heat, then end at Venetian/Palazzo for canals and indoor vibe.

topThingsToDo.title: See a top production show (book with seat strategy)
topThingsToDo.description: For Cirque-style shows, sit mid-center (not too close) for best sightlines; buy weekday performances and check same-day box office for last-minute drops.

topThingsToDo.title: Fremont Street + Downtown bars
topThingsToDo.description: Go around 8–11pm for the canopy light shows; pop into Container Park and nearby cocktail spots, then leave before late-night crowds if you want a calmer scene.

topThingsToDo.title: Red Rock Canyon scenic drive + short hike
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve a timed entry in peak season and arrive early; do Calico Tanks or Ice Box Canyon for big views without an all-day trek.

topThingsToDo.title: Neon Museum at dusk (photo-friendly)
topThingsToDo.description: Book the evening slot for the best lighting and fewer harsh shadows; pair it with a quick stop at the Arts District for breweries and murals.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street performers and costumed characters shakedowns
scamsToAvoid.description: If you take a photo, they may demand $20–$40 per person; agree on a price before any photo or keep walking and don’t engage.

scamsToAvoid.title: Club promoter ‘free entry’ bait-and-switch
scamsToAvoid.description: Free guest lists often mean long waits or hidden minimums; confirm cover, arrival cutoff time, and drink/table requirements in writing (text).

scamsToAvoid.title: Timeshare “free tickets” booths
scamsToAvoid.description: Those “2 free show tickets” usually require a 2–3 hour presentation; skip unless you’re genuinely shopping for a timeshare and value your time.

localTips.title: Resort fees and parking add up fast
localTips.description: Compare total price (room + resort fee + taxes + parking) before booking; some properties offer free self-parking to hotel guests only.

localTips.title: Use indoor routes to save time and energy
localTips.description: The Strip looks close but isn’t—use casino corridors and pedestrian bridges, and plan stops by cluster (Center Strip, Venetian/Wynn, MGM area).

localTips.title: Hydrate like it’s a plan, not a suggestion
localTips.description: Buy a big water at CVS/Walgreens on the Strip and refill; desert air plus alcohol dehydrates quickly even in winter.

localTips.title: Happy hours and late-night dining are where value lives
localTips.description: Check casino bar happy hours and off-Strip Chinatown deals; many kitchens serve strong late-night menus without nightclub pricing.

foodToTry.title: Tacos in Chinatown (Spring Mountain Rd)
foodToTry.description: Head off-Strip for better prices and real variety; go early on weekends to beat lines at popular taquerias.

foodToTry.title: Vegas-style buffets (go for brunch)
foodToTry.description: Brunch pricing often includes breakfast + lunch items; book ahead and arrive right at opening to avoid the longest waits.

foodToTry.title: Steakhouse with a classic Vegas room
foodToTry.description: Look for old-school spots in longtime resorts for the vibe; ask for a booth and split sides—they’re usually huge.

foodToTry.title: Late-night noodles/ramen
foodToTry.description: Chinatown late-night ramen and hand-pulled noodles can be faster and cheaper than Strip options after shows.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare pickup zones (don’t guess)
gettingAround.description: Each resort has a specific Uber/Lyft location that can be a 5–10 minute walk; follow in-app directions and set the pickup before you start walking.

gettingAround.title: Use the Monorail for long Strip jumps
gettingAround.description: It’s best for moving between MGM Grand and Sahara quickly; it’s not ideal for west-side resorts, so combine with short walks through casinos.

gettingAround.title: Deuce/SDX-style bus on the Strip (budget but slow)
gettingAround.description: Good for one-direction sightseeing if you’re not rushed; avoid it right after major events when lines spike.

topThingsToDo.title: Frenchmen Street live music (not Bourbon)
topThingsToDo.description: Go after 9pm for packed sets; wander between clubs and tip the band. Arrive early for smaller rooms like d.b.a. and Spotted Cat—lines form fast on weekends.

topThingsToDo.title: Garden District walk + Lafayette Cemetery No. 1 area
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll Magazine Street to Prytania for historic homes; pair it with coffee and a slow loop through nearby streets. Cemetery access can be restricted, so check day-of and consider a small-group tour if closed.

topThingsToDo.title: Ride the St. Charles streetcar at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Use the Canal-to-Carrollton line for a scenic, cheap ride; sit on the right side heading uptown for mansion views. Bring exact fare or use the Le Pass app to avoid delays.

topThingsToDo.title: Creole history in Tremé + Congo Square
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Congo Square in Louis Armstrong Park, then walk to Tremé for culture-focused museums and second-line history. Go daytime and book a guided tour for context you won’t get from plaques.

topThingsToDo.title: Bayou or swamp trip close to the city
topThingsToDo.description: Choose smaller boats for quieter wildlife viewing and less touristy stops. Morning tours are cooler and usually have better animal activity.

scamsToAvoid.title: "I bet I know where you got your shoes" hustle
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore and keep walking—engaging is the trick to getting cornered for cash. Don’t argue or explain; a firm “no thanks” works best.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial street parking/boot threats
scamsToAvoid.description: Only pay meters/apps you initiate; don’t hand cash to anyone claiming to “watch your car.” If someone mentions towing, verify signage and call 311/non-emergency if harassed.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced pedicabs and unmetered rides
scamsToAvoid.description: Pedicabs must show rates—confirm total price before you sit down. For rideshare/taxis, use the app or ensure the meter is on; don’t accept a vague flat rate.

localTips.title: Skip Bourbon for drinks, use it for a quick pass-through
localTips.description: Grab one photo, then pivot to Frenchmen, Chartres, or Magazine for better bars and fewer headaches. If you do Bourbon, go early evening—not after midnight.

localTips.title: Weather is the boss: plan shade, rain, and AC breaks
localTips.description: In summer, do outdoor sights before 11am and after 4pm, and schedule a museum or long lunch mid-day. Carry a compact poncho—storms pop up fast.

localTips.title: Second lines and parades: follow the brass, not the crowd
localTips.description: If you hear a band, step aside and let the parade flow, then join behind the rope line. Don’t block sidewalks or doorways; locals take routes seriously.

localTips.title: Cash helps, but don’t flash it
localTips.description: Many bars are quick-cash for tips and cover, yet keep bills separated and pay fast. Use hotel ATMs or bank branches, not random corner machines with high fees.

foodToTry.title: Gumbo (know what you’re ordering)
foodToTry.description: Order seafood gumbo on Friday for tradition, or chicken-and-andouille for a richer, smokier bowl. Ask if it’s roux-based and how spicy it runs—recipes vary wildly.

foodToTry.title: Po’boy (dress it right)
foodToTry.description: Try fried shrimp or oyster on Leidenheimer bread and order it “dressed” (lettuce, tomato, pickle, mayo). For less wait, go mid-afternoon when lunch crowds fade.

foodToTry.title: Chargrilled oysters
foodToTry.description: Get them hot off the grill and eat immediately—best texture and flavor. If you’re sharing, order a half-dozen first; they’re rich and add up fast.

foodToTry.title: Beignets beyond the hype
foodToTry.description: Eat them fresh and piping hot; if they’re lukewarm, ask for a new batch. Bring wet wipes or step outside first—powdered sugar gets everywhere.

gettingAround.title: Streetcars and buses (Le Pass app)
gettingAround.description: Buy day passes in the Le Pass app to avoid fumbling with cash; service can be slow, so build buffer time. Use streetcars for scenery, not strict schedules.

gettingAround.title: Walking smart in the Quarter/Marigny
gettingAround.description: Most key spots are walkable—use well-lit main streets like Decatur, Chartres, Royal, and Frenchmen late at night. Cut through quiet blocks only in groups.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare/taxis for late nights and bad weather
gettingAround.description: Surge pricing spikes after shows and on weekends—walk a few blocks away from Frenchmen/Bourbon before requesting. Confirm your pickup pin; streets can be blocked by events.

topThingsToDo.title: Snorkel or dive the Underwater Museum (MUSA)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a morning snorkel from Puerto Cancún or Aquaworld for calmer water; bring reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard.

topThingsToDo.title: Isla Mujeres day trip (Playa Norte + golf cart loop)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the early ferry from Ultramar (Puerto Juárez) to beat crowds, then rent a golf cart for 2–4 hours to circle Punta Sur.

topThingsToDo.title: Cenotes near Puerto Morelos or Ruta de los Cenotes
topThingsToDo.description: Go with a small-group driver to hit 2–3 cenotes (e.g., Verde Lucero, La Noria); bring water shoes and cash for lockers.

topThingsToDo.title: Chichén Itzá with a timing hack
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening (or go late afternoon) and pair it with a nearby cenote (Ik Kil is busy; ask for alternatives like Yokdzonot).

topThingsToDo.title: Laguna Nichupté sunset boat ride
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a smaller boat/kayak tour from the Hotel Zone for mangroves and wildlife; sunset slots sell out 1–2 days ahead.

scamsToAvoid.title: Airport timeshare “welcome” desks
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone offering free transport, vouchers, or “tourist tax” help after customs; go straight outside to your pre-booked pickup.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi price switching in the Hotel Zone
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm the total fare before getting in and have it written in your phone; better yet use ADO bus or authorized transfers at night.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bar/club overcharges and forced tips
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask for a printed menu with prices, check the bill line-by-line, and avoid handing your card away; pay cash per round if unsure.

localTips.title: Use ADO to skip pricey airport transfers
localTips.description: ADO buses run from the airport to downtown Cancún and Playa del Carmen; buy tickets at the official counter and keep small bills.

localTips.title: Best beaches depend on wind direction
localTips.description: When it’s windy on the Caribbean side, go to calmer Playa Langosta/Las Perlas (north Hotel Zone) or take the ferry to Isla Mujeres.

localTips.title: Sargassum strategy
localTips.description: Check daily sargassum reports and choose beaches with active cleanup (often central Hotel Zone); snorkeling is clearer on Isla Mujeres days.

localTips.title: Withdraw cash at bank ATMs, not convenience stores
localTips.description: Use ATMs inside banks or supermarkets (Chedraui/Soriana) for better fees and safety; decline dynamic currency conversion in pesos.

foodToTry.title: Tacos al pastor (with piña)
foodToTry.description: Order 3–4 and add salsa gradually; look for high-turnover taquerías in downtown (Centro) for freshest meat.

foodToTry.title: Cochinita pibil
foodToTry.description: Try it in tortas or tacos with pickled red onion and habanero; best earlier in the day when it’s just been carved.

foodToTry.title: Ceviche and aguachile
foodToTry.description: Choose busy marisquerías and ask what’s freshest; pair with a michelada and request “poco picante” if sensitive.

foodToTry.title: Marquesitas
foodToTry.description: Grab this crunchy street crepe at night (often parks/plazas); classic filling is Edam cheese with Nutella or cajeta.

gettingAround.title: Hotel Zone buses (R1/R2)
gettingAround.description: Cheap and frequent along Blvd. Kukulcán; pay cash, tell the driver your stop, and keep coins/small bills ready.

gettingAround.title: ADO for intercity trips
gettingAround.description: Use ADO from downtown terminal for Playa del Carmen, Tulum, and Mérida; choose “Primera Clase” for AC and assigned seats.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and transfers
gettingAround.description: For late nights or groups, pre-book an authorized transfer or agree on the fare before riding; avoid hailing outside clubs where rates spike.

topThingsToDo.title: Teotihuacan at sunrise (or late afternoon)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early to beat crowds and heat; book a direct transport tour that skips “artisan shop” stops. Pack water and a hat—there’s little shade on the Avenue of the Dead.

topThingsToDo.title: Chapultepec Park + Anthropology Museum combo
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Museo Nacional de Antropología when it opens, then walk to Chapultepec Castle for skyline views. Aim for weekdays to avoid long entry lines.

topThingsToDo.title: Historic Center walk: Zócalo to Bellas Artes via Madero
topThingsToDo.description: Go in daylight and pop into Palacio de Correos for architecture photos; keep your phone secured on busy pedestrian streets. Time it for golden hour at Torre Latino’s mirador.

topThingsToDo.title: Xochimilco in the morning (less party, more nature)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose Embarcadero Cuemanco for calmer canals and fewer aggressive sellers. Agree on total price and duration before boarding and pay at the official ticket window.

topThingsToDo.title: Coyoacán + Frida Kahlo Museum (with a plan)
topThingsToDo.description: Buy timed tickets online in advance; same-day entry often sells out. Pair it with Mercado de Coyoacán snacks and a short walk to Jardín Centenario.

scamsToAvoid.title: Airport taxi/tour “helpers”
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore unsolicited offers inside the terminal; use authorized taxi counters or app-based rides from the official pickup area. Confirm the car plate and driver before getting in.

scamsToAvoid.title: Restaurant/menu swap and inflated bills
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask for a printed menu with prices before ordering and check the bill for added items or “service” you didn’t agree to. Pay by card when possible and keep your card in sight.

scamsToAvoid.title: Xochimilco price games
scamsToAvoid.description: Some boatmen quote per person instead of per boat or extend time without consent; get the rate, route, and end time clearly agreed. Buy tickets only at official booths, not from people in the walkway.

localTips.title: Pick the right neighborhoods to base yourself
localTips.description: For walkability and food: Roma Norte/Condesa; for museums and calm: Polanco/San Miguel Chapultepec; for budget and central: Centro (choose a well-reviewed hotel). Nightlife is louder in Roma/Condesa—ask for a quiet room.

localTips.title: Altitude + air quality can hit you
localTips.description: Take it easy the first day, hydrate, and limit heavy alcohol; headaches are common at 2,240m. If sensitive, plan big outdoor days after checking air quality (IMECA) and avoid rush-hour traffic corridors.

localTips.title: Street food: choose the busy stand, order like a local
localTips.description: Go where there’s a line and high turnover; ask for “con todo” only if you want salsa, onion, cilantro. Keep small cash and napkins—many stands don’t have change or tissues.

localTips.title: Safety in crowds: carry less, use pockets wisely
localTips.description: In the Metro and Centro, keep your phone away from train doors and your bag zipped in front. Use ATMs inside banks during daytime, not standalone street machines.

foodToTry.title: Tacos al pastor
foodToTry.description: Order 2–3 at a time so they arrive hot; try with pineapple and a bit of green salsa. Late-night stands in Roma/Condesa are reliable when busy.

foodToTry.title: Chilaquiles for breakfast
foodToTry.description: Ask for “crujientes” if you like them less soggy and choose red/green sauce based on spice tolerance. Add eggs or cecina for a filling start.

foodToTry.title: Barbacoa and consomé (weekend morning)
foodToTry.description: Look for weekend-only stalls; order a taco plus a small consomé to sip. If you see fresh handmade tortillas, it’s usually a good sign.

foodToTry.title: Churros + chocolate at a classic churrería
foodToTry.description: Get “rellenos” if you want filled churros, or plain for dipping; chocolate is thick, so share if you’re sampling more food. Go off-peak to avoid long lines.

gettingAround.title: Use Metro/Metrobús strategically
