gettingAround.description: Metrobús Line 1 is great for Reforma; avoid Metro rush hours for comfort and keep belongings close. Buy a rechargeable mobility card (Tarjeta de Movilidad Integrada) for multiple systems.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare for late nights and point-to-point trips
gettingAround.description: Uber/Didi are usually safer than hailing random street taxis; verify plate and driver name before entering. Add extra time—traffic is heavy even for short distances.

gettingAround.title: Walking + bikes in Roma/Condesa
gettingAround.description: These areas are best explored on foot; use Ecobici for short hops if you’re comfortable in traffic. Stick to well-lit streets at night and avoid flashing your phone at intersections.

topThingsToDo.title: San Telmo + Sunday Feria
topThingsToDo.description: Go late morning for antiques and street tango; eat at Mercado de San Telmo but keep your phone secured in crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Palermo parks + coffee-hopping
topThingsToDo.description: Walk Bosques de Palermo and the Rose Garden, then do cafés in Palermo Soho/Hollywood; reserve popular brunch spots on weekends.

topThingsToDo.title: Recoleta Cemetery + museums
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Recoleta Cemetery early to avoid tour groups, then pair it with Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes (free) a short walk away.

topThingsToDo.title: La Boca (Caminito) with timing
topThingsToDo.description: Go mid-day, stick to the main tourist streets, and leave before late afternoon; use a radio taxi/ride-hail to arrive and depart.

topThingsToDo.title: Tango without the tourist trap
topThingsToDo.description: Watch locals dance at milongas like La Catedral or Salón Canning; take a beginner class and go in shoes with smooth soles.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Bird poop/mustard” distraction
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone points out a stain and offers to help clean, refuse and walk away—accomplices often pickpocket during the distraction.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial money changers
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid street “cambio” offers; use reputable casas de cambio or arrange currency via trusted channels and count bills carefully.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip random street taxis at night; use ride-hailing or radio taxis and confirm the route before moving, especially from tourist areas.

localTips.title: Cash strategy
localTips.description: Carry small bills for kiosks and tips; many places accept cards, but cash is still useful for smaller restaurants and markets.

localTips.title: Late dining culture
localTips.description: Restaurants fill after 9:30–10:00 pm; book steakhouses for 10:00 pm to get better tables and a livelier atmosphere.

localTips.title: Stay neighborhoods-wise
localTips.description: Base in Palermo, Recoleta, or Villa Crespo for walkability and dining; treat Microcentro as daytime-only unless you know the area.

localTips.title: Safety habits that matter
localTips.description: Keep phones off tables on terraces, use a crossbody bag, and avoid flashing cameras near ATMs and train stations.

foodToTry.title: Parrilla (asado) + provoleta
foodToTry.description: Order bife de chorizo or vacío and start with provoleta; ask for “a punto” if you don’t want very rare steak.

foodToTry.title: Empanadas (salteña style)
foodToTry.description: Try carne cortada a cuchillo and humita; grab them from a neighborhood bakery for fresher batches than tourist strips.

foodToTry.title: Milanesa napolitana
foodToTry.description: A giant breaded cutlet topped with tomato, ham, and melted cheese; share one and pair it with a simple salad.

foodToTry.title: Helado artesanal
foodToTry.description: Go to a good heladería and try dulce de leche granizado or sambayón; Argentines often buy it by the kilo to take home.

gettingAround.title: SUBE card for transit
gettingAround.description: Buy a SUBE and load it at kiosks or stations; it works on subte, buses, and trains and is far cheaper than taxis.

gettingAround.title: Subte basics
gettingAround.description: The subway is fast for cross-city hops, but lines don’t cover everything; avoid rush-hour crush on weekdays if you can.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing and taxis
gettingAround.description: Use apps (or radio taxis) at night and for airport runs; double-check the pickup location and keep luggage in the trunk.

topThingsToDo.title: Christ the Redeemer (Corcovado) at off-peak hours
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (first trains) or late afternoon for cooler temps and fewer crowds; book official tickets in advance and avoid on-site “helpers” upselling.

topThingsToDo.title: Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar) for sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive 1.5–2 hours before sunset to clear both cable car legs without rushing; the second peak gets packed, so stake a spot early.

topThingsToDo.title: Pedra do Sal night samba in Saúde
topThingsToDo.description: Hit Monday or Friday roda de samba; go light on valuables, use ride-hailing both ways, and stick to the busy streets around the crowd.

topThingsToDo.title: Tijuca Forest: hike to Pedra Bonita or Vista Chinesa
topThingsToDo.description: Choose Pedra Bonita for a safer, shorter hike with hang-glider views; go with daylight and avoid empty trails—ask your hotel which routes are calm that week.

topThingsToDo.title: Beach day like a local (Ipanema/Leblon)
topThingsToDo.description: Pick a 'posto' (lifeguard station) to meet friends—Posto 9 is lively, Posto 12 calmer; pay vendors in small bills and keep your phone out of sight.

scamsToAvoid.title: Beach card-skimmer and overcharge
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid handing your card to roaming vendors; pay cash or use contactless you control, and confirm the amount on the screen before tapping.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial tour/taxi touts at attractions
scamsToAvoid.description: At Corcovado, Sugarloaf, and airports, ignore people offering “last tickets” or “special routes”; use official counters, apps, or prebooked transfers.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bar/club tab padding in Lapa
scamsToAvoid.description: Only open a tab at reputable spots and keep your comanda (paper card) with you; if you lose it, you may be charged a large fixed fee.

localTips.title: Use neighborhoods strategically
localTips.description: Stay in Ipanema/Leblon for walkability and beach safety, Botafogo for food and metro access, and Santa Teresa for charm—avoid wandering far from your base at night.

localTips.title: Time the city’s rhythm
localTips.description: Museums and outdoor sights are best before 11am; late afternoons bring traffic, and many areas empty after dark—plan door-to-door transport at night.

localTips.title: Blend in with a “street-ready” setup
localTips.description: Carry one card + small cash, keep phone in a front pocket or pouch, and leave flashy jewelry at home; you’ll be treated more like a local.

localTips.title: Ask about ‘morro’ boundaries
localTips.description: Some streets shift quickly from tourist to risky; have a local (hotel host, bartender) mark where not to walk, especially around Centro/Lapa and Santa Teresa.

foodToTry.title: Feijoada (Saturday lunch)
foodToTry.description: Order it as a long lunch with farofa, couve, and orange; go early to avoid sold-out portions at popular spots.

foodToTry.title: Churrasco at a rodízio
foodToTry.description: Start with grilled meats, not the buffet sides, and pace yourself; ask for “mal passado/ao ponto” to control doneness.

foodToTry.title: Açaí the Rio way
foodToTry.description: Try it unsweetened or lightly sweetened, topped with granola and banana; avoid syrup-heavy versions if you want the classic taste.

foodToTry.title: Pão de queijo + cafezinho at a padaria
foodToTry.description: Stop at a neighborhood bakery for fresh pão de queijo and a tiny strong coffee; it’s a cheap, reliable snack between sights.

gettingAround.title: Metro for fast cross-city moves
gettingAround.description: Use the metro for Zona Sul ↔ Centro and avoid surface traffic; keep bags in front during rush hour and exit into busy streets.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing for nights and tricky routes
gettingAround.description: Use Uber/99 after dark or when crossing unfamiliar areas; confirm the plate before entering and set pickup points on well-lit corners.

gettingAround.title: Walking and bikes along the beachfront
gettingAround.description: The Copacabana–Ipanema–Leblon promenade is easy on foot or bike (Bike Itaú); don’t cycle with a phone in hand and avoid empty stretches late at night.

topThingsToDo.title: Enter on an early time slot (Circuit-based visit)
topThingsToDo.description: Book the first entry you can and pick a circuit that includes the classic viewpoint; you can’t freely wander or backtrack, so choose the route that matches your priorities.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike Huayna Picchu OR Machu Picchu Mountain
topThingsToDo.description: Grab permits weeks/months ahead; Huayna Picchu is steeper with iconic overlooks, while Machu Picchu Mountain is longer but less exposed and often easier to get.

topThingsToDo.title: Do the Sun Gate (Inti Punku) add-on
topThingsToDo.description: If your ticket allows, hike to Inti Punku for a high panoramic view without the extreme climbs; go right after entry to beat congestion and clouds.

topThingsToDo.title: Visit the Inca Bridge trail (when open)
topThingsToDo.description: A short, narrow cliffside walk with big views and fewer people; follow staff instructions because sections can close for safety.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise-to-late-morning photography loop
topThingsToDo.description: Start at the main viewpoint for the postcard shot, then use the rest of your circuit to shoot terraces and stonework as crowds shift and light improves.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Last-minute” Machu Picchu ticket resellers in Cusco/Aguas Calientes
scamsToAvoid.description: Many charge high markups or sell the wrong circuit/date; buy only via official channels and verify circuit, time, and passport details.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial bus queues and fake “priority” tickets
scamsToAvoid.description: At Aguas Calientes, ignore anyone offering shortcuts; use the official Consettur ticket booth and the clearly marked line.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi/collectivo price bait-and-switch to Hidroeléctrica
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may quote a low price then add fees for “tolls” or “extra passengers”; agree on total price and drop-off in writing before you get in.

localTips.title: Bring your passport and match it to your ticket
localTips.description: Rangers check IDs and may deny entry if names/numbers don’t match; a photo of the passport is risky—carry the original.

localTips.title: Pack a small daypack only
localTips.description: Large backpacks can be refused; use a compact pack with water, rain layer, sun protection, and snacks for after your visit.

localTips.title: Use the toilets before entering (and keep coins)
localTips.description: There are no bathrooms inside the ruins; the entrance toilets are paid and re-entry is generally not allowed.

localTips.title: Plan for weather to change fast
localTips.description: Morning can be misty and cool, then hot by late morning; a light rain jacket and quick-dry layers beat bulky clothing.

foodToTry.title: Trucha (Andean trout)
foodToTry.description: Order it a la plancha or al ajo in Aguas Calientes; it’s fresh, quick, and lighter than heavy set menus before hikes.

foodToTry.title: Lomo saltado
foodToTry.description: A reliable post-ruins meal; ask for “poco aceite” if you want it less greasy after a long day.

foodToTry.title: Quinoa soup (sopa de quinua)
foodToTry.description: Great for altitude and cool mornings; look for small local lunch spots offering a daily menú with soup included.

foodToTry.title: Coca tea (mate de coca)
foodToTry.description: Sip it in Cusco or Aguas Calientes to ease altitude discomfort; avoid it right before strict drug tests as it can trigger screening.

gettingAround.title: Cusco/Ollantaytambo to Aguas Calientes by train
gettingAround.description: Book early for better times and prices; sit on the river side for views and keep your passport handy for boarding.

gettingAround.title: Aguas Calientes to Machu Picchu by official shuttle bus
gettingAround.description: Buses start early and run continuously; queue 30–60 minutes ahead in peak season and buy round-trip if you’re unsure of exit time.

gettingAround.title: Walk up/down instead of the bus (fit travelers)
gettingAround.description: The steep stair trail takes about 60–90 minutes up; start before dawn with a headlamp and use trekking poles for the descent.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Walled City at dawn
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (6–8am) for shade and empty streets; start at Torre del Reloj and wander toward Plaza Santo Domingo before vendors set up.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset on the city walls
topThingsToDo.description: Enter the ramparts near Baluarte de Santo Domingo and stroll toward Café del Mar area; bring water and claim a spot 45–60 minutes before sunset.

topThingsToDo.title: Getsemaní street art + nightlife loop
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Plaza de la Trinidad at dusk, then walk Calle de la Sierpe for murals and low-key bars; keep valuables minimal in crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Castillo de San Felipe + Las Bóvedas
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening to beat tour buses; hire a licensed guide at the entrance for the tunnel stories, then shop for crafts at Las Bóvedas (negotiate politely).

topThingsToDo.title: Rosario Islands day trip (choose the right style)
topThingsToDo.description: For calmer water and fewer crowds, pick a small-group speedboat leaving 8–9am and confirm return time and island stops in writing; avoid “party boat” if you want beach time.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unpriced menu items and “free” samples
scamsToAvoid.description: Only order from menus with visible prices (including taxes/service); decline “try this” offers from street vendors unless you agree on a price first.

scamsToAvoid.title: Aggressive beach vendors (massages, oysters, photos, chairs)
scamsToAvoid.description: On Bocagrande/Playa Blanca, ask “¿Cuánto cuesta en total?” before anyone starts; if they begin without agreement, firmly say “No, gracias” and walk away.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi fare surprises and detours
scamsToAvoid.description: Taxis often don’t use meters—confirm the fare before entering and pay in small bills; if a driver won’t quote a price, take another or use an app.

localTips.title: Heat strategy that locals use
localTips.description: Plan outdoor sightseeing 7–11am and after 4pm; take a long lunch/siesta in the hottest hours and carry electrolytes, not just water.

localTips.title: Where to stay by vibe
localTips.description: Walled City for walkability and architecture, Getsemaní for nightlife and murals, Bocagrande for high-rises and beach access; check sound levels if you’re a light sleeper.

localTips.title: Money and bargaining
localTips.description: ATMs inside malls (e.g., Plaza Bocagrande) are safer and reliable; negotiate on souvenirs but not on clearly priced restaurant bills.

localTips.title: Rainy-season reality
localTips.description: Short downpours are common—pack a compact poncho and sandals; schedule islands on the clearest forecast day and keep a city-museum backup plan.

foodToTry.title: Arepa de huevo
foodToTry.description: Best as a mid-morning snack; order it hot and eat immediately so it stays crisp.

foodToTry.title: Ceviche cartagenero
foodToTry.description: Try it from a busy, high-turnover spot; ask for “poco picante” if you want it mild and skip if it’s been sitting in the sun.

foodToTry.title: Posta negra cartagenera
foodToTry.description: A slow-cooked, slightly sweet beef dish—great for dinner in the Walled City; pair with coconut rice and patacones.

foodToTry.title: Limónada de coco
foodToTry.description: Order it without extra sugar if you’re sensitive; it’s a perfect heat break between walking stops.

gettingAround.title: Walk within Centro + Getsemaní
gettingAround.description: Most sights are 10–25 minutes apart on foot; wear breathable clothes and choose shaded streets (Calle de la Iglesia/Calle del Porvenir area) midday.

gettingAround.title: Use ride-hailing for clear pricing
gettingAround.description: Apps can reduce haggling and help with directions; confirm the license plate before getting in and avoid accepting “cash-only” changes mid-ride.

gettingAround.title: Boats and island transfers
gettingAround.description: Departures leave from Muelle de la Bodeguita; ask about sea conditions, life jackets, and exact return hour, and keep valuables in a dry bag.

topThingsToDo.title: Monserrate at the right time
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday morning for clear views and fewer crowds; take the cable car up and funicular down to avoid long lines.

topThingsToDo.title: La Candelaria + Museo del Oro combo
topThingsToDo.description: Start early with Museo del Oro, then walk Calle 11/12 to Plaza de Bolívar; keep your phone put away on quieter side streets.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunday Ciclovía like a local
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike near Parque Virrey or Parque Nacional and ride the car-free routes; stop for fresh juice and arepas from street vendors.

topThingsToDo.title: Usaquén flea market and brunch
topThingsToDo.description: Go Sunday before noon for the best crafts and fewer pickpockets; book a brunch spot nearby and pay by card when possible.

topThingsToDo.title: Andrés Carne de Res (Chía) or Zona G night
topThingsToDo.description: If you go to Chía, arrange a round-trip car and leave before late-night traffic; for an easier night, bar-hop Zona G/Chapinero.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter ‘issues’ and route padding
scamsToAvoid.description: Use app-based rides or request the fare estimate before moving; if the driver refuses, get out while still at the curb.

scamsToAvoid.title: Distraction theft in busy spots
scamsToAvoid.description: Watch for someone bumping you or asking to sign a petition while another grabs your phone; keep valuables in a zipped front pocket.

scamsToAvoid.title: Card skimming at bars and small shops
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask for the card machine to be brought to you (“datáfono aquí”) and avoid handing your card over; use contactless when available.

localTips.title: Plan around altitude and weather
localTips.description: Bogotá is high and cool—drink water, take it easy day one, and carry a light rain jacket; weather can change in 10 minutes.

localTips.title: Use neighborhoods strategically
localTips.description: Stay/meet friends in Chapinero, Zona G, or Parque 93 for walkability; visit La Candelaria in daylight and leave before rush hour.

localTips.title: Cash is still king for small spends
localTips.description: Carry small bills (10k–20k COP) for markets and tips; ask for “cambio” early because vendors run out.

localTips.title: Safety in practice, not paranoia
localTips.description: Keep your phone out of sight on the street and step into a café to check maps; at night, take door-to-door rides instead of walking.

foodToTry.title: Ajiaco santafereño
foodToTry.description: Classic Bogotá chicken-and-potato soup; order it with avocado, capers, and cream for the full experience.

foodToTry.title: Chocolate santafereño with cheese
foodToTry.description: Hot chocolate served with salty cheese to dunk; best as a late-afternoon warm-up in La Candelaria.

foodToTry.title: Tamales tolimenses (breakfast)
foodToTry.description: Hearty tamal wrapped in leaf, often with hot chocolate; go early to bakeries because they sell out.

foodToTry.title: Empanadas with ají + chicha/masato
foodToTry.description: Grab crispy empanadas and add the local spicy ají; try traditional fermented drinks in La Candelaria from reputable spots.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing over street taxis
gettingAround.description: Use apps for price transparency and safer pickups; share your trip details and meet the car inside a well-lit entrance.

gettingAround.title: TransMilenio for fast corridors (with care)
gettingAround.description: It’s efficient on main lines but crowded—avoid peak hours and keep bags in front; buy a rechargeable card at stations.

gettingAround.title: Walking and biking in the right areas
gettingAround.description: Walk in Parque 93/Zona T/Zona G during the day and early evening; for longer distances, bike on Ciclovía routes rather than traffic-heavy avenues.

topThingsToDo.title: Eat your way through Miraflores & Barranco
topThingsToDo.description: Do a ceviche lunch (best before 3pm) then hit a pisco sour bar in Barranco; reserve top restaurants weeks ahead or go for a weekday late lunch.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Miraflores Malecón at sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Parque del Amor and continue to Larcomar cliffs; keep your phone off the street edge and use the parks’ paths instead of roadside sidewalks.

topThingsToDo.title: Explore Centro Histórico early
topThingsToDo.description: Go right at opening for Plaza Mayor, Cathedral, and San Francisco catacombs; use a registered walking tour and leave valuables at your hotel.

topThingsToDo.title: Barranco street art + Puente de los Suspiros
topThingsToDo.description: Visit mid-morning for quiet photos, then walk Bajada de Baños down toward the coast; finish with coffee or craft beer on Avenida San Martín.

topThingsToDo.title: Museo Larco in Pueblo Libre
topThingsToDo.description: Go late afternoon to avoid school groups and pair it with the on-site café; use a rideshare—street hailing here can be slow.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake/overpriced taxis at airport and hotspots
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip random drivers holding signs or offering “fixed price”; book via official airport taxi counters or use a reputable rideshare from inside the terminal.

scamsToAvoid.title: Card swap/extra charges in bars and small shops
scamsToAvoid.description: Pay contactless when possible and watch the card the whole time; insist on the receipt before you leave the counter.

scamsToAvoid.title: Distraction theft in crowded areas
scamsToAvoid.description: Be wary of people bumping you, offering help with menus/ATMs, or spilling something on you; move away and check your belongings immediately.

localTips.title: Timing for ceviche matters
localTips.description: Locals eat ceviche at lunch because it’s freshest then; for dinner, choose tiradito, causas, or arroz con mariscos instead.

localTips.title: Lima is humid and gray—pack for microclimates
localTips.description: Bring a light jacket year-round and sunscreen even on overcast days; evenings on the coast can feel chilly.

localTips.title: Choose neighborhoods strategically
localTips.description: Base yourself in Miraflores or Barranco for walkability; visit Centro by day and return by rideshare after dark.

localTips.title: Cash helps, but use the right ATMs
localTips.description: Use bank ATMs inside malls (Larcomar, Jockey Plaza) and withdraw in soles; decline “dynamic currency conversion” if offered.

foodToTry.title: Ceviche + leche de tigre
foodToTry.description: Order at a dedicated cevichería before mid-afternoon; ask for spice level and pair with chicha morada.

foodToTry.title: Lomo saltado
foodToTry.description: Try it at a classic criollo spot and ask for the fries separate if you like them crisp; it’s a great non-seafood staple.

foodToTry.title: Anticuchos
foodToTry.description: Best from busy evening street grills (often outside stadiums/parks); go where locals queue and pay with small bills.

foodToTry.title: Pisco sour or chilcano
foodToTry.description: Order at a proper bar and ask for quebranta pisco; one is strong—sip slowly and eat something with it.

gettingAround.title: Rideshares are simplest
gettingAround.description: Use Uber/Cabify/InDrive, confirm the plate, and sit in the back; avoid street hailing late at night.

gettingAround.title: Metropolitano bus for fast north–south trips
gettingAround.description: Buy and top up the card at stations and use it to bypass traffic on main corridors; avoid rush-hour if you dislike crowds.

gettingAround.title: Walking + short hops within Miraflores/Barranco
gettingAround.description: These areas are the most pedestrian-friendly; for the steep bajadas to the beach, take a rideshare down and walk back up via parks.

topThingsToDo.title: Cerro San Cristóbal (Parque Metropolitano)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for clear Andes views; ride the funicular up and walk down through Bellavista. On Sundays, streets are calmer and families fill the park.

topThingsToDo.title: Barrio Lastarria + GAM
topThingsToDo.description: Browse independent galleries and bookstores, then catch a cheap performance or exhibit at Centro GAM. Aim for weekday afternoons to avoid peak crowds and higher menu prices.

topThingsToDo.title: Sky Costanera at sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Book online and time entry 45–60 minutes before sunset for daylight-to-night views. Skip weekends if you hate lines; weekday evenings move fast.

topThingsToDo.title: Mercado Central + La Vega (food crawl)
topThingsToDo.description: Eat seafood at Mercado Central, then cross to La Vega for fruit juices and local snacks—carry small bills and keep your phone out of sight. Go before 1 pm for fresher selection and less chaos.

topThingsToDo.title: Cajón del Maipo day trip
topThingsToDo.description: Use a reputable tour or rental car; leave at dawn to beat traffic and secure viewpoints. In winter, check road conditions and bring layers—temperature swings are sharp.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Mustard/ketchup stain” distraction theft
scamsToAvoid.description: Someone points out a stain and offers to help while an accomplice grabs your bag/phone; step away, say no, and keep moving. Don’t stop to “clean up” in the street.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter games from the airport
scamsToAvoid.description: Some drivers “forget” the meter or take long routes; use official taxi stands with a fixed fare voucher or app rides. Confirm the price before getting in and avoid curbside solicitations.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake or overcharging currency exchange
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid street exchangers and tiny kiosks with vague rates; use bank branches or reputable casas de cambio and count cash before leaving. Be wary of “special rates” offered by strangers.

localTips.title: Pick your neighborhoods to stay
localTips.description: For walkability and dining, base yourself in Lastarria, Bellas Artes, Providencia, or Las Condes near a Metro station. Avoid booking right by major bus terminals if you’re sensitive to petty theft risk.

localTips.title: Know when Santiago rests
localTips.description: Many places slow down on Sundays and some close on Mondays; plan museums and shopping for Tue–Sat. Lunch menus (menú del día) are best value on weekdays.

localTips.title: Handle phone safety like a local
localTips.description: Don’t use your phone at curb edges, Metro doors, or while walking in crowded areas; step inside a shop to check maps. Use a crossbody bag worn in front in busy markets.

localTips.title: Daytime hikes, nightlife later
localTips.description: Hike Cerro Santa Lucía or San Cristóbal earlier, then do bars in Barrio Italia/Lastarria at night with short rides home. If you’re out late, use app rides door-to-door rather than walking long blocks.

foodToTry.title: Pastel de choclo
foodToTry.description: Corn pie with beef, chicken, egg, and olives—best in home-style restaurants (picadas). Ask for “con ensalada chilena” to balance the richness.

foodToTry.title: Empanada de pino
foodToTry.description: Classic baked empanada with beef, onion, egg, olive; it’s filling enough for a meal. Watch for the hot juice inside—bite carefully.

foodToTry.title: Completo italiano
foodToTry.description: Chilean hot dog loaded with avocado, tomato, and mayo—order it “italiano” at Fuente Alemana-style sandwich shops. Go hungry; portions are big.

foodToTry.title: Mariscos + paila marina
foodToTry.description: Seafood stew is ideal at Mercado Central; pick a place with clear posted prices and ask the total before ordering extras. Pair with a chilled white wine from the Central Valley.

gettingAround.title: Metro (fastest within the city)
gettingAround.description: Buy a Bip! card and top up at stations; tap in and out and keep it handy for buses too. Avoid rush-hour crush if you’re carrying luggage (roughly 8–9:30 am, 6–7:30 pm).

gettingAround.title: App rides for nights and hills
gettingAround.description: Use ride-hailing for late evenings, uphill areas, or when connecting neighborhoods like Bellavista to Providencia. Verify plate and driver name before entering.

gettingAround.title: Airport transfers
gettingAround.description: For budget, use official airport buses (e.g., to Los Héroes or Pajaritos) then Metro; for comfort, book an official transfer or fixed-fare taxi at the counter. Avoid random drivers inside arrivals offering deals.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk Old Havana early (Habana Vieja)
topThingsToDo.description: Start around 7–9am for cooler temps and fewer crowds; hit Plaza Vieja, Catedral, and side streets like Oficios for real neighborhood life.

topThingsToDo.title: Malecón at sunset, then Centro Habana snacks
topThingsToDo.description: Go for golden hour breezes; after, grab pizza or churros from local windows along San Lázaro/Neptuno instead of tourist bars.

topThingsToDo.title: Fábrica de Arte Cubano (FAC) night
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive before doors open and bring cash; it’s part gallery, part concerts/club with multiple rooms—check schedule same day on social pages.

topThingsToDo.title: Classic car ride with a fixed route
topThingsToDo.description: Negotiate price and itinerary before getting in; a solid loop is Vedado (Hotel Nacional), Plaza de la Revolución, and along the Malecón.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to Playas del Este (Santa María)
topThingsToDo.description: Go midweek for space and calmer service; bring water/snacks and ask your driver to pick a specific “guardia” beach entrance for easy return.

scamsToAvoid.title: The “friend” who leads you to a bar/restaurant
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone insists on escorting you to a “best mojito/cigar” spot, expect inflated bills and commissions—politely decline and keep walking.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake cigars and street “factory deals”
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid buying cigars on the street or from “my cousin at the factory”; buy sealed boxes from official shops and check for intact seals/labels.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi price switch or ‘meter broken’
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm total fare (and currency) before the ride and have small bills; if the driver changes terms mid-ride, get out at a safe, busy corner.

localTips.title: Cash is king; plan for limited cards/ATMs
localTips.description: Carry enough cash for daily expenses and keep it split up; exchange only at official exchange houses or reputable hotels, not random street offers.

localTips.title: Offline maps and addresses matter
localTips.description: Download maps for offline use and screenshot your casa/hotel address; many places have weak data and street signs can be inconsistent.

localTips.title: Bring basics that are hard to find
localTips.description: Pack sunscreen, mosquito repellent, meds, and a power bank; shortages are common and prices can be high when available.

localTips.title: Choose live music venues carefully
localTips.description: Ask locals/casa hosts for what’s good tonight; some “show” venues overcharge—small neighborhood peñas and cultural centers feel more authentic.

foodToTry.title: Ropa vieja with moros y cristianos
foodToTry.description: Order it in a paladar; ask for “con tostones” if you want crispy plantains on the side.

foodToTry.title: Lechón asado (roast pork)
foodToTry.description: Best on weekends or at family-style spots; go early because popular places sell out.

foodToTry.title: Tostones or maduros
foodToTry.description: Ask for them freshly made (“recién hechos”); they’re the go-to side when main dishes are limited.

foodToTry.title: Cuban coffee and a guava pastry
foodToTry.description: Try a strong cafecito or cortadito; pair with pastelito de guayaba from a bakery window for a cheap breakfast.

gettingAround.title: Taxis: agree on price and use set pickup points
gettingAround.description: Negotiate upfront and confirm the route; for reliability, ask your host/hotel to arrange a taxi and set a clear pickup landmark.

gettingAround.title: Walking between Habana Vieja, Centro, and Vedado
gettingAround.description: Daytime walks are doable via the Malecón corridor; at night, use taxis for longer stretches and stick to well-lit main streets.

gettingAround.title: Shared options (almendrones/collectivos)
gettingAround.description: Shared rides run along common arteries like 23rd Street and major avenues; ask locals “¿por dónde pasa?” and pay in small cash.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk Old Québec (Upper + Lower Town)
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Terrasse Dufferin, then take the Breakneck Stairs down to Petit-Champlain; go early or after 7pm to dodge day-trip crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Cycle or stroll the Promenade Samuel-De Champlain
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike and follow the riverfront paths for skyline views; pack a wind layer even in summer.

topThingsToDo.title: Montmorency Falls + Ile d’Orléans loop
topThingsToDo.description: Pair the falls with a drive to Île d’Orléans for cideries and farm stands; book tastings on weekends in peak season.

topThingsToDo.title: Citadelle & Plains of Abraham
topThingsToDo.description: Catch the Changing of the Guard (summer) and then picnic on the Plains; the Musée national des beaux-arts is an easy add-on nearby.

topThingsToDo.title: Evening food + drinks on Rue Saint-Jean or Rue Saint-Joseph
topThingsToDo.description: For a more local vibe than Petit-Champlain, bar-hop Saint-Jean (inside the walls) or Saint-Joseph (Saint-Roch) and reserve dinner Fri–Sat.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed “tour guide” pitches in Old Québec
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore unsolicited street pitches for paid tours; book through official operators or the tourist info center to avoid bait-and-switch itineraries.

scamsToAvoid.title: Inflated taxi rides from the station/airport
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm the meter is on and ask for an estimate before you get in; consider the 80/76 buses or pre-booked rides to avoid surprise totals.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘authentic’ souvenirs on Petit-Champlain
scamsToAvoid.description: Watch for imported goods sold as local; look for “Fabriqué au Québec/Canada” labels or shop at local makers in Saint-Roch.

localTips.title: Use the funicular strategically
localTips.description: Take the funicular up from Petit-Champlain to avoid the steep climb; walk down for the views and photo stops.

localTips.title: Time your Old Port visit around cruise ships
localTips.description: On cruise days, Old Québec gets packed mid-day; do museums and quieter neighborhoods then, and save the walls for early morning.

localTips.title: Dress for micro-weather by the river
localTips.description: The St. Lawrence wind can feel 5–10°C cooler; bring a light shell even if it’s sunny in the city core.

localTips.title: Reservations are essential in peak periods
localTips.description: For popular bistros, book 3–7 days ahead in summer and during Carnaval; walk-ins are easiest at 5pm or after 8:30pm.

foodToTry.title: Poutine (Québec-style)
foodToTry.description: Go for fresh squeaky curds and proper gravy; try it as a late-night snack when queues are shorter.

foodToTry.title: Tourtière
foodToTry.description: Order the meat pie with pickles and mustard; it’s especially common in winter menus and holiday season.

foodToTry.title: Maple “tire sur la neige” (in season)
foodToTry.description: In late winter/early spring, visit a sugar shack to roll hot maple syrup on snow and eat it on a stick.

foodToTry.title: Local cider and ice cider
foodToTry.description: Sample ice cider from Île d’Orléans producers; it’s dessert-sweet and best shared as a tasting flight.

gettingAround.title: Walk, but plan for hills and cobblestones
gettingAround.description: Old Québec is compact yet steep; wear grippy shoes and use the funicular or bus to save your knees.

gettingAround.title: RTC buses for key connections
gettingAround.description: Buses are reliable for Montcalm, Saint-Roch, and Sainte-Foy; buy passes or tickets ahead to avoid hunting for change.

gettingAround.title: Driving and parking strategy
gettingAround.description: Skip driving inside the walls; park once (garage in Old Port/Saint-Roch) and explore on foot to avoid narrow streets and pricey meters.

topThingsToDo.title: Stanley Park Seawall (bike or walk)
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike near Denman St and go counterclockwise for smoother flow; start early to beat crowds and stop at Siwash Rock and the Lions Gate viewpoint.

topThingsToDo.title: Granville Island (market + studios)
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday morning for the Public Market, then wander the backstreets for artist studios; grab lunch to eat outside by the water taxis.

topThingsToDo.title: Capilano Suspension Bridge or Lynn Canyon
topThingsToDo.description: For a paid, polished experience go Capilano near opening; for a free local alternative do Lynn Canyon’s suspension bridge and the Baden-Powell trail loop.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset at English Bay to the Seawall beaches
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the Seawall from Sunset Beach to Kits Beach at golden hour; pick up snacks on Denman or in Yaletown and sit by the Inukshuk.

topThingsToDo.title: North Shore gondola views (Grouse or Sea to Sky)
topThingsToDo.description: Grouse is quickest from downtown for city views; if you have a car, Sea to Sky Gondola in Squamish pairs well with Shannon Falls.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “tour” taxis at cruise/airport
scamsToAvoid.description: Use the official taxi queue or ride-hail with in-app pricing; if offered a “special flat rate,” decline and stick to the meter/app fare.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake charity petitions on Granville/Robson
scamsToAvoid.description: Some canvassers pressure for on-the-spot donations or card taps; donate later via the organization’s official website instead.

scamsToAvoid.title: Ticket resellers for events and attractions
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid street/online scalpers for Canucks/attractions; buy from official sites or verified resale platforms to prevent invalid QR codes.

localTips.title: Plan around rain, not temperature
localTips.description: Bring a light waterproof shell and shoes with grip; locals skip umbrellas in wind and use hoods instead.

localTips.title: Downtown Eastside awareness
localTips.description: Around Hastings/Main, expect visible street disorder; it’s generally safe to pass through, but keep valuables put away and stay alert at night.

localTips.title: Best viewpoint with minimal effort
localTips.description: Take the Canada Line to Olympic Village and walk to Cambie Bridge for skyline photos, especially after dusk when the city lights up.

localTips.title: Reservations matter in peak season
localTips.description: Book popular spots (sushi, waterfront patios, tasting menus) a few days ahead, especially Fri–Sun; walk-ins are much easier before 6 pm.

foodToTry.title: Sushi (Vancouver-style)
foodToTry.description: Prioritize neighborhood sushi bars over tourist strips; look for daily specials with BC spot prawns (in season) and local albacore.

foodToTry.title: Japadog
foodToTry.description: Try the Terimayo or Okonomiyaki-style toppings; it’s quick, filling, and ideal between downtown sights.

foodToTry.title: BC salmon (cedar-plank or smoked)
foodToTry.description: Order sockeye when available; for a casual option, grab smoked salmon from Granville Island and picnic by the water.

foodToTry.title: Dim sum in Richmond
foodToTry.description: Take the Canada Line to Richmond for better value and variety than downtown; go early (10–11 am) to avoid long waits.

gettingAround.title: Transit with Compass Card
gettingAround.description: Use Compass (card or mobile wallet) for SkyTrain, buses, and SeaBus; avoid weekday rush hours for easier luggage trips.

gettingAround.title: Seabus to North Vancouver
gettingAround.description: From Waterfront Station, it’s a scenic 12-minute ride; combine with Lonsdale Quay for food and a quick city skyline view.

gettingAround.title: Biking and micro-mobility
gettingAround.description: The separated lanes downtown are excellent; use bike share for short hops but lock carefully and avoid leaving bikes unattended overnight.

topThingsToDo.title: St. Lawrence Market + Distillery District
topThingsToDo.description: Go before noon for the best selection at St. Lawrence Market, then walk or streetcar to the Distillery for shops and galleries; weekdays are far less crowded.

topThingsToDo.title: Toronto Islands by ferry (or water taxi)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the ferry from Jack Layton Terminal; for speed, use a water taxi back to the city at sunset for skyline views and shorter lines.

topThingsToDo.title: Kensington Market + Chinatown food crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Visit on a weekday afternoon for the best vibe; grab snacks in Chinatown (Spadina) and wander Kensington’s vintage shops and patios.

topThingsToDo.title: CN Tower + Ripley’s Aquarium (timed right)
topThingsToDo.description: Book the first entry slot or go after 8pm to dodge school groups; pair with Ripley’s next door and walk the waterfront after.

topThingsToDo.title: High Park + Roncesvalles
topThingsToDo.description: Take Line 2 to High Park Station and explore Grenadier Pond trails; afterward, eat along Roncesvalles for low-key neighborhood spots.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed taxi/ride solicitation
scamsToAvoid.description: At Pearson/Union, ignore anyone approaching you inside the terminal; use the official taxi stand, UP Express, or order rideshare in-app.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street petition/donation pressure
scamsToAvoid.description: In busy areas (Yonge-Dundas, Eaton Centre), decline clipboards asking for quick “signatures” or tap donations—some are aggressive and opaque.

scamsToAvoid.title: Online resale tickets for big events
scamsToAvoid.description: For Leafs/Raptors/concerts, avoid sketchy DMs and off-platform transfers; use official vendors or reputable resale sites with buyer protection.

localTips.title: Use PRESTO or contactless, not paper fares
localTips.description: Tap with PRESTO or credit/debit on TTC and GO; it’s faster and avoids fumbling for exact change on streetcars.

localTips.title: Streetcars: board any door, then tap
localTips.description: On new streetcars you can enter at any door; tap at the reader inside to avoid fare inspectors’ fines.

localTips.title: Skip Queen Quay bottlenecks
localTips.description: If the waterfront is jammed, walk one block north (Front/King) to get moving, then cut back down to the lake.

localTips.title: Plan around sports nights
localTips.description: When there’s a game at Scotiabank Arena, Union Station and nearby bars get packed; eat earlier or head east to St. Lawrence for calmer options.

foodToTry.title: Peameal bacon sandwich
foodToTry.description: Get it at St. Lawrence Market; go early to avoid the longest lines and ask for extra mustard/pickles if you like it punchy.

foodToTry.title: Jamaican patties
foodToTry.description: Grab a spicy beef patty from a Caribbean bakery; it’s an easy, cheap snack that’s everywhere in the core.

foodToTry.title: Hakka (Indo-Chinese) dishes
foodToTry.description: Try chili chicken or Manchurian noodles in Scarborough or near the suburbs; it’s a Toronto specialty many visitors miss.

foodToTry.title: Korean fried chicken (Koreatown)
foodToTry.description: Hit Bloor near Christie/Bathurst; go later in the evening when tables turn faster and pair with a light lager.

gettingAround.title: TTC subway + streetcars for the core
gettingAround.description: The subway is fastest north–south; for downtown, streetcars beat taxis in traffic if you’re staying along King/Queen/Spadina.

gettingAround.title: UP Express from Pearson
gettingAround.description: It’s the simplest airport transfer to Union Station in about 25 minutes; buy at the kiosk and tap contactless to enter.

gettingAround.title: Walk + bike share for short hops
gettingAround.description: Downtown is very walkable; Bike Share Toronto is great for waterfront and neighborhood-to-neighborhood trips—use the app to find open docks.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Montreal early (or late) walk
topThingsToDo.description: Go before 10am or after 8pm to avoid crowds; start at Place Jacques-Cartier, loop to the Old Port, and pop into Notre-Dame Basilica (book a timed entry).

topThingsToDo.title: Mount Royal at golden hour
topThingsToDo.description: Take the Olmsted trail from Avenue du Parc to the Kondiaronk Belvedere for skyline views; bring layers—wind up top is real even in summer.

topThingsToDo.title: Jean-Talon Market + Little Italy snack crawl
topThingsToDo.description: Shop and sample at the market, then walk to Saint-Viateur/Beaubien for espresso and pastries; weekdays are calmer than Saturday.

topThingsToDo.title: Plateau + Mile End street art and shops
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll Rue Saint-Denis and Boulevard Saint-Laurent, then detour onto side streets for colorful exterior staircases and murals; download the MURAL Festival map for a self-guided route.

topThingsToDo.title: Canal Lachine bike ride
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a BIXI and ride the flat path from Atwater Market toward the Old Port; stop for picnic supplies at Atwater and watch boats at the locks.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed ticket resellers
scamsToAvoid.description: Outside big festivals/venues, avoid people offering “last-minute” passes; buy only from official box offices or the event’s verified resale platform.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced horse carriages in Old Montreal
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm total price, duration, and route before getting in and insist it’s written; many visitors get upsold for “extra time” mid-ride.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake parking/payment QR codes
scamsToAvoid.description: Use the city-approved app/sign instructions and check the URL/app name; scammers sometimes place lookalike QR stickers on meters.

localTips.title: Sunday tam-tams at Mount Royal
localTips.description: In warm months, head to the George-Étienne Cartier monument area Sunday afternoon; bring cash for snacks and expect a relaxed, family-friendly vibe.

localTips.title: Know the terrace rules on busy streets
localTips.description: On popular strips (Saint-Laurent, Saint-Denis, Crescent), patios fill fast—eat earlier (5–6pm) or later (after 8:30pm) for shorter waits.

localTips.title: Language goes a long way
localTips.description: Start with “Bonjour” in shops and you’ll usually get seamless bilingual service; it’s a small etiquette point locals notice.

localTips.title: Plan for construction season
localTips.description: Road closures are constant in summer—use metro or BIXI when possible and add buffer time if you must take a taxi/ride-share.

foodToTry.title: Poutine (done right)
foodToTry.description: Look for squeaky curds and fresh fries; go off-peak late afternoon to avoid lines at the best counters.

foodToTry.title: Montreal-style bagels
foodToTry.description: Try them warm from the wood-fired oven and keep it simple with sesame + cream cheese; they’re smaller, denser, and sweeter than NYC bagels.

foodToTry.title: Smoked meat sandwich
foodToTry.description: Order “medium-fat” on rye with mustard for the classic; go at opening or late lunch to dodge the longest queues.

foodToTry.title: Québec classics: tourtière or sugar-shack flavors
foodToTry.description: In winter, seek out maple taffy (tire sur la neige) and hearty tourtière; many bistros serve seasonal versions without leaving the city.

gettingAround.title: STM metro + buses
gettingAround.description: Buy an OPUS card or use contactless at stations; the metro is fastest for crossing town, and buses cover neighborhoods like Plateau and Mile End well.

gettingAround.title: BIXI bike share
gettingAround.description: Best from April–November; use protected lanes on de Maisonneuve and the Canal Lachine path for low-stress riding.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and ride-shares
gettingAround.description: Taxis are plentiful downtown and at the airport; for late nights, compare apps and confirm pickup spot—some streets are one-way and easily missed.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset at Jemaa el-Fna (from above)
topThingsToDo.description: Skip the ground-level hassle and watch the square from a rooftop cafe (order mint tea, tip 10–20 MAD) as food stalls and performers ramp up after dusk.

topThingsToDo.title: Get lost (strategically) in the Medina souks
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Bab Agnaou or Rahba Kedima and wander with offline maps; shop deeper inside for better prices and ask for a written total before they wrap anything.

topThingsToDo.title: Bahia Palace + Mellah spice alleys
topThingsToDo.description: Go at opening to beat tour groups, then walk to the Mellah for calmer streets and specialty shops (preserved lemons, ras el hanout) at local prices.

topThingsToDo.title: Jardin Majorelle early + Yves Saint Laurent Museum
topThingsToDo.description: Book the first timed entry online and pair it with the nearby museum; it’s the easiest way to avoid the long midday lines.

topThingsToDo.title: Traditional hammam (non-tourist version)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a neighborhood hammam (bring flip-flops, a change of underwear, and 1–2 small towels) and ask for gommage + savon beldi for the real scrub.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Friendly guide’ to your riad
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone insists your street is closed or offers to “help,” decline firmly and keep walking; only follow directions from your host or official signage.

scamsToAvoid.title: Henna artists grabbing your hand
scamsToAvoid.description: They may start without asking and then demand high payment; keep hands in pockets in Jemaa el-Fna and agree on a price before any contact.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter ‘broken’ or inflated fare
scamsToAvoid.description: Insist on the meter (“compteur”) or set the price before entering; for airports, confirm the fixed tariff posted at the rank.

localTips.title: Best times to explore
localTips.description: Walk the Medina 9–11am for open shops and less crowding; do Jemaa el-Fna after 7pm when the food stalls are in full swing.

localTips.title: Bargaining that works
localTips.description: Ask the price, counter at ~40–50%, and walk away politely; the best deals usually happen when you’re already leaving.

localTips.title: Photography etiquette
localTips.description: Many performers and stall owners expect payment for photos; ask first and tip small (5–10 MAD) to avoid arguments.

localTips.title: Cash and small notes
localTips.description: Carry 10/20/50 MAD bills for tips and small buys; many souks won’t have change and card acceptance is limited in the Medina.

foodToTry.title: Tanjia (Marrakech specialty)
foodToTry.description: Order it at a local restaurant or ask your riad to arrange it; it’s slow-cooked meat best eaten at lunch, not late-night.

foodToTry.title: Mechoui
foodToTry.description: Try it in the morning or early afternoon when it’s freshest; go for shoulder cuts and eat with bread and cumin-salt on the side.

foodToTry.title: Harira + chebakia
foodToTry.description: A classic soup-and-sweet combo, especially good at dusk; choose busy stalls with steaming pots and quick turnover.

foodToTry.title: Fresh orange juice (but pick your spot)
foodToTry.description: Go to stands where they rinse the press and use covered ice; confirm the price per glass before they pour.

gettingAround.title: Walking in the Medina
gettingAround.description: Most lanes are pedestrian-only; use an offline map pin for your riad and note a nearby landmark (mosque, gate) to navigate back easily.

gettingAround.title: Petit taxis (inside the city)
gettingAround.description: Use them for short hops outside the Medina; always confirm meter use before the door closes and keep small bills for payment.

gettingAround.title: Apps and airport transfers
gettingAround.description: InDriver is common for agreed fares; for stress-free arrivals, pre-book a transfer through your riad so a driver meets you outside the terminal.

topThingsToDo.title: Giza Pyramids + Sphinx (early entry)
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening to beat heat and crowds; buy tickets at the main office and ignore “mandatory guide” claims. For photos, walk to Panorama Point for the classic three-pyramid view.

topThingsToDo.title: Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
topThingsToDo.description: Go on a weekday morning and buy timed entry online if available to avoid long queues. Plan 2–4 hours and add the outdoor plaza for pyramid-facing views.

topThingsToDo.title: Islamic Cairo: Al-Muizz Street + Khan el-Khalili at night
topThingsToDo.description: Visit after sunset when the historic facades are lit and temperatures drop; keep small cash for mosque entry/donations. For calmer shopping, start at Al-Muizz and end at the market.

topThingsToDo.title: Citadel of Saladin + Mosque of Muhammad Ali
topThingsToDo.description: Go late afternoon for golden-hour city panoramas and cooler weather. Dress modestly and bring socks if you prefer not to walk barefoot on mosque carpets.

topThingsToDo.title: Coptic Cairo: Hanging Church + Ben Ezra Synagogue
topThingsToDo.description: Combine sites in one walk around Mar Girgis Metro; arrive early to avoid tour groups. Stop at a nearby bakery for fresh baladi bread and snacks between visits.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Closed today” / “Only this entrance” at major sites
scamsToAvoid.description: People may redirect you to a shop or paid guide; verify hours on official signage and proceed to the main ticket office. Don’t follow anyone who grabs your arm or blocks your path.

scamsToAvoid.title: Camel/horse rides with price changes
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree on total price, duration, and drop-off point before mounting, and confirm it includes returning you to the gate. Pay only after the ride and keep small bills to avoid “no change” tricks.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter ‘broken’ and inflated fares
scamsToAvoid.description: Use Uber/Careem when possible, or set a price before you get in and confirm it’s for the whole car. Avoid drivers who insist on stopping at “papyrus/perfume” factories.

localTips.title: Cash is king—carry small notes
localTips.description: Keep 10/20/50 EGP notes for tips, toilets, and tickets; it prevents overpaying and awkward change games. Use ATMs inside banks/malls rather than street ATMs late at night.

localTips.title: Friday timing matters
localTips.description: Many shops open later on Fridays and midday traffic around mosques spikes after prayers. Do museums in the morning and markets in the evening.

localTips.title: Dress code + entry etiquette
localTips.description: For mosques, covered shoulders/knees and quiet behavior matter more than strict rules; women may want a light scarf. Ask before photographing people, especially in religious areas.

localTips.title: Beat the heat and pollution
localTips.description: Plan outdoor sights at sunrise/sunset and use midday for museums or cafés. A light mask/scarf helps on dusty days, and hydration salts are useful in summer.

foodToTry.title: Koshary
foodToTry.description: Cairo’s iconic mix of pasta, lentils, rice, onions, and spicy tomato sauce; order “medium hot” first time. Ask for extra crispy onions for texture.

foodToTry.title: Foul and Ta’ameya (Egyptian falafel)
foodToTry.description: Best as a breakfast street meal; ta’ameya is made from fava beans and is greener and fluffier than chickpea falafel. Pair with baladi bread, pickles, and tahini.

foodToTry.title: Hawawshi
foodToTry.description: Spiced minced meat baked inside baladi bread; request it well-done and eat it hot. Add tahini and pickles from the counter.

foodToTry.title: Molokhia with rice and chicken/rabbit
foodToTry.description: A garlicky green soup served at home-style restaurants; try it with “ta’sheesha” (garlic-coriander tempering). Ask for lemon on the side to brighten it.

gettingAround.title: Metro (fastest for many routes)
gettingAround.description: Use it to bypass traffic, especially between central Cairo and Coptic Cairo (Mar Girgis) or Giza areas. Avoid peak rush hours (roughly 8–10am, 4–7pm) if you want space.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing (Uber/Careem)
gettingAround.description: Usually the least hassle for visitors and avoids fare bargaining; set pickup points on main roads, not inside alleys. Keep a little cash in case drivers prefer it for short trips.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and microbuses (only if confident)
gettingAround.description: White taxis can be fine if you agree on price first; avoid long negotiations by stating your fare clearly and walking away if needed. Microbuses are cheap but confusing without Arabic route knowledge.

topThingsToDo.title: Table Mountain (cableway or Platteklip Gorge hike)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (first cable up) for clear views before the “tablecloth” cloud; book tickets online to skip queues. If hiking, start at sunrise and carry layers—weather flips fast.

topThingsToDo.title: Cape Peninsula road trip (Chapman’s Peak + Cape Point)
topThingsToDo.description: Drive clockwise: Hout Bay → Chapman’s Peak (toll) → Noordhoek → Cape Point → Simon’s Town. Leave by 8:00 to beat tour buses and wind closures.

topThingsToDo.title: Kirstenbosch Botanical Garden + boomslang walkway
topThingsToDo.description: Pack a picnic and time it for late afternoon light; summer Sunday concerts sell out, so buy tickets ahead. Use the Gate 2 parking if Gate 1 is full.

topThingsToDo.title: Bo-Kaap and city food stop
topThingsToDo.description: Go in the morning for photos and quieter streets; be respectful of residents and avoid blocking doorways. Pair it with a Cape Malay lunch nearby (bobotie or koesisters).

topThingsToDo.title: Wine tasting in Constantia (closest vineyards)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose 2–3 estates (Groot Constantia, Buitenverwachting, Steenberg) instead of rushing Stellenbosch. Book Uber both ways—parking fills on weekends.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Helpful” strangers offering directions/ATM help
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone approaches near ATMs or parking areas, disengage and step into a shop or busy spot. Never let anyone handle your phone/card or “watch your PIN.”

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial tour guides at viewpoints
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t accept surprise guiding fees at Signal Hill/Table Mountain parking; use licensed guides booked through reputable operators. Keep valuables out of sight in the car.

scamsToAvoid.title: Car break-ins via “spotters”
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t leave anything (even a jacket) visible; thieves target rental cars. If you need to stop, use staffed parking or shopping malls rather than roadside pull-offs.

localTips.title: Plan around wind and clouds
localTips.description: Use the Table Mountain webcam and wind forecast; if it’s blown out, swap in Kirstenbosch, Zeitz MOCAA, or a Constantia tasting. Keep a flexible day for the mountain.

localTips.title: Sunset is for Signal Hill, not always Lion’s Head
localTips.description: Lion’s Head gets crowded and dark on the descent; Signal Hill is safer and easier if you’re not hiking-savvy. If hiking Lion’s Head, bring a headlamp.

localTips.title: Beach choice matters
localTips.description: Clifton/Camps Bay are classic but cold; for warmer water go to Muizenberg or Fish Hoek. Arrive early for parking and avoid leaving bags unattended.

localTips.title: Load-shedding can affect plans
localTips.description: Ask your hotel for the schedule and pick cafés/restaurants with backup power for work or reservations. Keep a small power bank for your phone.

foodToTry.title: Gatsby sandwich
foodToTry.description: Share one—it's huge; try steak or masala steak from a classic takeaway. Best eaten fresh while the chips are crisp.

foodToTry.title: Cape Malay bobotie
foodToTry.description: A spiced mince bake with egg topping; order it with yellow rice and sambals. Great lunchtime dish around the City Bowl/Bo-Kaap.

foodToTry.title: Braai and boerewors
foodToTry.description: Look for a casual braai spot or weekend market; boerewors is the must-try sausage. Ask for chakalaka or pap on the side.

foodToTry.title: Koeksisters (Cape Malay style)
foodToTry.description: Go for the spiced, coconut-dusted version (different from the syrupy Afrikaner one). Buy early in the day from bakeries for the freshest batch.

gettingAround.title: Use Uber/Bolt for most trips
gettingAround.description: They’re generally easiest between the CBD, Sea Point, Camps Bay, and Constantia; confirm plate/driver before getting in. Avoid hailing random cars at night.

gettingAround.title: Rent a car for the Peninsula and wine days
gettingAround.description: Start early to avoid traffic and secure parking; keep doors locked and windows up at intersections. Never leave luggage visible—drop bags at your stay first.

gettingAround.title: MyCiTi bus for the Atlantic Seaboard
gettingAround.description: Reliable for CBD ↔ Sea Point ↔ Camps Bay routes; buy/recharge a myconnect card at stations. It’s best in daylight and for planned routes.

topThingsToDo.title: Nairobi National Park (sunrise game drive)
topThingsToDo.description: Go at gate-opening for the best wildlife sightings and cooler temps; book a 4x4 with a pop-up roof and carry a jacket for the morning chill.

topThingsToDo.title: Sheldrick Wildlife Trust (elephant orphanage)
topThingsToDo.description: Reserve online early (limited slots) and arrive 15–20 minutes before the viewing to get a front spot; bring sunglasses for the dust.

topThingsToDo.title: Giraffe Centre + early lunch in Karen
topThingsToDo.description: Visit on a weekday morning to avoid school crowds, then pair it with nearby Karen spots; keep small cash for donations and snacks.

topThingsToDo.title: Karura Forest walk/cycle
topThingsToDo.description: Enter via the main gate and stick to marked trails to the waterfall; rent a bike on-site and carry repellent for shady sections.

topThingsToDo.title: Nairobi National Museum + Snake Park
topThingsToDo.description: Do this on a rainy afternoon; hire an official museum guide at the entrance for context and time-saving highlights.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “taxi” offers outside malls/airport
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip drivers who approach you; use Uber/Bolt or your hotel’s known driver and confirm the plate and fare in-app before getting in.

scamsToAvoid.title: M-Pesa/phone “wrong number” or payment reversal tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t send money back to strangers; if a payment issue happens, contact the provider or the business directly and keep the SMS as proof.

scamsToAvoid.title: Curio bracelet/shoe-shine distraction in CBD
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone starts a “free” service, firmly say no and keep walking; avoid flashing cash and keep your phone out of sight on crowded streets.

localTips.title: Plan around traffic peaks
localTips.description: Avoid cross-city trips 7–9am and 4:30–7pm; cluster activities by area (Karen/Lang’ata vs Westlands vs CBD) to save hours.

localTips.title: Cash and small change still matter
localTips.description: Cards work in many places, but carry small notes for park fees, tips, and quick buys; ask “Do you take card?” before ordering.

localTips.title: Dress and carry smart in public
localTips.description: In busy areas keep your phone in a front pocket/bag and avoid wearing expensive jewelry; in upscale neighborhoods it’s fine but stay alert.

localTips.title: Sunday vibe and closures
localTips.description: Many offices and some shops shut early on Sunday; it’s a great day for parks, brunch in Westlands/Kilimani, and quieter museum visits.

foodToTry.title: Nyama choma + kachumbari
foodToTry.description: Order grilled goat or beef with fresh tomato-onion salsa; ask for the meat to be weighed before cooking and share family-style.

foodToTry.title: Ugali with sukuma wiki
foodToTry.description: A classic combo found everywhere; eat with your right hand and ask for “sukuma” less oily if you prefer lighter.

foodToTry.title: Githeri or mukimo
foodToTry.description: Hearty local staples (beans/maize stew or mashed greens/potato); try them at reputable cafeterias for a quick, inexpensive lunch.

foodToTry.title: Pilau and viazi karai (Swahili street bites)
foodToTry.description: Look for busy stalls with high turnover; go easy on the chili sauce first—heat levels vary a lot.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing (best for visitors)
gettingAround.description: Use Uber/Bolt/Little Cab, sit in the back, and share your trip; set pickup pins carefully at malls to avoid confusion.

gettingAround.title: Private driver for a full day
gettingAround.description: For Karen/Lang’ata + parks, hiring a driver is often cheaper than multiple rides and saves time; agree on hours, fuel, and waiting time upfront.

gettingAround.title: Matatus (only if you’re confident)
gettingAround.description: They’re fast and cheap but hectic; use them in daylight, keep valuables secured, and confirm route numbers with a local before boarding.

topThingsToDo.title: Stone Town at dawn + rooftop sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the lanes before 9am for cooler temps and fewer touts, then book a rooftop spot (Emerson on Hurumzi or 6 Degrees) 30–45 min before sunset.

topThingsToDo.title: Spice farm with a cooking stop
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a smaller farm near Kizimbani and ask for a short tour plus a Swahili lunch; negotiate price per person including transport before leaving town.

topThingsToDo.title: Snorkel Mnemba (timing matters)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early morning on a calm day from Matemwe/Nungwi and confirm you’ll snorkel outside the reserve boundary (fees vary); bring reef shoes for boat entries.

topThingsToDo.title: Jozani Forest + mangroves
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive right at opening to see red colobus before crowds; combine with the mangrove boardwalk and carry small cash for official tickets only.

topThingsToDo.title: Paje/Jambiani lagoon day (tides plan the beach)
topThingsToDo.description: Check the tide chart: low tide is best for walking sandbars and seaweed farms, high tide for swimming/kitesurf lessons; plan your beach time around it.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxi 'island tour' add-ons
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may push surprise stops/fees; agree on a fixed itinerary, total price, and fuel/parking included before you get in.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake 'official' fees in Stone Town
scamsToAvoid.description: Only pay at ticket windows for museums/attractions; ignore people claiming mandatory guide fees on the street.

scamsToAvoid.title: ATM/helpful stranger card tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Use ATMs inside banks in daylight and decline unsolicited help; cover your PIN and keep your card in your hand at all times.

localTips.title: Respect the call to prayer and dress norms
localTips.description: In towns/villages wear shoulders and knees covered; beachwear stays on the beach to avoid hassle and offense.

localTips.title: Carry small notes (TZS) and confirm currency
localTips.description: Many small places can’t break large bills; clarify if prices are in USD or TZS and agree before ordering/boarding.

localTips.title: Friday + Sunday planning
localTips.description: Friday midday is quieter with some closures, while Sunday has more local outings; book popular tours a day ahead in high season.

localTips.title: Mosquito timing
localTips.description: Bites spike at dusk near stagnant water; use repellent from 5pm, and check your room has a functioning net or request one.

foodToTry.title: Zanzibar pizza (Forodhani)
foodToTry.description: Order from the busiest stall at Forodhani Gardens after dark; watch it cooked and pay after you receive it.

foodToTry.title: Urojo (Zanzibar mix)
foodToTry.description: Try it mid-afternoon in Stone Town—tangy soup with fritters and chutneys; ask for “kidogo pilipili” if you want mild spice.

foodToTry.title: Octopus curry or grilled pweza
foodToTry.description: Best along the east coast (Jambiani/Paje); ask for it not overcooked and pair with coconut rice.

foodToTry.title: Sugarcane juice + tangawizi (ginger)
foodToTry.description: Get it fresh-pressed at night markets; request ginger and lime for a cleaner, less sweet taste.

gettingAround.title: Dala-dala (shared minibuses)
gettingAround.description: Cheapest for local routes but crowded; ask your guesthouse the exact stand and last departure time, and keep valuables zipped.

gettingAround.title: Taxis (negotiate once, then ride)
gettingAround.description: Agree the all-in fare before entering and confirm if it includes waiting time; have your hotel call a trusted driver when possible.

gettingAround.title: Scooter or car rental (only if confident)
gettingAround.description: Check brakes/tires, take a quick video of existing damage, and carry your license/permit; avoid night driving due to poor lighting and animals.

topThingsToDo.title: Valley of the Kings (early entry)
topThingsToDo.description: Be at the gates at opening to avoid heat and crowds; the standard ticket includes 3 tombs, so check the daily list and pick varied ones (e.g., Seti I is usually an extra ticket).

topThingsToDo.title: Hatshepsut Temple + Deir el-Medina combo
topThingsToDo.description: Do Hatshepsut first, then add Deir el-Medina for smaller, vividly painted tombs most tours skip; bring small change for site toilets and guards.

topThingsToDo.title: Karnak at golden hour + Luxor Temple at night
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Karnak late afternoon for better light and fewer tour groups, then go to Luxor Temple after dark when it’s dramatically lit and cooler.

topThingsToDo.title: West Bank bicycle loop (quiet villages and fields)
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike in Gezira/West Bank and ride to lesser-visited spots like Ramesseum or Medinet Habu; start before 9am and carry water.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise hot-air balloon (weather dependent)
topThingsToDo.description: Confirm exact pickup time and launch site the evening before; choose operators that mention limited passenger counts and avoid “too cheap to be true” deals.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Site is closed, come with me’ detour
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone claiming closures or “special entrances” and walk to the official ticket window; closures are posted at gates, not by random touts.

scamsToAvoid.title: Carriage/driver price switch
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree on total price, route, and duration before getting in, and confirm it’s not “per person” or “per hour” after the ride.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘official guide’ or forced tipping
scamsToAvoid.description: Licensed guides carry ID; if you don’t want a guide, say no firmly and don’t accept “free” help that turns into demanded baksheesh.

localTips.title: Split days by bank to save time
localTips.description: Do all East Bank sites in one block and West Bank in another; crossing the Nile repeatedly wastes hours in traffic and ferry waits.

localTips.title: Medinet Habu is the West Bank sleeper hit
localTips.description: It’s often quieter than the big names and has excellent wall reliefs; pair it with nearby Ramesseum to maximize the same ride.

localTips.title: Carry small bills for tickets, toilets, and tips
localTips.description: Many places can’t break large notes; keep 10–50 EGP notes handy to avoid awkward “no change” upsells.

localTips.title: Respect photography rules to avoid fines
localTips.description: Some tombs ban photos or require an extra photo ticket; don’t sneak shots—guards will stop you and can force deletion or charge on the spot.

foodToTry.title: Koshary
foodToTry.description: A filling local bowl of lentils, rice, pasta, and spicy tomato sauce; ask for extra fried onions and vinegar on the side.

foodToTry.title: Ta‘ameya (Egyptian falafel)
foodToTry.description: Made with fava beans, greener and fluffier than chickpea falafel; best eaten hot in a baladi bread sandwich.

foodToTry.title: Molokhia
foodToTry.description: Garlicky green soup/stew often served with chicken or rabbit; order it with rice and lemon to cut the richness.

foodToTry.title: Fresh sugarcane juice (asab)
foodToTry.description: Get it from a busy juicer so it’s freshly pressed; drink immediately and skip ice if you have a sensitive stomach.

gettingAround.title: Private driver for West Bank loops
gettingAround.description: Best value for multiple sites in one day; set a fixed itinerary and total price, and confirm the driver waits at each stop.

gettingAround.title: Nile ferry instead of motorboat
gettingAround.description: Use the public ferry for quick, cheap East–West crossings; pay the posted fare and avoid “tourist boat” quotes on the spot.

gettingAround.title: Taxis in town (meter-free reality)
gettingAround.description: Most don’t use meters, so negotiate before getting in; have your destination pinned in Arabic on your phone to avoid long detours.

topThingsToDo.title: Hassan II Mosque (book the interior tour)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early or late for softer light and fewer crowds; buy the official guided tour ticket on-site (non-Muslims need the tour) and dress modestly with socks for the marble floors.

topThingsToDo.title: Walk the Corniche & Ain Diab at sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Start near the Hassan II Mosque promenade and continue toward Ain Diab; stop for mint tea by the ocean and watch locals surf and stroll, especially on weekends.

topThingsToDo.title: Habous Quarter (New Medina) for shopping
topThingsToDo.description: Shop here instead of the Old Medina for better quality leather, ceramics, and books with less hassle; compare prices at 2–3 stalls before buying.

topThingsToDo.title: Marché Central for seafood lunch
topThingsToDo.description: Choose your fish at the stalls and have it grilled on the spot; ask the price per kilo before they weigh it and request a simple grill to avoid add-ons.

topThingsToDo.title: Art Deco downtown + Place Mohammed V
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll Boulevard Mohammed V to see colonial-era facades; pop into hidden passages and cafes, and time it for early evening when offices empty and streets feel lively.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial ‘guides’ in the medina
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone insists you’re going the “wrong way” and offers to lead you, decline firmly and keep walking; use offline maps and enter the Old Medina only with a plan.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi meter refusal and ‘broken meter’ story
scamsToAvoid.description: Insist on the meter (“compteur”) before getting in; if they won’t use it, step out and take the next red petit taxi.

scamsToAvoid.title: Inflated prices at ATM exchange/phone shops near tourist spots
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm fees and totals before handing over cash or cards; for SIMs and top-ups, use official carrier stores (Maroc Telecom/Orange/inwi).

localTips.title: Friday timing matters
localTips.description: Plan major errands and some restaurants outside Friday prayer time (around midday), when many places slow down or close briefly.

localTips.title: Cash is king for small buys
localTips.description: Carry small notes and coins for taxis, cafes, and markets; many places can’t break large bills, especially in the morning.

localTips.title: Use French key phrases
localTips.description: A quick “Bonjour” and “S’il vous plaît” often gets better service; many signs and menus are in French rather than English.

localTips.title: Dress codes at religious and upscale spots
localTips.description: For the mosque and nicer restaurants, avoid shorts and sleeveless tops; a light layer helps with sea breeze and indoor A/C.

foodToTry.title: Seafood grill (poisson du jour)
foodToTry.description: Best value at Marché Central or simple grills by the coast; ask for price per kilo and choose what you want cooked.

foodToTry.title: Pastilla
foodToTry.description: Try the classic pigeon/chicken with almond and cinnamon; order a small portion as it’s rich and often shareable.

foodToTry.title: Tajine (kefta or lemon-olive chicken)
foodToTry.description: Look for places serving it bubbling hot in clay; ask for “mzyan ma t7arrq” (not too spicy) if you’re sensitive.

foodToTry.title: Harira + chebakia
foodToTry.description: A comforting soup-and-sweet combo often served in the evenings; great for a light dinner when you don’t want a heavy tagine.

gettingAround.title: Petit taxis (red) for short trips
gettingAround.description: They’re for travel within the city; insist on the meter and have your destination pinned in maps to avoid confusion.

gettingAround.title: Tramway for easy, cheap cross-town rides
gettingAround.description: Buy a rechargeable card at stations and validate each ride; it’s reliable for downtown-to-neighborhood hops when traffic is bad.

gettingAround.title: ONCF trains for airport/nearby cities
gettingAround.description: Use Casa-Voyageurs or Casa-Port stations for Rabat, Tangier, and Marrakech connections; for the airport, follow the ONCF service to Mohammed V and leave extra time for security.

topThingsToDo.title: Get lost (smartly) in Fes el-Bali Medina
topThingsToDo.description: Start at Bab Boujloud and wander the Talaa Kebira/Talaa Sghira spine; pin your riad and 2–3 landmarks on offline maps so you can re-orient fast.

topThingsToDo.title: Al Quaraouiyine area + Medersa Bou Inania
topThingsToDo.description: You can’t enter the mosque as a non-Muslim, but the surrounding lanes are the soul of Fez; visit Bou Inania near late afternoon for softer light and fewer groups.

topThingsToDo.title: Tanneries viewpoint (Chouara)
topThingsToDo.description: Use a terrace with a posted price or confirm “free to look, no pressure to buy” before you go up; bring a mask or scarf—the smell can be intense.

topThingsToDo.title: Pottery and zellige in the artisans’ quarter
topThingsToDo.description: Go to Ain Nokbi (outside the medina) to watch kiln work and tile-cutting without the medina markup; ask to see the workshop before any showroom.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset at Borj Nord / Merenid Tombs overlook
topThingsToDo.description: For the best city panorama, go 45–60 minutes before sunset; take a petit taxi up and walk down if you’re comfortable with steps and uneven paths.

scamsToAvoid.title: The “I’ll guide you” trap
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone insists you’re lost, firmly say “La, shukran” and keep walking; only use officially arranged guides or your riad’s recommendation with a set fee.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tannery terrace pressure sales
scamsToAvoid.description: Some terraces funnel you through a shop and demand tips; agree on a small viewing fee (or none) before going up and leave if you’re blocked from exiting.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced taxi rides and fake meters
scamsToAvoid.description: Most petit taxis don’t use meters reliably—agree on the fare before getting in, especially from the station/airport, and keep small bills to avoid “no change.”

localTips.title: Medina navigation hack
localTips.description: Drop a pin at Bab Boujloud, your riad, and one major landmark (Bou Inania or Nejjarine); the medina’s side alleys look identical after dark.
