localTips.title: Best time to visit popular sights
localTips.description: Go early (9–10am) for quiet lanes and photos; many shops open late, and afternoons can feel crowded with tour groups.

localTips.title: Shopping like locals
localTips.description: For spices/olive oil, buy from busy neighborhood hanout shops, not only tourist streets; ask for prices per 100g to compare fairly.

localTips.title: Respectful dress and access expectations
localTips.description: Light, covered shoulders/legs reduces hassle and is appreciated; remember most historic mosques are viewable from doors only for non-Muslims.

foodToTry.title: Bissara
foodToTry.description: Thick fava-bean soup topped with olive oil and cumin—best as a warm breakfast in simple medina cafes.

foodToTry.title: Pastilla (bastilla)
foodToTry.description: Sweet-salty pigeon or chicken pie with almonds and cinnamon; order a small one to share because it’s rich.

foodToTry.title: Rfissa
foodToTry.description: Shredded msemen with lentils, fenugreek, and chicken—often a Friday/Sunday-style home dish; ask your riad if they can arrange it.

foodToTry.title: Mechoui
foodToTry.description: Slow-roasted lamb sold by weight in the medina; go early afternoon when it’s freshest and ask for a mix of crisp and tender pieces.

gettingAround.title: Walking in the medina
gettingAround.description: Most of Fes el-Bali is car-free; wear grippy shoes and step aside for mules/carts—hug walls on narrow alleys to let loads pass.

gettingAround.title: Petit taxis (inside newer city areas)
gettingAround.description: Good for Ville Nouvelle, Borj Nord, and Ain Nokbi; agree on the price before departure and avoid taking the front seat if you want fewer “shared ride” surprises.

gettingAround.title: Airport and long transfers
gettingAround.description: For FES airport or day trips (Meknes/Volubilis/Ifrane), pre-arrange a fare with your riad or use a reputable app/driver; it’s usually cheaper than negotiating on arrival.

topThingsToDo.title: Jamestown & Chale Wote-style street art walk
topThingsToDo.description: Go with a local guide for the lighthouse, boxing gyms, and murals; late afternoon light is best and the neighborhood feels calmer than mid-day.

topThingsToDo.title: Makola Market essentials run
topThingsToDo.description: Shop for fabrics, shea, spices, and baskets early (9–11am) before peak heat; keep small cash and ask prices at 2–3 stalls before buying.

topThingsToDo.title: Osu: food crawl + nightlife
topThingsToDo.description: Start with street snacks around Oxford Street, then move to a lounge/rooftop; weekdays are easier for seating and parking.

topThingsToDo.title: Black Star Square & Independence Arch
topThingsToDo.description: Visit at sunrise or just before sunset for photos with fewer crowds; combine with a quick stop at the nearby Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park.

topThingsToDo.title: Beach day at Labadi (or a quieter alternative)
topThingsToDo.description: Labadi is lively on weekends—agree on chair/umbrella price upfront; for calmer vibes, go earlier or choose less-busy stretches toward the east.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi “broken meter” or inflated foreigner price
scamsToAvoid.description: Most taxis don’t use meters—confirm the full fare before you enter, or use a ride-hailing app to lock price and route.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overfriendly “guides” at markets/attractions
scamsToAvoid.description: Some helpers steer you to overpriced shops for commission; politely decline, keep walking, and hire a guide only through a verified tour/operator.

scamsToAvoid.title: Currency-switching and short-change
scamsToAvoid.description: Count notes in front of the seller and avoid letting anyone handle your cash stack; for exchanges, use banks/official forex bureaus, not street offers.

localTips.title: Time your day around traffic
localTips.description: Accra congestion spikes 7–10am and 4–7pm; plan major cross-town moves midday or after 7:30pm.

localTips.title: Carry small denominations
localTips.description: Markets and tro-tros often can’t break large notes; keep mixed small bills to avoid “no change” pricing.

localTips.title: Dress code cues
localTips.description: Lightweight modest clothing is appreciated in markets and public areas; bring a light layer for strong A/C in malls and restaurants.

localTips.title: Stay connected and share location
localTips.description: Buy a local SIM/eSIM for maps and ride-hailing; when meeting drivers or guides, share live location instead of describing landmarks.

foodToTry.title: Jollof rice (Ghana style)
foodToTry.description: Try it with grilled chicken or fish and shito; go earlier in the day when popular spots haven’t sold out.

foodToTry.title: Waakye
foodToTry.description: A hearty breakfast/lunch of rice and beans with stew, gari, spaghetti, and egg; ask for “small” first—portions are big.

foodToTry.title: Kenkey with fried fish
foodToTry.description: Sour corn dough dumplings served with pepper and onions; eat at busy stalls where turnover is high and fish is freshly fried.

foodToTry.title: Banku with tilapia (or okra stew)
foodToTry.description: A classic pairing at beachside grills; confirm the fish price by size/weight before it hits the fire.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing apps
gettingAround.description: Use Bolt/Uber/Yango for predictable pricing; set pickup at a clear landmark (hotel gate, major shop) to reduce cancellations.

gettingAround.title: Taxis (street or call-in)
gettingAround.description: Negotiate the total fare before entering and clarify whether it’s “drop” (solo) or “shared”; keep your route open on maps for peace of mind.

gettingAround.title: Tro-tros for short, cheap hops
gettingAround.description: Best for daytime and simple routes; ask “station for [place]?” and have exact change—routes aren’t posted consistently.

topThingsToDo.title: National Museum of Ethiopia
topThingsToDo.description: Go early to avoid school-group crowds and spend time on the hominid hall (Lucy) and modern art upstairs; guides are optional but helpful for context.

topThingsToDo.title: Merkato (with a local fixer)
topThingsToDo.description: Visit with a trusted local/guide and a clear shopping list; stick to main lanes and use cash in small notes for quick purchases.

topThingsToDo.title: Mount Entoto viewpoints + churches
topThingsToDo.description: Take a morning trip for clearer views and cooler air; bring a light jacket and combine with a quick stop at a traditional coffee stall.

topThingsToDo.title: Holy Trinity Cathedral & museum
topThingsToDo.description: Dress modestly and time it around a service to hear the choir; the small museum gives great context on modern Ethiopian history.

topThingsToDo.title: Coffee ceremony in a neighborhood café
topThingsToDo.description: Skip hotel versions and go to a busy local spot in Bole or Piazza; ask for a full ceremony (abol, tona, bereka) and take your time.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi price switching or ‘meter’ theatrics
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree the total fare before getting in (or use a ride-hailing app); if the price changes on arrival, pay the agreed amount and walk away calmly.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Helpful’ strangers leading you to shops/ATMs
scamsToAvoid.description: Politely decline unsolicited help, especially near Merkato and busy intersections; use bank ATMs inside branches or malls, not street-side machines.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced tours and “special access” claims
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone offers exclusive museum/church entry or last-minute permits, verify at the official ticket window; book day trips through reputable hotels or known operators.

localTips.title: Carry small birr and a backup payment plan
localTips.description: Many places struggle with change and card networks can be spotty; keep 50/100 birr notes and withdraw during daytime at bank branches.

localTips.title: Plan around traffic and altitude
localTips.description: Addis sits around 2,300m—take it easy the first day and schedule cross-town trips outside rush hours (roughly 7–9am, 4–7pm).

localTips.title: Use a few Amharic basics
localTips.description: A simple “Selam” (hello) and “Amesegenallo” (thank you) improves interactions; ask “Sint new?” to confirm prices before ordering or buying.

localTips.title: Dress and behavior in religious sites
localTips.description: Bring a scarf/light wrap for churches; avoid photos during services and follow local cues for where to stand and when to remove shoes.

foodToTry.title: Injera with tibs
foodToTry.description: Order sizzling tibs (meat) served on injera for a classic first meal; ask for “mild” if you’re not used to berbere spice.

foodToTry.title: Beyaynetu (vegetarian platter)
foodToTry.description: Great on fasting days and widely available; choose a busy spot so the lentils and greens are fresh and not sitting out too long.

foodToTry.title: Kitfo
foodToTry.description: Try it at a reputable restaurant and specify “leb leb” (lightly cooked) if you prefer; pair with ayib (fresh cheese) and gomen (greens).

foodToTry.title: Tej or local beers (St. George, Habesha)
foodToTry.description: Tej (honey wine) is best in traditional tej bets—taste first because sweetness varies; local beers are easy, reliable options with spicy dishes.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing apps (recommended)
gettingAround.description: Use apps like Ride or Feres for clearer pricing and less haggling; keep some cash because drivers may prefer it even on app trips.

gettingAround.title: Blue-and-white minibuses
gettingAround.description: Fast and cheap but confusing—ask your hotel to write your destination in Amharic and confirm the route before you board.

gettingAround.title: Light Rail (LRT)
gettingAround.description: Useful for a few corridors when traffic is bad; avoid peak crush times and keep valuables secured in crowds and at stations.

topThingsToDo.title: Harbour ferry hop (Manly + Watsons Bay)
topThingsToDo.description: Use public ferries for the best-value harbour cruise: Circular Quay to Manly for a beach day, then try Watsons Bay for sunset views and the short South Head walk.

topThingsToDo.title: Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (before 9am) to beat crowds and heat; detour down to Gordon’s Bay for a quieter swim and snorkel.

topThingsToDo.title: Sydney Opera House tour or a cheap performance
topThingsToDo.description: Book a guided tour for backstage context, or look for last-minute/weekday performances for better prices than peak weekend shows.

topThingsToDo.title: The Rocks laneways + weekend markets
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the historic backstreets (Nurses Walk, Suez Canal) and time it for The Rocks Markets (weekends) for local crafts and snacks without CBD mall vibes.

topThingsToDo.title: Blue Mountains day trip (Katoomba + Wentworth Falls)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the train to Katoomba, then use local buses to viewpoints; start at Wentworth Falls for better walks and fewer tour groups than the Three Sisters mid-day rush.

scamsToAvoid.title: Harbour “tour” upsells at Circular Quay
scamsToAvoid.description: Some operators pitch pricey cruises on the spot; compare with regular Opal ferries first, which cover most iconic views for a fraction of the cost.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed rides and inflated taxi fares late-night
scamsToAvoid.description: Stick to official taxis (meter on) or reputable rideshare; avoid anyone offering cash rides outside venues or at rank exits.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced souvenir shops in The Rocks
scamsToAvoid.description: Check labels for made-in-Australia if that matters, and price-compare with local markets or museum shops to avoid tourist markups.

localTips.title: Swim between the flags
localTips.description: Sydney surf can be deceptively strong; always choose patrolled sections and check Surf Life Saving signage before entering.

localTips.title: Book beach parking and popular restaurants ahead
localTips.description: Bondi/Manly parking fills fast and pricey; use public transport and reserve standout spots (especially Fri–Sun) to avoid long queues.

localTips.title: Tap water and public facilities are excellent
localTips.description: Carry a bottle—CBD, beaches, and parks have drink fountains and clean public toilets (often near surf clubs).

localTips.title: Mind the sun even on cloudy days
localTips.description: UV is high year-round; buy SPF 50+ locally and reapply before coastal walks or ferry days.

foodToTry.title: Modern Aussie brunch
foodToTry.description: Try a flat white with smashed avo or corn fritters; go midweek in Surry Hills or Newtown to dodge weekend lines.

foodToTry.title: Barramundi or fish and chips by the water
foodToTry.description: Order barramundi (grilled or battered) and eat it seaside at Manly or Watsons Bay for the full Sydney feel.

foodToTry.title: Meat pie and sausage roll from a good bakery
foodToTry.description: Grab one for an easy lunch; look for flaky pastry and fresh batches (ask what’s just come out of the oven).

foodToTry.title: Lebanese charcoal chicken and mezze
foodToTry.description: Head to the inner west for chicken, toum, tabbouleh, and fresh bread—great value and a true local staple.

gettingAround.title: Use Opal or contactless tap-on/tap-off
gettingAround.description: Tap a card/phone on trains, buses, ferries, and light rail; always tap off to avoid default fares and keep one card per person.

gettingAround.title: Ferries are transport and sightseeing
gettingAround.description: Sit outside on the left side leaving Circular Quay for Harbour Bridge/Opera House views; ferries are often faster than driving to beach suburbs.

gettingAround.title: Skip driving in the CBD
gettingAround.description: Traffic, tolled roads, and expensive parking add up; take the train to Town Hall/Wynyard and walk or light rail for city sights.

topThingsToDo.title: Laneways street art + coffee crawl (CBD)
topThingsToDo.description: Start early at Hosier Lane then cut through Degraves/Hardware Lane for espresso; go before 10am to avoid tour groups and get fresh murals.

topThingsToDo.title: NGV International + NGV Australia (free highlights)
topThingsToDo.description: Hit NGV International’s water-wall entrance, then walk across to Ian Potter Centre (Fed Square) for Australian art; both have strong free sections.

topThingsToDo.title: Queen Victoria Market (best times + what to buy)
topThingsToDo.description: Go Wed/Fri mornings for locals’ pace; grab fresh borek, seasonal fruit, and smallgoods—ask for tasters before you buy.

topThingsToDo.title: St Kilda to Brighton coastal ride
topThingsToDo.description: Rent a bike near St Kilda and follow the Bay Trail to Brighton Bathing Boxes; go on a weekday and return by train from Brighton Beach station if tired.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip: Great Ocean Road (smart routing)
topThingsToDo.description: Drive/coach west via inland route first, then return along the coast for the best daylight at the Twelve Apostles; pack layers—weather flips fast.

scamsToAvoid.title: Card surcharge surprises
scamsToAvoid.description: Some venues add 1–2% card fees and 10–15% weekend/public-holiday surcharges; check the menu fine print before ordering.

scamsToAvoid.title: Myki fare traps
scamsToAvoid.description: Touch on AND off trains/trams/buses (except trams within the Free Tram Zone); failing to do so can mean a default fare and possible fine.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed ride offers outside venues
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore drivers soliciting rides after events; use the official taxi rank, rideshare app pickup points, or Night Network services.

localTips.title: Use the Free Tram Zone strategically
localTips.description: Hop trams free within the CBD to move between Flinders, Docklands, Queen Vic Market and Parliament; once you leave the zone you must have a valid touch-on.

localTips.title: Weather: dress for “four seasons”
localTips.description: Carry a light rain jacket and an extra layer even in summer; wind off the bay can drop temps quickly in the evening.

localTips.title: Book restaurants like a local
localTips.description: For popular spots, reserve 1–2 weeks out (especially Thu–Sat); walk-ins work best at 5–6pm or after 8:30pm.

localTips.title: Best skyline views without a ticket
localTips.description: For quick, free views, try the Bolte Bridge lookouts at Docklands or the Shrine of Remembrance forecourt at sunset.

foodToTry.title: Melbourne flat white (or magic)
foodToTry.description: Order a flat white for the classic, or ask for a “magic” (double ristretto with textured milk) at specialty cafes in the CBD/Fitzroy.

foodToTry.title: Vietnamese pho + banh mi (Richmond)
foodToTry.description: Head to Victoria Street for late-night pho and crisp banh mi; go hungry and compare two spots—locals do.

foodToTry.title: Greek souvlaki (CBD)
foodToTry.description: Try a proper souvlaki after dark around Swanston Street/Greek precinct; expect a queue—service moves fast.

foodToTry.title: Modern Australian small plates (Fitzroy/Collingwood)
foodToTry.description: Book a set menu for best value and variety; many kitchens focus on seasonal produce and natural wines.

gettingAround.title: Myki basics
gettingAround.description: Buy a Myki at 7‑Eleven or stations and top up via the PTV app; touching on caps your daily fare, so it’s usually not worth single tickets.

gettingAround.title: Trams and etiquette
gettingAround.description: Signal trams at stops (they won’t always stop automatically) and keep left on platforms; let passengers off before boarding.

gettingAround.title: Airport to city (best options)
gettingAround.description: SkyBus to Southern Cross is the simplest; rideshare/taxi is faster off-peak but pricey—compare in-app before you land.

topThingsToDo.title: Ferry to Waiheke Island (wine + beaches)
topThingsToDo.description: Take the Downtown ferry early, then use the local bus or e-bike to hit 2–3 vineyards plus Oneroa/Onetangi Beach; book tastings ahead on summer weekends.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike Rangitoto at sunrise or late afternoon
topThingsToDo.description: Catch a ferry to Rangitoto and do the summit loop for skyline views; bring water and sun protection—there’s little shade on the volcanic rock.

topThingsToDo.title: West Coast black-sand beaches (Piha/Karekare/Muriwai)
topThingsToDo.description: Go for dramatic surf and cliffs; swim only between flags because rips are serious, and check road conditions after heavy rain.

topThingsToDo.title: Tāmaki Drive + Mission Bay to St Heliers
topThingsToDo.description: Walk or rent a bike for an easy waterfront route; stop for a quick swim or fish and chips, and avoid peak traffic by going before 10am or after 6pm.

topThingsToDo.title: Auckland War Memorial Museum + Domain
topThingsToDo.description: Start with the Māori galleries and volcano exhibits, then picnic in the Domain; time it for a kapa haka performance if scheduled.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial airport taxi overcharging
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore drivers approaching inside the terminal; use the official taxi rank, pre-booked shuttles, or ride-hail from the designated pickup area.

scamsToAvoid.title: Facebook/Marketplace accommodation deposits
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t pay a deposit via bank transfer for short-term rentals without verified booking protection; reverse-image search listings and insist on a secure platform.

scamsToAvoid.title: Car break-ins at trailheads and beaches
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t leave bags in the car (even in the boot) at spots like Piha and popular lookout carparks; take valuables with you or use secure parking.

localTips.title: Weather changes fast—pack layers
localTips.description: Carry a light rain shell and a warm layer even in summer; wind and showers can roll in quickly, especially near the harbours and west coast.

localTips.title: Book ferries and popular dinners ahead
localTips.description: Waiheke ferries, island buses, and top CBD restaurants fill up on Fridays and summer weekends; reserve online and aim for early sailings.

localTips.title: Plan around rush-hour bridges and motorways
localTips.description: Avoid driving 7–9am and 4–6pm if crossing the Harbour Bridge; consider ferries for the easiest CBD-to-shore commute.

localTips.title: Respect local tikanga (customs) at marae and cultural sites
localTips.description: If you join a cultural visit, follow the host’s guidance (shoes off when asked, no food in sacred areas) and ask before photographing people or carvings.

foodToTry.title: Hāngi-inspired meals
foodToTry.description: Try a modern hāngi plate or pie for smoky, earthy flavors; look for Māori-run kitchens or cultural events for the most authentic versions.

foodToTry.title: Fresh green-lipped mussels and local oysters
foodToTry.description: Order them at a waterfront spot or a good seafood bar; they’re best in-season and often served simply with lemon and mignonette.

foodToTry.title: Kiwi flat white and café brunch
foodToTry.description: Auckland takes coffee seriously—order a flat white and a cabinet slice, and go early on weekends to avoid long waits.

foodToTry.title: Pacific Island flavors in Ōtāhuhu or Avondale
foodToTry.description: Seek out samoan/korean/tongan-influenced street food and bakery treats; weekend markets are the easiest way to sample widely.

gettingAround.title: Use an AT HOP card for buses, trains, and ferries
gettingAround.description: Buy/top up at stations or convenience stores; tag on/off every trip to avoid maximum fares and to get cheaper transfers.

gettingAround.title: Ferries are often faster than driving
gettingAround.description: From Downtown, ferries to Devonport, Waiheke, and some shore routes can beat peak traffic; arrive 15–20 minutes early for popular sailings.

gettingAround.title: Driving: watch parking rules and beach roads
gettingAround.description: CBD parking is pricey and time-limited—use buildings or park-and-ride; on west-coast roads drive cautiously and don’t rely on late-night fuel stops.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise at Bob’s Peak (via Skyline Gondola or Tiki Trail)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for fewer crowds and clear views over Lake Wakatipu; book the gondola ahead in peak season or hike the Tiki Trail if you want to skip lines.

topThingsToDo.title: Glenorchy day trip (scenic drive + short walks)
topThingsToDo.description: Drive the lakeside road to Glenorchy and do Bob’s Cove or the Lagoon Walkway; start before 9am to avoid tour-bus congestion and limited parking.

topThingsToDo.title: Shotover Jet (or Kawarau Jet for a smoother ride)
topThingsToDo.description: Pick Shotover for tight canyon turns; book the first sessions for calmer water and bring a waterproof layer even in summer.

topThingsToDo.title: Day hike: Ben Lomond Saddle or Queenstown Hill
topThingsToDo.description: Ben Lomond Saddle gives the best payoff without committing to the summit; carry layers—weather changes fast and the top gets windy.

topThingsToDo.title: Arrowtown half-day (history + Autumn colors)
topThingsToDo.description: Wander the heritage main street and the Chinese Settlement; arrive midweek for easy parking and skip pricey Queenstown gift shops.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial ‘discount’ adventure bookings
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid random street/online resellers offering huge discounts; book direct or through i-SITE for clear cancellation and safety/operator details.

scamsToAvoid.title: Parking fines from ‘almost free’ spots
scamsToAvoid.description: Check signage carefully—many areas are time-limited or permit-only; use the council parking machines/app rather than guessing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced airport transfers on arrival
scamsToAvoid.description: Some shuttles/taxis upsell fixed fares; compare with the bus or pre-booked shuttles and confirm total price before loading luggage.

localTips.title: Book key activities early (especially summer + ski season)
localTips.description: Popular time slots sell out days ahead; lock in gondola, jet boats, Milford day tours, and ski lessons as soon as dates are set.

localTips.title: Plan for rapid weather swings
localTips.description: Carry a packable rain layer and warm mid-layer year-round; mountain forecasts can differ from town by several degrees.

localTips.title: Best lakefront moment without crowds
localTips.description: Walk the Frankton Track at dusk for calm water and Remarkables views; start from Frankton Marina for easier parking.

localTips.title: Save money with supermarket + picnic viewpoints
localTips.description: Grab supplies in Frankton (usually cheaper than town) and picnic at Sunshine Bay or Kelvin Heights for views without restaurant prices.

foodToTry.title: Fergburger (or go off-peak)
foodToTry.description: Iconic, but queues get long—go mid-afternoon or late evening; consider pre-order/nearby alternatives if you’re tight on time.

foodToTry.title: Southland lamb
foodToTry.description: Look for lamb shoulder, rack, or pies—great after a cold day; book dinner in advance on weekends.

foodToTry.title: Green-lipped mussels
foodToTry.description: Often served in creamy sauces or with fries; best paired with local white wine in a lakeside pub.

foodToTry.title: Pavlova or hokey pokey gelato
foodToTry.description: Classic Kiwi sweets—try a café pav or grab gelato for a quick treat between activities.

gettingAround.title: Walk the core, avoid driving in the center
gettingAround.description: Central streets are busy and parking is scarce; stay near the lakefront if you want to walk to most restaurants and tours.

gettingAround.title: Use local buses for Frankton, Arrowtown links, and the airport
gettingAround.description: Buses are the best-value option for short hops; tap on/off with a Bee Card where available and check timetables as evening frequency drops.

gettingAround.title: Rent a car only for day trips (and start early)
gettingAround.description: A car shines for Glenorchy, Wanaka, and scenic lookouts; leave town before 8–9am to beat traffic and secure parking at trailheads.

topThingsToDo.title: Snorkel the Yasawa or Mamanuca reefs
topThingsToDo.description: Base on a smaller island (not just Denarau) and snorkel straight off the beach at high tide; bring reef shoes for coral and urchins.

topThingsToDo.title: Do a village visit and kava (yaqona) ceremony
topThingsToDo.description: Go with a reputable operator or stay at a village homestay; bring a small sevusevu gift (bundle of yaqona root) and dress modestly (shoulders/knees covered).

topThingsToDo.title: Surf Cloudbreak or watch from Tavarua/Namotu area
topThingsToDo.description: Strong currents and sharp reef—book a licensed boat transfer and go with an experienced guide; non-surfers can snorkel nearby while sets roll through.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike and swim at Bouma National Heritage Park (Taveuni)
topThingsToDo.description: Start early for the Tavoro Falls trail to beat crowds and humidity; pack a dry bag and cash for entry and local guides.

topThingsToDo.title: Lagoon cruise to the Sawa-i-Lau Caves (Yasawas)
topThingsToDo.description: Time it for calm seas and ask your skipper about tide/visibility; bring a headlamp or waterproof light for the inner chamber swim.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxi “no meter” pricing
scamsToAvoid.description: At Nadi/Suva, insist on the meter or agree a total price before getting in; take a photo of the taxi number if anything feels off.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘island day tour’ upsells at the port
scamsToAvoid.description: Compare with direct operator rates online or at your hotel desk; confirm what’s included (lunch, gear, landing fees) in writing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Timeshare-style ‘free gift’ or ‘tour voucher’ pitches
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone offers freebies for attending a “short talk,” expect hard selling and time loss—politely decline and walk away.

localTips.title: Respect Sunday quiet hours
localTips.description: Many villages and some shops close or slow down—stock up Saturday and keep noise low near residential areas.

localTips.title: Know the greeting and a few basics
localTips.description: Say “Bula” (hello) and “Vinaka” (thank you); it opens doors and often gets you better service and local help.

localTips.title: Cash is king off the main island
localTips.description: ATMs can be scarce or empty on outer islands—carry small notes for boats, entrance fees, and village donations.

localTips.title: Pack for sandflies and reef protection
localTips.description: Sandflies hit at dusk—use repellent and cover ankles; use reef-safe sunscreen and rinse gear to avoid coral cuts getting infected.

foodToTry.title: Kokoda
foodToTry.description: Fijian ceviche with coconut cream and lime—best at small local eateries; ask for it “not too spicy” if needed.

foodToTry.title: Lovo feast
foodToTry.description: Earth-oven meat, fish, and root crops—book on a night your resort or village actually fires the lovo (often 1–2 times/week).

foodToTry.title: Rourou
foodToTry.description: Taro leaves in coconut cream; pair with cassava or dalo for a filling, inexpensive local meal.

foodToTry.title: Fiji-Indian curry and roti
foodToTry.description: Try a dhal curry or goat curry at a busy lunchtime spot in Nadi/Lautoka; order a side of roti or rice and a ginger beer.

gettingAround.title: Inter-island travel (boats/planes)
gettingAround.description: Use reputable fast ferries to Yasawas/Mamanucas and pad schedules for weather; for far islands, compare small flights vs overnight ferries for time and comfort.

gettingAround.title: On Viti Levu: local buses and minibuses
gettingAround.description: Cheap and frequent on main corridors—carry exact change and expect slower trips; sit on the right side for coastal views on the Coral Coast.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and ride-hailing alternatives
gettingAround.description: Taxis are common—ask for meter and have small bills; in some areas, hotels can arrange trusted drivers which reduces haggling and delays.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise at Marine Drive + Girgaum Chowpatty
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (6–8am) for a quiet walk, local breakfasts, and great photos before traffic and haze build up.

topThingsToDo.title: Gateway of India + Colaba backstreets
topThingsToDo.description: See the Gateway at dawn to avoid crowds, then wander behind Colaba Causeway for street art, cafés, and heritage lanes.

topThingsToDo.title: Ferries to Elephanta Caves
topThingsToDo.description: Take the first boat from Gateway for cooler weather; carry water and skip pushy guides unless you agree on a fixed fee.

topThingsToDo.title: Kala Ghoda + CST/Heritage precinct walk
topThingsToDo.description: Do a self-guided architecture loop (CST, BMC, Horniman Circle) in late afternoon; many buildings look best at golden hour.

topThingsToDo.title: Sassoon Dock fish market (early) + Mohammed Ali Road (late)
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Sassoon Dock at 6–8am for the auction vibe, then do Mohammed Ali Road after 8pm for peak street-food energy.

scamsToAvoid.title: Taxi/auto meter “not working”
scamsToAvoid.description: Insist on meter (or use Uber/Ola); if they refuse, walk 20 meters and take the next one.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake ‘closed’ attractions + redirect to shops
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone claims a site is closed and offers an alternative, ignore them and verify via Google/official listings yourself.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘special’ ferry/guide at Gateway
scamsToAvoid.description: Buy ferry tickets only from the official counter and confirm return timing; agree guide rates upfront or skip.

localTips.title: Plan around local train rush hours
localTips.description: Avoid 8–11am and 5–9pm on weekdays if you’re not commuting; mid-day rides are far calmer.

localTips.title: Dress for temples and upscale areas
localTips.description: Carry a light scarf; some temples require covered shoulders and you’ll want it for strong AC in malls/restaurants.

localTips.title: Cash + UPI both matter
localTips.description: Many small stalls prefer UPI; keep some cash for taxis, tips, and places with patchy signal.

localTips.title: Timing beats traffic
localTips.description: Cross-town cabs can take 60–120 minutes; group sights by area (South Mumbai vs Bandra/Juhu) to save hours.

foodToTry.title: Vada pav
foodToTry.description: Try it fresh from a busy stall; ask for “less spicy” if you’re sensitive and add dry garlic chutney carefully.

foodToTry.title: Pav bhaji
foodToTry.description: Best in the evening; request “extra pav” and a squeeze of lime—locals judge it by the buttery toasted bread.

foodToTry.title: Bombay sandwich
foodToTry.description: Order it grilled with chutney; it’s a perfect quick lunch while shopping in Colaba/Bandra.

foodToTry.title: Seafood thali / koli-style fry
foodToTry.description: Choose places with high turnover near the coast; ask what’s fresh that day rather than ordering specific fish.

gettingAround.title: Local trains (fastest on main corridors)
gettingAround.description: Use first-class for comfort on longer rides, and stand near the door only if you’re confident—platforms get crowded.

gettingAround.title: Metro (clean, predictable for select routes)
gettingAround.description: Great for avoiding traffic where it runs; buy a card/token and expect last-mile via rickshaw or short walk.

gettingAround.title: Uber/Ola + autos for last-mile
gettingAround.description: Use apps for longer trips and autos for short hops (metered); screenshot pickup points because GPS can drift in dense areas.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise at a quiet beach (South Goa)
topThingsToDo.description: Go to Agonda/Patnem before 7am for empty sands and calmer water; carry cash as shacks open later.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Goa churches + Latin Quarter walk
topThingsToDo.description: Do Basilica of Bom Jesus early to beat tour buses, then stroll Fontainhas in Panjim for Portuguese-era lanes and cafés.

topThingsToDo.title: Dolphin spot + sea swim (smartly)
topThingsToDo.description: Book small-boat trips from Sinquerim/Candolim at dawn for better sightings; insist on life jackets and skip overcrowded boats.

topThingsToDo.title: Spice plantation lunch near Ponda
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a plantation that includes a guided walk and Goan thali; go late morning and avoid peak weekend rush.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset viewpoints without the chaos
topThingsToDo.description: Try Cabo de Rama fort or Chapora’s quieter edges; arrive 45 minutes before sunset and park a short walk away to avoid jams.

scamsToAvoid.title: Inflated taxi fares and 'no meter' games
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree the fare before entering or use app-based cabs where available; for airport runs, prebook or use prepaid counters.

scamsToAvoid.title: Beach shack bill padding
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask for a printed menu and confirm taxes/service charges before ordering; check the bill item-by-item, especially for seafood by weight.

scamsToAvoid.title: Timeshare/party ticket touts
scamsToAvoid.description: Skip anyone offering “free” drinks, VIP entries, or resort presentations; buy event tickets only from official pages/venues.

localTips.title: Pick your coast based on vibe
localTips.description: North (Candolim–Anjuna) is busy and nightlife-heavy; South (Palolem–Agonda) is quieter and better for slow days.

localTips.title: Swim where lifeguards and flags are present
localTips.description: Rip currents happen even in calm-looking water; avoid swimming after dark and don’t swim near river mouths.

localTips.title: Carry small cash and a power bank
localTips.description: Many shacks/taxis prefer cash and ATMs can run dry on weekends; signal can be patchy in some beach belts.

localTips.title: Dress for church/temple visits
localTips.description: Carry a light scarf or shirt to cover shoulders and knees; mornings are cooler and less crowded for heritage sights.

foodToTry.title: Fish thali (Goan style)
foodToTry.description: Order at a local lunch spot for the best value; expect rice, curry, fried fish, sol kadi, and seasonal sides.

foodToTry.title: Prawn Balchão or Vindaloo
foodToTry.description: Ask for spice level—traditional versions can be punchy; pairs well with poi (local bread) or rice.

foodToTry.title: Bebinca
foodToTry.description: Try a fresh slice from a Goan bakery or dessert shop; it’s rich, so share if you’re sampling multiple sweets.

foodToTry.title: Feni cocktail (cashew or coconut)
foodToTry.description: Go for a simple feni-lime-soda first to gauge the flavor; buy sealed bottles from reputable stores if taking home.

gettingAround.title: Rent a scooter (with checks)
gettingAround.description: Photograph the bike, test brakes/lights, and confirm fuel policy; always carry license and wear a helmet (police checks are common).

gettingAround.title: Use local buses for cheap hops
gettingAround.description: Buses are frequent on main routes (Panjim–Mapusa–Margao); ask the conductor for the stop and keep small change.

gettingAround.title: Taxis for late nights and longer day trips
gettingAround.description: Negotiate a full-day rate for sightseeing with waiting included; save driver WhatsApp numbers for reliable return rides.

topThingsToDo.title: Amber Fort early + Panna Meena ka Kund
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening to beat crowds and heat; pair Amber with the nearby stepwell for photos and calmer vibes before tour buses roll in.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise at Nahargarh Fort
topThingsToDo.description: Go before dawn for the best city panorama; bring a light jacket in winter and avoid late-night stops if you’re solo.

topThingsToDo.title: City Palace + hidden courtyards
topThingsToDo.description: Buy the combined ticket if you want royal textiles/arms; time it for late afternoon light in the painted doorways and courtyards.

topThingsToDo.title: Hawa Mahal from the inside (and the best view of it)
topThingsToDo.description: Step inside for the breeze and lattice windows; for the classic façade photo, cross to the rooftop cafés opposite in the morning.

topThingsToDo.title: Old City bazaars with a purpose route
topThingsToDo.description: Do a loop: Johari Bazaar (gems), Tripolia (lac bangles), Bapu (textiles); ask for ‘fixed price’ shops or negotiate once, then walk.

scamsToAvoid.title: ‘Government’ gem/handicraft shop detours
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers may insist on a “government emporium” with commissions; refuse firmly and stick to your planned stops or use ride-hailing point-to-point.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake closed attraction / ticket help
scamsToAvoid.description: Strangers claim forts are closed or offer to ‘help’ buy tickets; ignore and purchase only at official counters/official websites.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘special’ tuk-tuk tours
scamsToAvoid.description: A cheap first quote often turns into add-ons (parking, guide, waiting); agree on a written all-in price and exact itinerary before starting.

localTips.title: Pick smart visiting hours
localTips.description: Most sights are best 8–11am and 4–6pm; midday is harsh—use it for museums, cafés, or a spa.

localTips.title: Skip elephant rides at Amber
localTips.description: Choose the jeep up to the fort instead; it’s quicker, kinder, and avoids long queues.

localTips.title: Plan for Friday crowds and festival surges
localTips.description: Market lanes and temples get packed on Fridays and during Teej/Diwali; start early and keep buffers for traffic.

localTips.title: Carry small cash + exact change
localTips.description: Many small shops and autos ‘don’t have change’; ₹10/₹20/₹50 notes speed up payments and reduce haggling friction.

foodToTry.title: Dal Baati Churma
foodToTry.description: Rajasthani staple—ask for extra ghee on the side if you want it rich, or request light ghee if you don’t.

foodToTry.title: Pyaaz Kachori + Mirchi Vada
foodToTry.description: Best as a hot breakfast snack; pair with mint/tamarind chutney and a cup of chai.

foodToTry.title: Laal Maas (or safer mild option)
foodToTry.description: Spicy mutton curry—confirm spice level; try a milder ‘safed maas’ if you’re heat-sensitive.

foodToTry.title: Ghewar / Mawa Kachori
foodToTry.description: Classic sweets—buy from a reputable sweet shop and get smaller portions; they’re very rich.

gettingAround.title: Use ride-hailing for clean pricing
gettingAround.description: App cabs/autos reduce negotiation and detours; set pickup a short walk from congested gates to avoid cancellations.

gettingAround.title: Auto-rickshaw: lock the fare and route
gettingAround.description: If you hail on the street, agree on an all-inclusive price (including parking/waiting) and share the destination pin to prevent ‘shop stops’.

gettingAround.title: Hire a driver for an Amber–Jaigarh–Nahargarh day
gettingAround.description: A half/full-day car is efficient for hill forts; start with Amber first, then Jaigarh, end at Nahargarh for sunset to avoid backtracking.

topThingsToDo.title: Old Delhi food walk + Jama Masjid at sunset
topThingsToDo.description: Go late afternoon: Jama Masjid views, then eat in lanes around Chandni Chowk (avoid peak noon crowds). Use a pre-decided route so you don’t get pulled into random shops.

topThingsToDo.title: Humayun’s Tomb + Sunder Nursery combo
topThingsToDo.description: Do them together (same area) for Mughal architecture plus a calm park break; weekdays are quieter. Carry water—options inside are limited and pricey.

topThingsToDo.title: Qutub Minar early entry
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive at opening to beat school groups and harsh heat; the complex is most photogenic in soft morning light. Pair with Mehrauli’s stepwell (Rajon ki Baoli) nearby.

topThingsToDo.title: Lodhi Colony street art + Lodhi Garden picnic
topThingsToDo.description: Walk the Lodhi Art District murals, then cross into Lodhi Garden for an easy low-traffic stroll. Go before 9am for the best light and least crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: Dilli Haat (INA) for crafts and regional bites
topThingsToDo.description: Good one-stop for handicrafts at fixed-ish prices and rotating state stalls; shop with a budget and compare a few stalls first. Evening visits have better atmosphere.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Tourist office is closed”/redirect scam
scamsToAvoid.description: Anyone near Connaught Place or stations claiming closures and steering you to a “government office” is likely a commission trap—walk away and use official counters/websites.

scamsToAvoid.title: Inflated taxi/auto fares from airports and stations
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid negotiating on the spot; use app cabs (Uber/Ola) or the official prepaid taxi booth. Confirm the pickup point before paying anything.

scamsToAvoid.title: Free bracelet/tilak or photo-with-sadhu shakedown
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone puts something on you “for blessing” and demands money, remove it, don’t argue, and leave. Keep small cash out of sight.

localTips.title: Time your sights around heat and traffic
localTips.description: Do monuments 8–11am, rest midday, then markets after 5pm; Delhi’s traffic spikes 9–11am and 6–8pm. Mondays many museums are closed—check before you go.

localTips.title: Use UPI/QR but keep backup cash
localTips.description: Most cafes and many shops take UPI; carry small notes for autos, temples, and tiny stalls. Avoid handing over your card for “swipe in the back” situations.

localTips.title: Dress and entry etiquette at religious sites
localTips.description: Carry a scarf for head/shoulder cover at gurdwaras and some mosques; shoes off is mandatory. At Bangla Sahib, accept the karah prasad with both hands.

localTips.title: Air quality and water strategy
localTips.description: In Oct–Jan, consider a mask and plan indoor afternoons if AQI is bad. Drink sealed bottled water and skip raw chutneys/salads from street stalls if you’re sensitive.

foodToTry.title: Chole bhature (breakfast/brunch)
foodToTry.description: Best eaten early while fresh and crisp; share one plate if you’re not used to heavy food. Ask for less spicy if needed—Delhi spice can sneak up.

foodToTry.title: Butter chicken + roomali roti
foodToTry.description: Try it in old-school Punjabi/North Indian restaurants in central or South Delhi for consistent quality. Order one gravy and rotate breads to avoid over-ordering.

foodToTry.title: Paranthe and kachori in Old Delhi
foodToTry.description: Go to Chandni Chowk lanes for stuffed parathas/kachori; pick busy stalls with fast turnover. Eat standing nearby and keep your phone secure in crowds.

foodToTry.title: Chaat (aloo tikki, golgappe, papdi chaat)
foodToTry.description: Choose reputable, high-turnover chaat joints and watch the water used for golgappe. If you’re cautious, stick to aloo tikki/papdi (less water exposure).

gettingAround.title: Delhi Metro is the fastest option
gettingAround.description: Use a QR ticket via DMRC app or a smart card; interchange stations are huge—follow signs by line color and end-station name. Avoid rush hours if you have luggage.

gettingAround.title: App cabs for point-to-point trips
gettingAround.description: Uber/Ola reduce haggling; verify the license plate and driver name before getting in. Expect cancellations in peak traffic—keep a buffer for airport runs.

gettingAround.title: Autos and e-rickshaws for last-mile
gettingAround.description: Agree on the fare before you sit, or insist on meter where it’s actually used (often it isn’t). Short hops around markets are easiest with e-rickshaws.

topThingsToDo.title: Taj Mahal at sunrise (book the first slot)
topThingsToDo.description: Enter via the East Gate to avoid heavy queues and get soft light for photos; bring a physical ID matching your ticket.

topThingsToDo.title: Mehtab Bagh for the “backside” Taj view
topThingsToDo.description: Go late afternoon for calm riverfront views and fewer crowds; it’s a great spot for wide shots without the mausoleum rush.

topThingsToDo.title: Agra Fort (Mughal palaces and Taj view points)
topThingsToDo.description: Start early to beat heat and school groups; don’t skip Musamman Burj for a framed Taj Mahal view.

topThingsToDo.title: Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj) + riverside walk
topThingsToDo.description: Visit mid-morning when marble inlay details pop; pair with a short walk around the quiet neighborhood lanes nearby.

topThingsToDo.title: Fatehpur Sikri half-day trip
topThingsToDo.description: Leave Agra by 7–8am to avoid peak heat; hire a round-trip cab with waiting included and skip “guide-only” routes.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Taj is closed / ticket counter moved” diversion
scamsToAvoid.description: Ignore anyone redirecting you to a different gate or office; go straight to the official entry gates and ticket counters.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “government emporium” and commission shops
scamsToAvoid.description: Drivers/guides may push marble inlay stores with hard selling; only shop where prices are tagged and you can walk out easily.

scamsToAvoid.title: Fake guides and photo add-on hustles
scamsToAvoid.description: Only use licensed guides with ID badges or book via your hotel/official channels; agree on total price and duration before starting.

localTips.title: Choose the right Taj gate
localTips.description: East Gate is usually fastest for entry; West Gate has more crowd management but longer lines in peak season.

localTips.title: Carry minimal items (security is strict)
localTips.description: Bags slow you down and some items are restricted; bring water, ID, phone/camera, and cash, and leave extras at your hotel.

localTips.title: Plan around Fridays and fog season
localTips.description: Taj Mahal is closed Fridays; in Dec–Jan mornings can be foggy, so keep a backup time slot later in the day.

localTips.title: Avoid peak monument crowds with smart timing
localTips.description: Do Agra Fort right at opening, then Baby Taj mid-day, and Taj at sunrise or near sunset to minimize tour-bus congestion.

foodToTry.title: Petha (classic Agra sweet)
foodToTry.description: Try fresh, lightly flavored varieties from a busy, well-known shop; buy small quantities since it’s very sweet.

foodToTry.title: Bedai + aloo sabzi breakfast
foodToTry.description: A local favorite: spicy fried puri-like bread with potato curry; go early morning when it’s freshest.

foodToTry.title: Mughlai kebabs and korma
foodToTry.description: Look for places with high turnover near Sadar/old city areas; ask for medium spice if you’re sensitive.

foodToTry.title: Chaat (aloo tikki, golgappa)
foodToTry.description: Pick stalls with filtered water/packed water use and steady crowds; avoid raw chutneys that sit uncovered.

gettingAround.title: Use app cabs for fixed pricing
gettingAround.description: Ola/Uber are best for point-to-point trips and outstation rides; confirm pickup spot away from monument traffic jams.

gettingAround.title: Auto-rickshaws: negotiate once, then ride
gettingAround.description: Agree on a total fare (not per person) before getting in; keep small notes to avoid “no change” games.

gettingAround.title: Hire a half-day car for Fatehpur Sikri
gettingAround.description: Book through your hotel or a reputable operator with a written all-in price (tolls/parking/waiting); decline surprise stop “shopping breaks.”

topThingsToDo.title: Explore Old Dhaka (Puran Dhaka) on foot
topThingsToDo.description: Go early morning around Shankhari Bazar and the riverside lanes for the best photos and fewer crowds; keep cash small and pockets zipped in the crush.

topThingsToDo.title: Lalbagh Fort + Ahsan Manzil combo
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Lalbagh Fort right at opening, then take a short rickshaw ride to Ahsan Manzil; weekday mornings are quieter and cooler.

topThingsToDo.title: Sadarghat riverfront and a short Buriganga boat ride
topThingsToDo.description: Use a small rowboat for a 20–30 minute loop (agree price before boarding) and keep your phone secured—piers are hectic and slippery.

topThingsToDo.title: Shahbag–Dhaka University–Ramna Park circuit
topThingsToDo.description: Stroll the campus area and end at Ramna Park in late afternoon; pair it with a quick stop at the National Museum if it’s too hot outside.

topThingsToDo.title: New Market + Nilkhet book bazaar
topThingsToDo.description: Shop for local clothes and browse secondhand books; bargain gently and check items for defects before paying.

scamsToAvoid.title: Rickshaw/CNG ‘meter’ tricks
scamsToAvoid.description: Most won’t use meters—set the fare and route clearly before you sit down, and pay after you get off.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced ‘guide’ at Sadarghat/Old Dhaka attractions
scamsToAvoid.description: Friendly helpers may steer you to their boat/shop for commission; decline politely and choose your own boat or ticket counter.

scamsToAvoid.title: Counterfeit or short-changed cash in markets
scamsToAvoid.description: Count change immediately and avoid large notes in busy bazaars; use ATMs inside banks or malls when possible.

localTips.title: Time your day around traffic
localTips.description: Plan one neighborhood per half-day; avoid cross-city hops at 5–9pm when a short ride can take an hour.

localTips.title: Dress and behavior for smoother interactions
localTips.description: Modest clothing reduces unwanted attention; ask before photographing people, especially in Old Dhaka lanes and markets.

localTips.title: Heat, water, and rest strategy
localTips.description: Carry oral rehydration salts and buy sealed water; take AC breaks in malls (Bashundhara City/Jamuna Future Park) midday.

localTips.title: Friday/holiday closures
localTips.description: Many offices and some museums have limited hours on Friday; double-check opening times and keep a backup plan like parks or malls.

foodToTry.title: Kacchi biryani (Old Dhaka style)
foodToTry.description: Go for lunchtime at well-known biryani spots in Old Dhaka; ask for “half” if you want a manageable portion.

foodToTry.title: Fuchka and chotpoti street snacks
foodToTry.description: Choose stalls with high turnover and freshly filled shells; request less chili if you’re not used to spice.

foodToTry.title: Beef tehari
foodToTry.description: A Dhaka classic—best in the early evening at busy local eateries; pair with borhani if available.

foodToTry.title: Mishti (Bengali sweets) like roshogolla and chomchom
foodToTry.description: Buy from reputable sweet shops and ask for the day’s freshest batch; get smaller mixed boxes to sample variety.

gettingAround.title: Ride-hailing is your default
gettingAround.description: Use apps like Uber/Pathao for cars or motorbikes; always verify the plate and driver name before getting in.

gettingAround.title: Rickshaws for short hops in Old Dhaka
gettingAround.description: They’re fastest in narrow lanes—agree fare upfront and keep your route simple to avoid detours.

gettingAround.title: Intercity bus/train for day trips
gettingAround.description: If going outside Dhaka (e.g., Sonargaon), start early and book seats from major terminals; keep extra time for unpredictable traffic.

topThingsToDo.title: Swim with sea turtles (Carlisle Bay)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early (8–10am) for calmer water and fewer boats; book a small-group snorkel from Bridgetown or Brown’s Beach and ask to avoid “baiting” stops.

topThingsToDo.title: Friday night Oistins Fish Fry
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive before 7pm to beat the lines, pick your fish at the grill (mahi-mahi, marlin, flying fish), and pay at the counter before you sit.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike/drive the east coast (Bathsheba & Soup Bowl)
topThingsToDo.description: The Atlantic side is for views, not swimming—walk the boardwalk/rocks at low tide and stop for coconut water and salt bread from roadside vendors.

topThingsToDo.title: Harrison’s Cave (tram tour)
topThingsToDo.description: Book the first tour slot to avoid big coach crowds and bring a light jacket—the cave feels cool and damp even on hot days.

topThingsToDo.title: Rum + heritage day (Mount Gay or St. Nicholas Abbey)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose one distillery tour and pair it with a nearby stop (Holetown/Paynes Bay west coast) to keep travel time down; reserve tastings in peak season.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered taxi “island tour” price creep
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree on a total price and route before you get in (including stops and waiting time); ask your hotel for the going rate by area.

scamsToAvoid.title: Beach chair/umbrella surprise fees
scamsToAvoid.description: On busy beaches, confirm the full-day price and whether it includes the umbrella before they set you up; pay only once and keep the receipt.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced turtle/snorkel trips on the sand
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid cash-only touts with no boat name or pickup details; book with an operator that provides exact departure point, duration, and what’s included.

localTips.title: Pick beaches by coast
localTips.description: West/south coasts are calmer for swimming; east coast is rough—enjoy viewpoints and stay out unless you’re experienced and locals are in the water.

localTips.title: Plan around Sunday closures
localTips.description: Many shops close or shorten hours—stock snacks, sunscreen, and water on Saturday; beaches and nature spots are still great.

localTips.title: Timing beats traffic and crowds
localTips.description: Do attractions before 10am, then beach/siesta; sunset is best on the west coast (Paynes Bay, Holetown) with fewer day-trippers.

localTips.title: Bring small cash for local eats
localTips.description: Fish fry stalls, rum shops, and minibuses often prefer cash; carry small notes to avoid “no change” situations.

foodToTry.title: Flying fish & cou-cou
foodToTry.description: Try it at a fish fry or local lunch spot; ask for pepper sauce on the side—it’s hotter than it looks.

foodToTry.title: Macaroni pie
foodToTry.description: A Bajan staple served with fish or chicken; best from neighborhood bakeries and lunch counters rather than resort buffets.

foodToTry.title: Pudding and souse
foodToTry.description: Typically a Saturday specialty—look for places that sell out by early afternoon and order a small first if you’re new to pickled flavors.

foodToTry.title: Cutters (salt bread sandwiches)
foodToTry.description: Grab a ham, cheese, or flying-fish cutter for an easy beach meal; bakeries sell freshest in the morning.

gettingAround.title: Public buses (blue government buses)
gettingAround.description: Cheap and reliable on main routes; have exact fare in cash and expect limited service late evening.

gettingAround.title: Minibuses & ZR vans (white/yellow)
gettingAround.description: Fast and frequent but can be crowded—tell the conductor your stop, keep small change, and hold on tight for quick accelerations.

gettingAround.title: Taxis and self-drive
gettingAround.description: Taxis are fixed-rate by zone (confirm before departure); if renting a car, drive left, take roundabouts slowly, and watch for narrow shoulders at night.

topThingsToDo.title: Blue Mountains sunrise + coffee farm
topThingsToDo.description: Go with a licensed guide from Kingston for a pre-dawn hike; pair it with a small coffee estate visit near Mavis Bank to taste fresh-roasted beans.

topThingsToDo.title: Portland: Blue Lagoon + Frenchman’s Cove day
topThingsToDo.description: Arrive early to beat tour buses; hire a local raft at Blue Lagoon and bring cash for Frenchman’s Cove entry and food stalls.

topThingsToDo.title: Negril cliffs at sunset (West End)
topThingsToDo.description: Skip Seven Mile crowds and base yourself on the cliffs; watch sunset from the bars near Rick’s without paying for a ‘VIP’ seat.

topThingsToDo.title: South Coast: Black River safari + Pelican Bar
topThingsToDo.description: Book the first boat of the day for better wildlife viewing, then do a local fisherman’s boat to Pelican Bar (weather dependent).

topThingsToDo.title: Kingston culture loop
topThingsToDo.description: Do the Bob Marley Museum plus Trench Town Culture Yard with a local guide; finish at Dub Club (Sunday nights) if you’re comfortable with the vibe.

scamsToAvoid.title: “Official” taxi upsells at airports/cruise ports
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm the total price before loading bags and choose a driver from the official dispatch desk; avoid anyone who approaches you in the exit lane.

scamsToAvoid.title: Free tour/bracelet/weed “gift” that becomes a bill
scamsToAvoid.description: Decline anything placed in your hand and don’t follow hustlers down side streets; if you accept a service, agree the price first.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced beach chairs, parking, or entry fees
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask to see the posted rate (or ticket booth) and pay at the counter when possible; keep small bills so you don’t get stuck with “no change.”

localTips.title: Use cash smartly
localTips.description: Carry small JMD notes for tips, tolls, and roadside food; many small vendors won’t take cards and USD often gets a bad exchange rate.

localTips.title: Know when to go out
localTips.description: Plan long drives in daylight—roads can be narrow with potholes and few lights; start early and keep evenings for nearby spots.

localTips.title: Beach access hack
localTips.description: Many of the best swims are at public beaches like Winnifred (Portland) or Fort Clarence (near Kingston); bring your own towel and reef-safe sunscreen.

localTips.title: Respect the sound system + Sunday rhythm
localTips.description: Earplugs help near nightlife zones, and Sundays can be slower outside tourist strips—stock snacks and confirm tour departures in advance.

foodToTry.title: Jerk chicken/pork (roadside jerk pan)
foodToTry.description: Go where you see smoke and locals lined up; ask for “festival” or bammy on the side and choose your heat level of pepper sauce.

foodToTry.title: Ackee and saltfish breakfast
foodToTry.description: Best early at cookshops; pair with fried dumpling or roasted breadfruit and a cup of strong tea or coffee.

foodToTry.title: Pepper shrimp (Hellshire Beach or street vendors)
foodToTry.description: Eat it hot and fresh—spicy and briny; bring napkins and cash, and follow it with coconut water if the pepper hits hard.

foodToTry.title: Ital or steamed fish with bammy
foodToTry.description: Try Ital plates in Kingston or Negril for a flavorful veggie meal, or order escovitch/steamed fish with bammy on the coast.

gettingAround.title: Route taxis and minibuses
gettingAround.description: Cheap and frequent in towns; agree the fare up front, keep valuables out of sight, and avoid late-night rides if you don’t know the route.

gettingAround.title: Private driver for cross-island days
gettingAround.description: For Ocho Rios–Negril–Portland hops, a vetted driver is safer and often faster than piecing together taxis; confirm stops and total cost before departure.

gettingAround.title: Driving yourself
gettingAround.description: Rent only if you’re confident with left-side driving and mountain roads; download offline maps, avoid night driving, and watch for unmarked speed bumps.

topThingsToDo.title: Old San Juan + the forts (Castillo San Felipe del Morro & San Cristóbal)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for shade, then walk the fort-to-fort route along the city walls; bring water and expect strong wind at El Morro. Sunset views from the lawns are great, but the streets get quiet after dinner.

topThingsToDo.title: La Placita de Santurce (day vs night)
topThingsToDo.description: Visit late afternoon for food stalls and bars without the crush; Thu–Sat nights turn into a street party. Keep your phone secure and use rideshare to avoid parking headaches.

topThingsToDo.title: Beach hop: Escambrón to Condado Lagoon
topThingsToDo.description: Swim at Playa Escambrón for calmer water and clearer snorkeling near the rocks; skip rough-surf days. Paddleboard/kayak at Condado Lagoon near sunset for manatee/turtle chances (no chasing).

topThingsToDo.title: Piñones for kiosks + mangrove boardwalk
topThingsToDo.description: Head out earlier in the day for fresher fritters and shorter lines, then walk the coastal boardwalk for a breezy break from the city. Go by rideshare and avoid leaving valuables in cars.

topThingsToDo.title: Coffee + art crawl in Santurce
topThingsToDo.description: Do a daytime loop around Calle Loíza and the Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico area for murals, galleries, and specialty coffee. Sundays can be slower; check hours before you go.

scamsToAvoid.title: Inflated taxi fares from the airport/cruise area
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm the fare and if it’s metered before getting in, or use an app-based ride to lock pricing. Avoid drivers who pressure you with “fixed” prices without clarity.

scamsToAvoid.title: Street drink overcharging in nightlife zones
scamsToAvoid.description: At busy spots (especially La Placita/Condado), ask for the total price before ordering rounds and watch the register. Pay per drink if a tab feels vague.

scamsToAvoid.title: Timeshare/“free tour” pitches near tourist hubs
scamsToAvoid.description: If someone offers freebies for “a quick presentation,” it’s usually a long sales session. Politely decline and keep walking.

localTips.title: Old San Juan is steep—plan your walk downhill
localTips.description: Start near Castillo San Cristóbal and finish toward the waterfront/El Morro to save your knees. Wear grippy shoes; the blue cobblestones get slick when wet.

localTips.title: Rain is quick but intense—pack a compact poncho
localTips.description: Short tropical showers can soak you in minutes, then clear up fast. A poncho beats an umbrella in the windier fort areas.

localTips.title: Book bioluminescent bay tours outside the city wisely
localTips.description: For the brightest glow, aim for a new-moon window and avoid tours after heavy rain. Confirm if transportation is included if you’re not renting a car.

localTips.title: Reserve dinners in popular neighborhoods
localTips.description: Weekend tables in Old San Juan, Miramar, and Santurce can fill up quickly; reserve or eat earlier. Many kitchens close earlier than bars.

foodToTry.title: Mofongo
foodToTry.description: Order it with garlic and pork cracklings, or seafood sauce if you want it richer. It’s filling—split one if you’re also snacking at kiosks.

foodToTry.title: Alcapurrias (kiosk-style fritters)
foodToTry.description: Best hot and fresh; ask what just came out and eat immediately. Try meat or crab versions when available.

foodToTry.title: Lechón + arroz con gandules
foodToTry.description: Look for crispy skin (“cuerito”) and moist meat; go earlier to avoid dried-out late batches. Pair with a simple salad to cut the richness.

foodToTry.title: Piña colada (where it’s iconic)
foodToTry.description: Order one in Old San Juan where it’s famously claimed, but compare styles—some are heavier and sweeter. Ask for it less sweet if you prefer more rum and pineapple.

gettingAround.title: Walking + rideshare combo
gettingAround.description: Old San Juan is best on foot; use rideshare between neighborhoods (Santurce, Condado, Isla Verde) to save time. Expect occasional surge pricing on weekend nights.

gettingAround.title: Public transit for specific corridors
gettingAround.description: The Tren Urbano is useful if you’re heading toward Bayamón/Sagrado Corazón, but it won’t cover most beach/Old San Juan routes. Buses can be slow and irregular—use them only if you have flexibility.

gettingAround.title: Car rentals: only if you’re leaving metro San Juan
gettingAround.description: Parking and traffic are frustrating in the city, but a car is worth it for day trips (El Yunque, west coast). Choose a place with included toll device options to avoid toll hassles.

topThingsToDo.title: Snorkel or beach day at Clifton Heritage National Park
topThingsToDo.description: Go early for the clearest water and fewer crowds; snorkel the underwater sculptures and reef sections (bring your own mask if you have one).

topThingsToDo.title: Explore the Queen’s Staircase + Fort Fincastle combo
topThingsToDo.description: Start in the morning before the midday heat; it’s an easy walk between the Staircase, Fort Fincastle, and nearby viewpoints.

topThingsToDo.title: Day trip to Blue Lagoon Island (choose your vibe)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a half-day for beach time or a full-day if you want activities; compare ferry times because last boats back can fill up.

topThingsToDo.title: Hit Arawak Cay (Fish Fry) for dinner
topThingsToDo.description: Go around sunset for the best atmosphere; walk a few doors before ordering—quality and prices vary stall to stall.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunset stroll + drinks at Paradise Island Marina Village
topThingsToDo.description: It’s a low-stress evening spot with breezes and people-watching; pair with a short walk along the Atlantis marina promenade.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial taxis with “special” rates
scamsToAvoid.description: Agree on a price before you get in (cash amount); if they won’t quote clearly, take a licensed taxi from an official stand.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “VIP” beach access or chair rentals
scamsToAvoid.description: Some sellers imply public beaches require payment; ask what’s included and walk away if they won’t itemize.

scamsToAvoid.title: Photo/bracelet/“free sample” pressure near cruise areas
scamsToAvoid.description: A quick interaction can turn into a demand for payment; keep walking and decline firmly without engaging.

localTips.title: Plan around cruise ship waves
localTips.description: Downtown and the Straw Market get slammed mid-morning; do museums and forts early, then beaches while the port is busiest.

localTips.title: Bring small bills (USD works, BSD is pegged 1:1)
localTips.description: Many spots prefer cash and may not have change; expect to receive Bahamian dollars back even if you pay in USD.

localTips.title: Beach hack: Cabbage Beach access points
localTips.description: Access can be confusing from the road—head toward public access paths and avoid anyone claiming the beach is “private.”

localTips.title: Weather timing for calm water
localTips.description: Mornings are usually calmer for snorkeling and boat trips; if it’s windy, switch to sheltered beaches or inland sights.

foodToTry.title: Cracked conch
foodToTry.description: Tenderized, battered, and fried—best eaten immediately; ask for it “fresh cracked” so it’s not overcooked.

foodToTry.title: Conch salad
foodToTry.description: Order it made-to-order (not pre-mixed) for the brightest flavor; it should be cold, citrusy, and crunchy.

foodToTry.title: Guava duff
foodToTry.description: A classic dessert—try it warm with rum sauce; great after a spicy seafood meal.

foodToTry.title: Bahamian stew fish + johnnycake
foodToTry.description: A hearty local breakfast/lunch; dip the johnnycake in the sauce and add pepper sauce if you like heat.

gettingAround.title: Taxis: negotiate and confirm destination details
gettingAround.description: Most rides are fixed-price by zone but not always posted—confirm the fare, number of passengers, and whether it includes luggage before leaving.

gettingAround.title: Jitneys (local buses) for cheap daytime hops
gettingAround.description: They’re cash-only and best for simple routes (like to Cable Beach); service thins out in the evening, so plan a taxi back.

gettingAround.title: Ferries and day-trip boats: book with buffer time
gettingAround.description: Check return times carefully and arrive early—boats can depart promptly and lines spike when cruise passengers arrive.

topThingsToDo.title: Sunrise walk in Positano + beach dip
topThingsToDo.description: Go down to Spiaggia Grande before 9:00 to avoid crowds and get the best photos; swim early, then grab a quick cornetto and espresso uphill.

topThingsToDo.title: Path of the Gods (Sentiero degli Dei)
topThingsToDo.description: Start from Bomerano (easier, mostly downhill) and finish in Nocelle/Positano; bring 1.5L water and cash for the lemon granita stands.

topThingsToDo.title: Ferry-hop Amalfi–Positano–Salerno
topThingsToDo.description: Use ferries for the fastest, least nauseating travel and the best views; aim for mid-morning departures and sit on the left side heading to Positano.

topThingsToDo.title: Ravello gardens with late-afternoon light
topThingsToDo.description: Visit Villa Cimbrone and Villa Rufolo after 16:00 for softer light and fewer tour groups; the terraces are windy—bring a light layer.

topThingsToDo.title: Boat to hidden coves (or private swim stop)
topThingsToDo.description: Book a small-group boat from Amalfi/Positano with a confirmed swim stop at quieter spots like Santa Croce or around Conca dei Marini; verify fuel/port fees are included.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unmetered “flat-rate” taxis and inflated transfers
scamsToAvoid.description: Confirm the total price before getting in (including luggage/night fees) and consider pre-booked NCC transfers with written quotes.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced boat tours with surprise add-ons
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask in advance about port taxes, fuel surcharges, snorkeling gear, and towels; pay by card when possible and keep the booking message.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tourist-menu traps with coperto/service surprises
scamsToAvoid.description: Check the menu prices and the coperto/service line before ordering; avoid places with aggressive greeters on the main piazzas.

localTips.title: Pick your base strategically
localTips.description: For fewer crowds and easier logistics, base in Salerno (best transport hub) or Maiori/Minori (more beach space) and day-trip to Positano/Amalfi.

localTips.title: Time towns, not just days
localTips.description: Do Positano early morning or after 18:00; do Amalfi mid-day only if you’re using ferries—buses and roads are slow and packed late morning.

localTips.title: Pack for stairs and slick stone
localTips.description: Expect hundreds of steps daily; wear grippy shoes (not smooth soles) and avoid dragging wheeled bags through steep lanes—use porter services if needed.

localTips.title: Reserve ahead for the best viewpoints
localTips.description: Book popular terraces (especially in Positano and Ravello) for sunset times; request an outdoor table and confirm the view in the notes.

foodToTry.title: Scialatielli ai frutti di mare
foodToTry.description: Handmade pasta typical of the coast—order it near the sea and ask for mixed local shellfish (vongole/cozze) when available.

foodToTry.title: Delizia al limone
foodToTry.description: A lemon-scented sponge dome with cream; try it in Amalfi or Minori where pastry shops do it best and it’s freshest mid-morning.

foodToTry.title: Alici di Cetara
foodToTry.description: Anchovies from Cetara (marinated or fried) and the famous colatura di alici; buy a small bottle from a reputable shop for pasta at home.

foodToTry.title: Lemon granita on the trail
foodToTry.description: Perfect on the Path of the Gods or Ravello walks; carry coins and ask for “con panna” if you want whipped cream.

gettingAround.title: Ferries (best option in season)
gettingAround.description: Run mainly spring–early fall and can stop in rough seas; buy tickets early on busy days and arrive 20–30 minutes before departure.

gettingAround.title: SITA buses (cheap but crowded)
gettingAround.description: Board at the first stop when possible to guarantee space (e.g., Amalfi terminal); validate tickets and expect delays on summer afternoons.

gettingAround.title: Scooter/driver vs. rental car
gettingAround.description: Cars are a parking nightmare and roads are tight; if you must drive, reserve parking in advance—otherwise hire an NCC driver for key transfers.

topThingsToDo.title: Drive the North Coast 500 (pick the best bits)
topThingsToDo.description: Do the west and north sections (Applecross Pass, Assynt, Durness) early mornings to beat campervans; book key stops (dinners, ferries) weeks ahead in summer.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike a classic ridge or glen (with a plan B)
topThingsToDo.description: Try Buachaille Etive Mòr (Glencoe) or the Old Man of Storr (Skye); carry a low-level alternative for sudden wind/cloud and start before 9am for parking.

topThingsToDo.title: Wild beaches and dunes
topThingsToDo.description: Go to Sandwood Bay (near Blairmore) or Achmelvich (Assynt); bring food and layers—facilities are limited and weather flips fast.

topThingsToDo.title: Castle + distillery combo day
topThingsToDo.description: Pair Eilean Donan with a nearby distillery (e.g., Talisker on Skye or Ben Nevis near Fort William); pre-book tours as walk-ins often sell out.

topThingsToDo.title: Loch Ness without the crowds
topThingsToDo.description: Skip the busiest viewpoints and take the quieter side roads near Foyers/Dores; do a short boat trip from Fort Augustus at off-peak times for better value.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unlicensed “tours” and cash-only drivers
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid drivers offering last-minute tours in car parks; use licensed operators with clear itineraries, insurance, and card payment.

scamsToAvoid.title: Overpriced “authentic” tartan and souvenirs
scamsToAvoid.description: Tourist shops may sell low-quality imports at premium prices; look for provenance labels (Made in Scotland) and buy from reputable mills or local makers.

scamsToAvoid.title: Misleading parking/fines and private clamps
scamsToAvoid.description: Don’t pay random “attendants”; use official meters/apps and keep proof—some small private lots use confusing signs and aggressive tickets.

localTips.title: Single-track road etiquette
localTips.description: Use passing places on the left, let faster traffic through, and don’t stop in passing places for photos—pull fully off the road.

localTips.title: Midges: timing beats repellent
localTips.description: They’re worst at dawn/dusk and in still, damp weather; plan hikes for breezier times and pack a head net for calm evenings.

localTips.title: Fuel, food, and toilets can be far apart
localTips.description: Top up when you hit half a tank in remote areas and carry snacks/water; some villages have limited hours and no public toilets.

localTips.title: Respect the Outdoor Access Code
localTips.description: Leave gates as found, keep dogs under control near livestock, and camp well away from houses/roads—use a trowel and pack out litter.

foodToTry.title: Cullen skink
foodToTry.description: Smoky haddock chowder—best in coastal towns; ask if it’s made with local smoked fish.

foodToTry.title: Venison (stew, burger, or loin)
foodToTry.description: Look for locally sourced Highland venison in pubs; it’s lean, so it’s best served medium or in slow-cooked dishes.

foodToTry.title: Fresh langoustines and scallops
foodToTry.description: Order simply grilled when you’re on the west coast; check day boats/landing notices for the freshest catches.

foodToTry.title: Cranachan
foodToTry.description: Oats, whisky, cream, and berries—often seasonal; ask for raspberries when in season for the best version.

gettingAround.title: Car (most flexible, but book early)
gettingAround.description: Reserve automatics months ahead in summer; download offline maps, and expect slow average speeds on single-track roads.

gettingAround.title: Trains + buses (scenic, limited frequency)
gettingAround.description: Use rail to Inverness/Fort William then local buses; check timetables carefully—many routes run only a few times daily.

gettingAround.title: Ferries to islands and peninsulas
gettingAround.description: Book vehicle spots early (especially Skye-linked routes and small crossings); arrive 30–45 minutes before departure and keep a backup sailing in mind.

topThingsToDo.title: Hike Torres del Paine (W or day hikes)
topThingsToDo.description: Book refugios/campsites months ahead in peak season; start sunrise hikes (Base Torres/Mirador Británico) to beat wind and crowds.

topThingsToDo.title: See Perito Moreno Glacier (El Calafate)
topThingsToDo.description: Go early or near closing for quieter boardwalks; add a kayak or mini-trek if you want time on the ice (bring layers and gloves).

topThingsToDo.title: Drive Ruta 40 & detour to El Chaltén
topThingsToDo.description: Plan fuel stops (stations can be far apart) and carry snacks; in El Chaltén, do Laguna de los Tres at first light for the best Fitz Roy views.

topThingsToDo.title: Boat to Magdalena Island penguins (Punta Arenas)
topThingsToDo.description: Choose a morning departure for calmer seas; pack a windproof outer layer even on sunny days.

topThingsToDo.title: Explore Tierra del Fuego (Ushuaia)
topThingsToDo.description: Do the national park by bus + short hikes, then take the Beagle Channel cruise; pick smaller boats for closer wildlife viewing.

scamsToAvoid.title: Unofficial park shuttles/taxis with inflated fares
scamsToAvoid.description: Use your accommodation to call a licensed taxi/remis and confirm price before getting in, especially around bus terminals.

scamsToAvoid.title: Tour upsells that hide mandatory extras
scamsToAvoid.description: Ask for the total cost including park entry, port fees, gear rental, and transfers; get it in writing/WhatsApp before paying.

scamsToAvoid.title: Bad exchange rates or “cash-only” pressure
scamsToAvoid.description: Avoid street exchangers; use bank ATMs or reputable casas de cambio and check the rate and fees before confirming.

localTips.title: Wind is the real challenge
localTips.description: Bring a windproof shell and secure hats/phones; start exposed hikes early and keep a buffer day for weather delays.

localTips.title: Reservations can be the trip’s bottleneck
localTips.description: In peak months, book TdP camps/refugios, buses, and key tours (penguins/ice treks) well ahead; walk-ins often sell out.
